Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan

# Baidu Qianfan Token Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Baidu Qianfan (百度千帆) has two Token Plans, personal and enterprise, and pay as you go, each with endpoints and keys of its own. Add Baidu Qianfan in jianmu with each key's plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other tools use Qianfan's DeepSeek and GLM through jianmu's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add Baidu Qianfan

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Baidu Qianfan, set the key's plan to Token Plan Personal, Token Plan Enterprise, Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as qianfan-code-latest or deepseek-v4-pro on a tool's row.

```
jianmu claude baidu-qianfan/qianfan-code-latest
jianmu codex baidu-qianfan/deepseek-v4-pro
jianmu opencode baidu-qianfan/glm-5.3
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Plan | Chat Completions and Responses | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Plan personal | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2/tokenplan/personal` | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic/tokenplan/personal` |
| Token Plan enterprise | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2/tokenplan/team` | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic/tokenplan/team` |
| Pay as you go | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2` | `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic` |

Each plan's key works at its own endpoints. Each key in the provider names its plan, so personal, enterprise and pay-as-you-go keys can share one provider, and each key's requests go to its own plan's endpoint.

## The plans' models

The plans' `/models` answers 404, so jianmu gives the models from both plans' docs: qianfan-code-latest, deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-pro-0813, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, glm-5.2, glm-5.1, among others. deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v3.2 and glm-5 are the enterprise plan's alone. qianfan-code-latest is whichever model the console has picked. A pay-as-you-go key reads Qianfan's `/v2/models`.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Qianfan's plans and pay as you go have Anthropic endpoints, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. Qianfan's plan endpoints serve Responses too, so Codex's requests go as they are. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; jianmu points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : jianmu writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use the Baidu Qianfan Token Plan in Claude Code?

Add Baidu Qianfan in jianmu with the key's plan set to Token Plan Personal or Enterprise, then pick qianfan-code-latest on Claude Code's row, or run jianmu claude baidu-qianfan/qianfan-code-latest. Requests go to the plan's Anthropic endpoint, such as https://qianfan.baidubce.com/anthropic/tokenplan/personal.

### Which model is qianfan-code-latest?

The one you picked for the plan in Qianfan's console. Change it there; the name in jianmu and your tools stays the same.

### Do the personal and enterprise plans have the same models?

Mostly. deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v3.2 and glm-5 are the enterprise plan's alone; deepseek-v4-pro, glm-5.3 and the others are in both.

### Does Baidu Qianfan work in Codex?

Yes. Qianfan's plan endpoints serve OpenAI Responses, so jianmu passes Codex's requests through. Run jianmu codex baidu-qianfan/deepseek-v4-pro, or pick it on Codex's row.

The same for other providers: [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine), [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow

# SiliconFlow in Claude Code and Codex

SiliconFlow (硅基流动) serves open models such as DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Qwen on one API key, over OpenAI's Chat Completions. Claude Code wants Anthropic Messages and Codex wants Responses, and SiliconFlow serves neither; jianmu's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425 converts between them, so these tools use SiliconFlow's models directly.

## Add SiliconFlow

1. **Add the provider.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick SiliconFlow, set the key to China or Global, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro on a tool's row.

```
jianmu claude siliconflow/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
jianmu codex siliconflow/zai-org/GLM-5.3
jianmu opencode siliconflow/moonshotai/Kimi-K3
```

## China and Global

| Site | Chat Completions | Console |
| --- | --- | --- |
| China | `https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1` | cloud.siliconflow.cn |
| Global | `https://api.siliconflow.com/v1` | cloud.siliconflow.com |

The Global site is another account, with keys and a balance (in $) of its own; a China key doesn't work there. Each key in the provider names its site, so keys from both can share one provider.

## Models

SiliconFlow's model names carry their maker, and go into jianmu and your tools as written: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, zai-org/GLM-5.3, moonshotai/Kimi-K3, moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code, Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0. jianmu takes their names, context and prices from models.dev's siliconflow catalog. On the command line, write `siliconflow/` then the name.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which this provider doesn't serve. jianmu converts each request to Chat Completions and the reply back, reasoning included. [Claude Code with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses. It has no Responses, so jianmu converts to Chat Completions; Codex's custom tools such as `apply_patch` go to the model as functions, and its calls come back as Codex can run them. [Codex with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; jianmu converts it to Chat Completions. [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so requests go as they are. [OpenCode with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Balance

SiliconFlow retired its balance query, `/v1/user/info`, on 2026-08-14 (it answers 410) with nothing in its place yet, and its old granted balance is a voucher now. So jianmu's usage card says where the balance is shown instead of an amount, and its button opens that site's console. A key refused for itself (401) is said as it came.

## FAQ

### How do I use SiliconFlow in Claude Code?

Add SiliconFlow in jianmu with your key, then pick a model such as deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro on Claude Code's row, or run jianmu claude siliconflow/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro. SiliconFlow has no Anthropic endpoint, so jianmu converts Claude Code's requests to Chat Completions.

### Does SiliconFlow work in Codex?

Yes. SiliconFlow has Chat Completions only, so jianmu converts Codex's Responses requests, custom tools like apply_patch included. Run jianmu codex siliconflow/zai-org/GLM-5.3.

### Does a China key work on the Global site?

No. cloud.siliconflow.com is another account, with its own keys and balance. Set each key's site to China or Global in jianmu.

### Why doesn't jianmu show my SiliconFlow balance?

SiliconFlow retired its balance API on 2026-08-14 and has no new one yet. jianmu's card takes you to the console, where the balance and vouchers are shown.

The same for other providers: [ModelScope](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope), [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope

# ModelScope in Claude Code and Codex

ModelScope's (魔搭) API-Inference takes a ModelScope account's access token as its key and serves models such as Qwen and GLM over Chat Completions and Responses. Add ModelScope in jianmu, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode use them through jianmu's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add ModelScope

1. **Add the provider.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick ModelScope, use your ModelScope access token as the key, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on a tool's row.

```
jianmu claude modelscope/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
jianmu codex modelscope/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.6
jianmu opencode modelscope/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507
```

## Endpoint and token

| API | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api-inference.modelscope.cn/v1` |
| Responses | `https://api-inference.modelscope.cn/v1` |

The key is a ModelScope account's access token, made at modelscope.cn/my/myaccesstoken. ModelScope is not Alibaba Cloud's DashScope: a DashScope key goes in the [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) provider, and neither works on the other. A provider added by hand at api-inference.modelscope.cn is taken as ModelScope too.

## Models

ModelScope's model names carry their organisation, written as they are: Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507, Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507, ZhipuAI/GLM-4.6, ZhipuAI/GLM-4.5, among others. jianmu takes their names and context from models.dev's modelscope catalog. On the command line, write `modelscope/` then the name.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which this provider doesn't serve. jianmu converts each request to Chat Completions and the reply back, reasoning included. [Claude Code with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses. It serves Responses too, so Codex's requests go as they are. [Codex with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; jianmu converts it to Chat Completions. [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so requests go as they are. [OpenCode with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Images

ModelScope draws through async tasks of its own: a request starts a task and answers its task_id, which is asked about until it succeeds or fails. It runs one task of a user's at a time and answers bursts with 429, so jianmu asks for one image at a time, waits a moment when it is busy, and hands the result to your tool as an image it can read.

## FAQ

### How do I use ModelScope in Claude Code?

Add ModelScope in jianmu with your access token as the key, then pick Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on Claude Code's row, or run jianmu claude modelscope/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct. ModelScope has no Anthropic endpoint, so jianmu converts to Chat Completions.

### Where do I get a ModelScope key?

ModelScope uses your account's access token, made at modelscope.cn/my/myaccesstoken. Paste it into jianmu's ModelScope provider.

### Is ModelScope the same as Alibaba's DashScope?

No. ModelScope's API-Inference is at api-inference.modelscope.cn on a ModelScope access token; DashScope takes an Alibaba Cloud key and is jianmu's Qwen provider.

### Does ModelScope work in Codex?

Yes. ModelScope serves Responses, so jianmu passes Codex's requests through. Run jianmu codex modelscope/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.6.

The same for other providers: [SiliconFlow](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow), [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud

# Huawei Cloud MaaS Token Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Huawei Cloud ModelArts MaaS's Token Plan is for personal accounts in 西南-贵阳一 (Guiyang) and serves GLM, Kimi and DeepSeek over Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages. Add Huawei Cloud in jianmu with the plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode use them through jianmu's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add Huawei Cloud

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Huawei Cloud MaaS, set the key's plan to Token Plan or Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as glm-5.3 on a tool's row.

```
jianmu claude huaweicloud/glm-5.3
jianmu codex huaweicloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash
jianmu opencode huaweicloud/kimi-k2.6
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Plan | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Plan | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/plan/v2` | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/plan/anthropic` |
| Pay as you go | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/openai/v1` | `https://api.modelarts-maas.com/anthropic` |

The Token Plan's quota is spent only at the endpoints under `/plan`, so jianmu uses the plan's by default; pay as you go bills apart. Both take a MaaS API key, made under the ModelArts console's authentication management. Each key in the provider names its plan. Neither serves Responses.

## Models

Until its list is fetched, jianmu gives the plan's models: glm-5.3, glm-5.1, kimi-k2.6, deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, lowercase as Huawei's OpenClaw page writes them. Once the list is in, Huawei's own list is the one served.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which the plan serves, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses, which Huawei Cloud doesn't serve, so jianmu converts to Chat Completions; custom tools such as `apply_patch` go to the model as functions and come back as Codex can run them. See [Codex with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; jianmu translates at the local gateway. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : jianmu writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use the Huawei Cloud Token Plan in Claude Code?

Add Huawei Cloud MaaS in jianmu with the key's plan set to Token Plan, then pick glm-5.3 on Claude Code's row, or run jianmu claude huaweicloud/glm-5.3. Requests go to the plan's Anthropic endpoint, https://api.modelarts-maas.com/plan/anthropic.

### Does Huawei Cloud MaaS work in Codex?

Yes. Huawei Cloud has no Responses endpoint, so jianmu converts Codex's requests to Chat Completions, custom tools included. Run jianmu codex huaweicloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash.

### Why the endpoints under /plan?

The Token Plan's quota is spent only at /plan/v2 and /plan/anthropic; requests to pay as you go's /openai/v1 bill apart. jianmu uses the plan's endpoints by default.

### Which models does the Huawei Cloud Token Plan have?

jianmu gives glm-5.3, glm-5.1, kimi-k2.6, deepseek-v4.1-flash and deepseek-v4-flash until Huawei's list is fetched, and then serves that list.

The same for other providers: [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud), [Baidu Qianfan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan), [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo

# Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan in Claude Code and Codex

Xiaomi's MiMo platform has a Token Plan and pay as you go. A Token Plan's tp- key works only at its region's own host (China, Singapore or Europe); pay as you go is api.xiaomimimo.com. Each serves Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages, so Claude Code's, Codex's and OpenCode's requests go as they are, with jianmu's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425 routing them and holding the key.

## Add Xiaomi MiMo

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick Xiaomi MiMo, set the key's plan to Plan · China, Plan · Singapore, Plan · Europe, Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as mimo-v2.6-pro on a tool's row.

```
jianmu claude xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro
jianmu codex xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro
jianmu opencode xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash
```

## Regions and endpoints

| Plan | Chat Completions and Responses | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token Plan · China | `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |
| Token Plan · Singapore | `https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |
| Token Plan · Europe | `https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |
| Pay as you go | `https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1` | `https://api.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic` |

A Token Plan's tp- key is spent only at the host of the region it was bought in. Each key in the provider names its region, so keys from several regions and pay as you go can share one provider. Plans and their keys are at platform.xiaomimimo.com/token-plan.

## Models

Each region names its own catalog: a plan's region lists the plan's models before Xiaomi's public catalog, and pay as you go uses the public one alone. The main chat models are mimo-v2.6-pro, mimo-v2.6-flash, mimo-v2.5-pro and mimo-v2.5. The plan catalogs price their models at $0, which jianmu doesn't take as a price, so a pay-as-you-go call is counted at Xiaomi's own prices, not at $0. The model list is read from api.xiaomimimo.com.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Each MiMo region has an Anthropic endpoint, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. Each MiMo region serves Responses, so Codex's requests go as they are. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; jianmu points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : jianmu writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## The MiMo app subscription

This page is about the platform's API keys. The MiMo app subscription you sign in to with a Xiaomi account (mimo-app) is another thing: it moved out of jianmu's built-ins into the community plugin `@magpie-community/opencode-mimo-auth`; install it from jianmu's Plugins page and sign in.

## FAQ

### How do I use Xiaomi MiMo in Claude Code?

Add Xiaomi MiMo in jianmu with your tp- key's region (say Plan · China), then pick mimo-v2.6-pro on Claude Code's row, or run jianmu claude xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro. Requests go to that region's Anthropic endpoint, such as https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic.

### Does a MiMo Token Plan key work in another region?

No. A tp- key is spent only at its own region's host. Set each key's region in jianmu; keys from several regions can share one provider.

### Does MiMo work in Codex?

Yes. Each MiMo region serves OpenAI Responses, so jianmu passes Codex's requests through. Run jianmu codex xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro.

### Can I use the MiMo app subscription too?

Yes, but not in this provider. The MiMo app subscription signed in with a Xiaomi account is served by the community plugin @magpie-community/opencode-mimo-auth; install it from jianmu's Plugins page.

The same for other providers: [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud), [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun

# StepFun Step Plan in Claude Code and Codex

StepFun has two sites with separate accounts: platform.stepfun.com in China and platform.stepfun.ai internationally. Each has a Step Plan and pay as you go; the Step Plan is served at its own step_plan endpoints, and its key is refused at pay as you go's. Add the provider for your site in jianmu with the key's plan, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode use Step's models through jianmu's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425.

## Add StepFun

1. **Add the provider and pick the plan.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick StepFun or StepFun (China), set the key's plan to Step Plan or Pay as you go, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as step-5-preview on a tool's row.

An international account is StepFun (provider id `stepfun`); a China account is StepFun (China) (`stepfun-cn`).

```
jianmu claude stepfun-cn/step-5-preview
jianmu codex stepfun-cn/step-3.7-flash
jianmu opencode stepfun/step-5-preview
```

## Sites, plans and endpoints

| Site and plan | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| China · Step Plan | `https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.com/step_plan` |
| China · Pay as you go | `https://api.stepfun.com/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.com` |
| International · Step Plan | `https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan` |
| International · Pay as you go | `https://api.stepfun.ai/v1` | `https://api.stepfun.ai` |

A Step Plan key works only at the endpoints under `step_plan` and is refused at pay as you go's, so jianmu sends each request by the plan its key names. A Step Plan key and a pay-as-you-go key on one site can share one provider. Neither serves Responses.

## Models

The Step Plan catalogs' chat models are step-5-preview, step-3.7-flash, step-3.5-flash and step-3.5-flash-2603; the China Step Plan has step-router-v1 too. Pay as you go adds the speech models stepaudio-2.5-asr, stepaudio-2.5-tts and step-tts-2.

## Balance and Step Plan windows

- **Balance.** : jianmu reads `/v1/accounts` with the API key, in yuan on the China site and dollars on the international one.
- **Step Plan windows.** : the 5-hour and weekly windows and the month's credits are told only to a sign-in on StepFun's platform, not to a key. Sign in on the platform in your own browser, run jianmu's bookmarklet on that page, and paste what it copies into jianmu. jianmu then renews the sign-in and reads the windows itself; it is kept in stepfun-auth.json beside providers.json, readable by you alone. Two providers on one site can be two accounts, each with its own windows.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Both StepFun sites have Anthropic endpoints, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. StepFun doesn't serve Responses, so jianmu converts Codex's requests to Chat Completions, custom tools such as `apply_patch` included. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; jianmu points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : jianmu writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use the StepFun Step Plan in Claude Code?

Add StepFun or StepFun (China) in jianmu with the key's plan set to Step Plan, then pick step-5-preview on Claude Code's row, or run jianmu claude stepfun/step-5-preview. Requests go to https://api.stepfun.ai/step_plan (api.stepfun.com in China).

### Why is my Step Plan key refused at /v1?

A Step Plan key works only at the endpoints under step_plan; pay as you go's /v1 refuses it. Set the key's plan to Step Plan in jianmu and requests go to /step_plan/v1.

### Does StepFun work in Codex?

Yes. StepFun has no Responses endpoint, so jianmu converts Codex's requests to Chat Completions. Run jianmu codex stepfun/step-3.7-flash.

### Can jianmu show the Step Plan's 5-hour and weekly windows?

Yes, once the platform's sign-in is brought over: sign in on platform.stepfun.ai or .com in your browser, run jianmu's bookmarklet and paste what it copies into jianmu. The balance needs only the key.

The same for other providers: [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo), [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud), [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/longcat

# Meituan LongCat in Claude Code and Codex

LongCat is Meituan's model platform, serving its own LongCat models at api.longcat.chat. Accounts from longcat.chat and longcat.ai share that host: Chat Completions and Responses under /openai/v1, Anthropic Messages under /anthropic. Add LongCat in jianmu, and Claude Code's, Codex's, Gemini CLI's and OpenCode's requests go as they are, with jianmu's local gateway on 127.0.0.1:3425 routing them and holding the key.

## Add LongCat

1. **Add the provider.** On Providers, click ＋ Add provider, pick LongCat, paste the key and save.
2. **Pick it for a tool.** On Agents, pick a model such as LongCat-2.0 on a tool's row.

Keys are made at longcat.chat/platform/api_keys.

```
jianmu claude longcat/LongCat-2.0
jianmu codex longcat/LongCat-2.0
jianmu opencode longcat/LongCat-2.5-Preview
```

## Endpoints

| API | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1` |
| Responses | `https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1` |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://api.longcat.chat/anthropic` |
| /models | `https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1/models` |

Both take the key as `Authorization: Bearer`; with `x-api-key` alone LongCat answers missing_api_key, and jianmu's Anthropic requests carry the key in both x-api-key and a Bearer by default, so they pass. An entry another app has at these endpoints is imported as LongCat.

## Models

jianmu gives LongCat-2.0 and LongCat-2.5-Preview, then reads LongCat's list from `/openai/v1/models` and serves that. Model names are case-sensitive; write them as the list does.

## In each agent

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. LongCat has an Anthropic endpoint, so requests go as they are. See [Claude Code with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. LongCat serves Responses, so Codex's requests go as they are. The models show in Codex's `/model`. See [Codex with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini's API; jianmu points it at the local gateway and translates. See [Gemini CLI with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** : jianmu writes the models into opencode.json. See [OpenCode with other models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## FAQ

### How do I use LongCat in Claude Code?

Add LongCat in jianmu with your longcat.chat platform key, then pick LongCat-2.0 on Claude Code's row, or run jianmu claude longcat/LongCat-2.0. Requests go to https://api.longcat.chat/anthropic.

### Does LongCat work in Codex?

Yes. LongCat serves Responses under /openai/v1, so jianmu passes Codex's requests through. Run jianmu codex longcat/LongCat-2.0.

### Why does Claude Code get missing_api_key from LongCat directly?

LongCat takes the key only as Authorization: Bearer and refuses x-api-key alone. Through jianmu, the key goes in both x-api-key and a Bearer by default.

### Does a longcat.ai account work?

Yes. longcat.chat and longcat.ai accounts share api.longcat.chat; add LongCat in jianmu for either.

The same for other providers: [StepFun](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun), [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm), [Kimi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi), [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek), [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen). Hit an error? See [troubleshooting](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen

# Qwen in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Alibaba serves Qwen through DashScope, on Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, Bailian and Qwen Cloud, pay as you go or on a Token Plan. Every one of them speaks OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages. Add your key to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Qwen through jianmu’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`.

## Add Qwen

1. **Get a key.** Pay as you go: [Model Studio](https://modelstudio.console.alibabacloud.com/?tab=playground#/api-key) (international) or [Bailian](https://bailian.console.aliyun.com/?tab=model#/api-key) (China). A Token Plan’s key comes from its own plan page.
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick the Qwen preset your key is from (the table below), paste the key and save. jianmu asks the endpoint which models it serves.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Qwen model such as `qwen3.8-max`.

```
jianmu provider add qwen sk-…                     # Model Studio, international
jianmu provider add qwen-cn sk-…                  # Bailian, China
jianmu provider add bailian-token-plan sk-sp-…    # Bailian Token Plan
jianmu provider add qwencloud sk-ws-… region=us-east-1
```

> **Each key works on its own host only.** A Token Plan key (`sk-sp-…`) is refused by pay-as-you-go endpoints and by the other Token Plans, and a Qwen Cloud key is refused outside its region. If a request comes back 401, check that the key sits under the preset it was made for.

## Plans and endpoints

| Preset | Plan and key | Endpoints (Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen qwen | pay as you go, international (Model Studio) | `https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen (China) qwen-cn | pay as you go, China (Bailian) | `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen Token Plan qwen-token-plan | subscription, `sk-sp-` | `https://token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Bailian Token Plan bailian-token-plan | subscription, `sk-sp-` | `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen Cloud qwencloud | pay as you go, `sk-ws-`, six regions, Singapore the default | `https://{region}.maas.qwencloudapi.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://{region}.maas.qwencloudapi.com/apps/anthropic` |
| Qwen Cloud Token Plan qwencloud-token-plan | subscription, `sk-sp-`, Singapore | `https://token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com/compatible-mode/v1` `https://token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com/apps/anthropic` |

When a Token Plan’s host gives no model list, jianmu offers the plan’s text models as its overview lists them: auto, qwen3.8-max, qwen3.8-flash, qwen3.7-max, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.6-flash, and the DeepSeek and GLM models the plan includes. The Bailian Token Plan also serves a decision model that can classify turns for [intent routing](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/intent).

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what jianmu writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
jianmu claude qwen/qwen3.8-max
jianmu codex qwen/qwen3.8-max
jianmu gemini model qwen/qwen3.7-plus
jianmu opencode qwen/qwen3.8-max
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does Qwen’s Anthropic endpoint, so its requests are passed on as they are. Every tier (opus, sonnet, haiku) runs on the model you pick unless you give one its own. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. DashScope serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not Responses, so jianmu translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included. The model shows in Codex’s `/model` with its reasoning efforts. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. jianmu points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants and cost. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

Qwen Code is one of the agents jianmu connects too: its row takes Qwen’s models or any other vendor’s.

## Thinking and images

- **Whole replies..** DashScope answers a thinking Qwen model only as a stream, and turns away a request for one whole reply. When an agent or a routing group’s classifier asks for one, jianmu asks DashScope for a stream and gives the agent the whole reply, thinking included.
- **Models that always think..** Some models on DashScope refuse to have thinking turned off, such as its `glm-5.3`. When an agent asks for it off and the model refuses, jianmu asks again with thinking left on.
- **Images..** The Qwen-Image and `wan2.7-image` models draw through DashScope’s own image API, on any of the six presets. Choose one in jianmu’s Settings → Models → Images. Give a size as `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, at most 2048×2048.

## Balance and usage

jianmu shows no balance or plan card for Qwen: DashScope has no API for a key’s balance, and neither Token Plan has one for its credits, which the plan’s subscription page in Alibaba’s console shows. The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model that went through jianmu.

## FAQ

### How do I use Qwen in Claude Code?

Add your key in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, then the Qwen preset your key is from), then pick a Qwen model such as `qwen3.8-max` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude qwen/qwen3.8-max`. jianmu writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and passes its requests to DashScope’s Anthropic endpoint.

### Can Codex use Qwen, Qwen3 Coder included?

Yes. jianmu lists the models DashScope gives your key, coder models included, and Codex can use any of them: jianmu translates Codex’s Responses requests to Chat Completions and the replies back. Pick the model on Codex’s row or run `jianmu codex qwen/qwen3.8-max`; it shows in Codex’s `/model` list.

### Which preset do I pick for my key?

The one whose site the key is from. A Token Plan key (`sk-sp-…`) works only on its own plan’s host, and a Qwen Cloud pay-as-you-go key (`sk-ws-…`) only in its own region, so a key added to another preset is turned away with 401.

### Can Qwen Code use other models?

Yes. Qwen Code is one of the agents jianmu connects, so its row in the Agents tab takes any model you have added, Qwen’s or another vendor’s.

### Why does a Qwen request without streaming work in jianmu?

DashScope turns away a thinking Qwen model asked for one whole reply (`enable_thinking` must be false for non-streaming calls). jianmu asks for it streamed and hands the agent the whole reply, thinking included.

### Does jianmu show my Token Plan credits?

No. Neither Token Plan has an API for its credits; the plan’s subscription page in Alibaba’s console shows them. jianmu’s Usage tab still counts the tokens each agent spent.

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Qwen Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen-code). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax

# MiniMax and the MiniMax Coding Plan in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

MiniMax serves an OpenAI-compatible Chat API and an Anthropic-compatible one, on a global site and a China site, for pay-as-you-go keys and Coding Plan keys alike. Add your key to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use models such as `MiniMax-M3` and `MiniMax-M2.7` through jianmu’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`.

## Add MiniMax

1. **Get a key.** Create one at [platform.minimax.io](https://platform.minimax.io/user-center/basic-information/interface-key), or [platform.minimaxi.com](https://platform.minimaxi.com/user-center/basic-information/interface-key) for the China site. A Coding Plan key starts with `sk-cp-`.
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick MiniMax or MiniMax (China), paste the key and save. A pay-as-you-go key and a Coding Plan key go in the same way.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a MiniMax model.

```
jianmu provider add minimax sk-…        # platform.minimax.io
jianmu provider add minimax-cn sk-cp-…  # Coding Plan, platform.minimaxi.com
```

## Plans and endpoints

| Preset | Site | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MiniMax minimax | platform.minimax.io | `https://api.minimax.io/v1` | `https://api.minimax.io/anthropic` |
| MiniMax (China) minimax-cn | platform.minimaxi.com | `https://api.minimaxi.com/v1` | `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic` |

The Coding Plan uses the same endpoints as pay as you go; the key decides which one a request is billed to. A global key and a China key are different accounts, so each goes under its own site’s preset.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what jianmu writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
jianmu claude minimax/MiniMax-M3
jianmu codex minimax/MiniMax-M3
jianmu gemini model minimax/MiniMax-M2.7
jianmu opencode minimax/MiniMax-M3
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does MiniMax’s Anthropic endpoint, so its requests are passed on as they are. Every tier (opus, sonnet, haiku) runs on the model you pick unless you give one its own. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. MiniMax serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not Responses, so jianmu translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included. The model shows in Codex’s `/model` with its reasoning efforts. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. jianmu points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants and cost. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

MiniMax Code is one of the agents jianmu connects too: its row takes MiniMax’s models or any other vendor’s.

## Thinking and effort

- **Interleaved thinking..** MiniMax’s Chat API gives a model’s thinking in the reply text, between `<think>` tags, and wants it back there on later turns. jianmu hands it to the agent as thinking and puts it back where MiniMax expects it.
- **Effort..** `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` and its preview think at levels from low to max. jianmu sends the level an agent asks for in `output_config.effort`, as MiniMax Code does, so it isn’t lost to a token budget.
- **Models that always think..** `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` refuses to have thinking turned off. When an agent asks for it off, jianmu asks again with thinking left on, so the agent gets an answer rather than the error.

## Coding Plan windows and usage

- **Coding Plan windows..** A Coding Plan key’s row shows what is left of each window MiniMax reports, a rolling one and a weekly one, read from MiniMax. Models draw on the general bucket; a bucket metered apart, such as video, shows as a count, like 4 / 5. A pay-as-you-go key has no windows and no card.
- **Routing..** With several Coding Plan keys, jianmu weighs them by their windows and rests one that has used a window up until it resets.
- **Usage..** The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model that went through jianmu.

## FAQ

### How do I use MiniMax M2.7 or M3 in Claude Code?

Add your MiniMax key in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, MiniMax or MiniMax (China)), then pick a model such as `MiniMax-M3` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude minimax/MiniMax-M3`. jianmu writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and passes its requests to MiniMax’s Anthropic endpoint, `https://api.minimax.io/anthropic`.

### How do I use the MiniMax Coding Plan?

Add the Coding Plan key (`sk-cp-…`) to the MiniMax preset of the site you bought it on, the same as a pay-as-you-go key. jianmu tells the two apart by what MiniMax says about the key, and shows a Coding Plan key’s usage windows on its row.

### Can Codex use MiniMax?

Yes. MiniMax serves Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages but not Responses, so jianmu translates Codex’s requests and MiniMax’s replies. Pick the model on Codex’s row or run `jianmu codex minimax/MiniMax-M3`; it shows in Codex’s `/model` list.

### Can MiniMax Code use other models?

Yes. MiniMax Code is one of the agents jianmu connects, so its row in the Agents tab takes any model you have added, MiniMax’s or another vendor’s.

### Why does MiniMax’s thinking show up in the text?

MiniMax’s Chat API puts a model’s thinking in the reply text between `<think>` tags. jianmu takes it out and gives it to the agent as thinking, then puts it back on the next turns, where MiniMax wants it.

### Can I use several MiniMax keys?

Yes. Add them all to the MiniMax provider and tick each one. jianmu spreads requests over them, and weighs and rests Coding Plan keys by their windows, so a key that has used up its window sits out until it resets.

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openrouter

# OpenRouter in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

OpenRouter sells many vendors’ models behind one key and serves them on OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages. Add the key to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use any OpenRouter model through jianmu’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent on a model of its own.

## Add OpenRouter

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys).
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick OpenRouter, paste the key and save. jianmu asks OpenRouter which models it serves.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose an OpenRouter model such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`.

```
jianmu provider add openrouter sk-…
jianmu provider test openrouter
```

Model ids in jianmu are `provider/model`, so OpenRouter’s read `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`: the provider, then OpenRouter’s own id. The key is kept in jianmu’s settings; jianmu doesn’t take it from your shell.

OpenRouter documents two optional headers that credit an app in its rankings, `HTTP-Referer` and `X-OpenRouter-Title`. jianmu doesn’t send them. The provider editor’s Headers field offers them if you want your requests credited.

## Endpoints

| API | Base URL | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | the model list, requests to non-Claude models, image models |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | Claude Code’s requests, and Claude models from any agent |
| Decisions | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | decision models for [intent routing](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/intent) |

jianmu doesn’t use OpenRouter’s Responses API. An agent that speaks Responses, such as Codex, is translated to one of the two above.

## Model list

- **Where it comes from..** jianmu fetches the list from `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`, which gives each model’s context length. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from the `openrouter` catalog on models.dev.
- **Which models agents see..** OpenRouter lists hundreds. Unless you pick some, jianmu shows agents the first 24 OpenRouter lists, newest first. Pick the rest in the provider’s model list, or turn on Best in family to keep only the newest of each family.
- **New models..** `auto-include` rules expose matching models now and each one a later fetch lists for the first time, and `refresh-every` has jianmu fetch the list again by itself.
- **Image models..** OpenRouter’s `/models` lists text models only, so jianmu reads image models such as FLUX, Seedream, Riverflow, Recraft and GPT Image from `/api/v1/images/models`. Choose one in Settings → Models → Images.
- **Decision models..** OpenRouter’s decision models (`liquid/d1`, `cloudflare/clef`, `~typesafe/jev-latest`…) are listed too, so a routing group can classify turns with the same key.

```
jianmu provider models openrouter +anthropic/claude-opus-5.5   # expose one more
jianmu provider models openrouter best                          # newest of each family
jianmu provider auto-include openrouter '*:free'               # every free model, now and later
jianmu provider refresh-every openrouter 1d
```

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what jianmu writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
jianmu claude openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
jianmu codex openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
jianmu gemini model openrouter/google/gemini-3-pro
jianmu opencode openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does OpenRouter at `https://openrouter.ai/api`, so its requests are passed on as they are. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. jianmu translates each request and the reply, streaming and tool calls included: a Claude model goes to OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint, every other model to Chat Completions. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. jianmu translates it the same way as Codex’s requests. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to OpenRouter as they are, except for Claude models, which jianmu sends to the Anthropic endpoint for their prompt cache (see below). [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

If OpenRouter says a model isn’t served on the endpoint jianmu chose, jianmu builds the request again for the other one and remembers that for the model.

## Reasoning

- **Models that always reason..** Some OpenRouter models refuse to have reasoning turned off (“reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled”). When an agent asks for it off, jianmu asks again with the level left to the model, on Chat Completions and on Messages alike.
- **Effort mid-conversation..** Claude Code sends a turn’s effort inside the conversation. OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint refuses that on some models, such as DeepSeek and GLM. jianmu asks again at once without it, and doesn’t send it to OpenRouter again until jianmu restarts.
- **Earlier thinking..** OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint turns away a thinking block without a signature, so jianmu always sends one. On Chat Completions, earlier reasoning that an agent sends back in OpenRouter’s `reasoning` or `reasoning_details` fields is read as the model’s thinking.

## Cache, cost and credits

- **Claude’s prompt cache..** On Chat Completions, a relay that serves both APIs drops `cache_control`, and every turn is billed uncached. So jianmu asks Claude models on OpenRouter’s Messages endpoint, from any agent, with the cache breakpoints the translation adds.
- **Cache tokens..** jianmu reads cache reads and OpenRouter’s `cache_write_tokens` from each reply, so the Usage tab counts cache hits and writes apart from the rest.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call with OpenRouter’s prices from models.dev, or the model maker’s list price when the catalog has none. A model listed at $0, such as one ending in `:free`, shows free beside it in jianmu’s pickers.
- **Which provider answered..** OpenRouter names the provider that served each reply. jianmu keeps it, and the call’s details in the Usage tab show it as Upstream provider.
- **Credits..** The OpenRouter row shows what is left on the account, in dollars: total credits less total usage, read from `/api/v1/credits`. It’s the whole account’s figure, so each key of one account shows the same.

## Several keys and free models

One OpenRouter provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over. The provider’s routing can also rotate, weight or drain them instead. Adding the preset again makes a second OpenRouter provider; to spread requests over several keys, add them all to the one provider.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when OpenRouter is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.
- **Free models..** OpenRouter’s free models take 20 requests a minute. `rpm` holds each key to a rate: one request more waits for room, up to 2 minutes, then gets a 429 with a `Retry-After`.
- **Free-model 429s..** When a free model is refused by the shared pool of the provider serving it, jianmu rests that model only and keeps the other free models in use. Any other 429 on a free model is OpenRouter’s account-wide free limit, and the key rests.
- **A pool of free models..** A routing group can take every free model OpenRouter lists with the pattern `openrouter/*:free`, today’s and those it lists later.

```
jianmu provider rpm openrouter 20
jianmu provider spend-cap openrouter <key> 20 month
jianmu provider fallback openrouter deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
jianmu group add my-free-pool models='openrouter/*:free' routing=order
jianmu group set opus-anywhere stays=session models+=openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
```

## Troubleshooting

- **The model list has only `anthropic/` ids, or fails to load..** A provider given only `https://openrouter.ai/api` gets OpenRouter’s catalog under `anthropic/` names it doesn’t serve. Give it the Chat Completions base, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, or use the OpenRouter preset, which has both.
- **“Mid-conversation reasoning effort (configuration_update) is not supported”..** OpenRouter says this about Claude Code’s per-turn effort on models such as DeepSeek and GLM. jianmu asks again at once without the effort, so the agent gets its answer, and stops sending it to OpenRouter until jianmu restarts.
- **402 with “can only afford” or “fewer max_tokens”..** OpenRouter refused the request’s size or its in-flight budget, not because the balance is spent. jianmu rests the key for half an hour and tries it again then; unlike a key out of credit, its rest doesn’t grow with each refusal.
- **Web search asks a model you didn’t pick..** It doesn’t: when OpenRouter answers jianmu’s web search, jianmu asks one of the OpenRouter models you have picked, since OpenRouter can refuse others for your region. For that search jianmu turns on OpenRouter’s own `web` plugin, which works with any of its models.
- **Checking a key..** `jianmu provider test openrouter` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use OpenRouter in Claude Code?

Add your OpenRouter key in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, OpenRouter), then pick a model such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`. jianmu writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and passes its requests on to OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint as they are.

### Can Codex use OpenRouter models?

Yes. Codex speaks only the Responses API, which jianmu doesn’t use at OpenRouter. jianmu translates each Codex request: a Claude model goes to OpenRouter’s Anthropic endpoint and every other model to Chat Completions, and the reply comes back to Codex as Responses.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use OpenRouter?

Yes. Gemini CLI’s requests are translated the same way as Codex’s. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to OpenRouter as they are, except for Claude models, which jianmu sends to the Anthropic endpoint so the prompt cache works.

### How do I use only OpenRouter’s free models?

Make a routing group from the pattern `openrouter/*:free`, for example `jianmu group add my-free-pool models='openrouter/*:free' routing=order`. It takes every free model OpenRouter lists, including ones it lists later. Models priced at $0 show free in jianmu’s pickers.

### Why do OpenRouter’s free models answer 429?

OpenRouter’s free models take 20 requests a minute. Set `jianmu provider rpm openrouter 20` and jianmu holds requests back to that rate. When the 429 comes from the shared pool of the provider serving one free model, jianmu rests only that model and keeps the other free models in use.

### Does jianmu show my OpenRouter credits?

Yes. jianmu reads OpenRouter’s credits endpoint and shows what is left in dollars: total credits less total usage. The figure is for the whole account, so every key of one account shows the same.

### Why does jianmu fetch OpenRouter’s model list from /api/v1?

Asked at the Anthropic base, OpenRouter answers with its catalog under `anthropic/` names it doesn’t serve. jianmu fetches the list from the Chat Completions base, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, and a provider given only OpenRouter’s Anthropic base is told to add that Chat base.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mistral) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.

# GitHub Copilot in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

A Copilot seat comes with Claude, GPT and Gemini models, among others. Sign in to Copilot once in jianmu, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use the models your plan gets, through jianmu’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`. No API key.

## Sign in to Copilot

1. **Open Add provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider and click the Copilot tile.
2. **Enter the code on GitHub.** jianmu shows a code and opens GitHub’s device page, `github.com/login/device`. Enter the code and approve. jianmu then asks GitHub whose account it is and which plan it has, and the account shows under Copilot.
3. **Pick a model for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a `copilot/…` model.

```
jianmu accounts add copilot                        # github.com
jianmu accounts add copilot --host acme.ghe.com    # GitHub Enterprise on GHE.com
jianmu accounts copilot                            # each account and what it has used
```

jianmu serves a Copilot sign-in from three places:

- **Copilot’s editor plugins..** The sign-in they keep in `~/.config/github-copilot` (`apps.json` or `hosts.json`).
- **The Copilot CLI..** Its sign-in in `~/.copilot/config.json`, with the token in the system keychain or in that file. jianmu on Windows also reads the Copilot CLI sign-in of a running WSL distro, from `config.json` only.
- **jianmu’s own..** Each account you sign in with a code in jianmu. Its token is kept in jianmu’s own `logins.json`.

The editors’ and the CLI’s sign-ins are only read; jianmu never writes them. When both are there, the editors’ github.com sign-in comes first, then the CLI’s, then an editor’s GHE.com sign-in. If GitHub turns away the editors’ token, jianmu uses the CLI’s sign-in of the same account instead, never another account’s.

> **GitHub Enterprise on GHE.com.** An enterprise with data residency signs in at its own `<name>.ghe.com`, so add the account with `--host` (or answer the GHE.com question in the sign-in sheet). jianmu accepts github.com or a `<name>.ghe.com` address and nothing else, so a GitHub token is never sent to a host of your choosing. The account is served at its enterprise’s `copilot-api.<name>.ghe.com`. One login on github.com and on GHE.com is two accounts: `you` and `you@acme.ghe.com`.

## The models your seat gets

jianmu asks Copilot’s `/models` for each account and lists what comes back, so the list follows your plan rather than a fixed table. The models are named `copilot/` and Copilot’s own id: `copilot/claude-opus-5.5`, `copilot/gpt-5.4`, `copilot/gpt-5.3-codex`. `jianmu models` prints them all.

- **Chat models only..** Copilot’s internal models and the ones no model picker offers are left out, and so is a model the account isn’t allowed to turn on.
- **Terms to accept..** A model whose terms are still waiting is listed anyway. The first request for it accepts them, as turning it on in Copilot’s editor would.
- **Reasoning efforts.** come from what Copilot lists for each model, and show in each agent’s picker.
- **Auto.** is always on the list; see Copilot Auto.
- **Image models.** such as GPT Image 2.5 Flare are listed for drawing (Settings → Models → Images), and are never offered as a chat model.
- **Older models..** A model for which Copilot names no API, such as GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o on a Student plan, is asked on Chat Completions only.

Claude Code reads a Claude version written with a dot as an older model, so jianmu gives it Copilot’s Claude models with dashes (`claude-opus-5-5`) and turns the name back before the request reaches Copilot. Other agents see Copilot’s own spelling.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what jianmu writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
jianmu claude copilot/claude-opus-5.5
jianmu codex copilot/gpt-5.4
jianmu gemini model copilot/gpt-5.4-mini
jianmu opencode copilot/claude-opus-5.5
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. Copilot serves its Claude models on Messages too, so Claude Code’s requests go to them as they are; a GPT or Gemini model gets them translated. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses, and jianmu asks Copilot’s OpenAI models on Responses, so they pass through. Codex’s web search runs on Copilot’s side for those models, and Codex’s native compaction works with them too, but not with Copilot’s Claude models. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s API. jianmu points it at its gateway and translates. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** gets the model in `opencode.json`, with its reasoning variants. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

The Copilot CLI is one of the agents jianmu connects, too. Its row offers `auto` (Copilot picks) and Copilot’s own models, plus every other model you have added to jianmu, which reach it through the Copilot CLI’s `providers.json`.

## How requests reach Copilot

Copilot doesn’t serve every model on every API. Its newest OpenAI models answer only on Responses; its Claude models on Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages; its Gemini models and the older ones on Chat Completions only. jianmu sends each request on an API the model is served on, and translates between that API and the agent’s when they differ, streaming and tool calls included.

- **Wrong API..** When Copilot answers that a model isn’t served on the API it was asked on, jianmu rebuilds the request for the next one and remembers which one worked.
- **Pin one yourself..** `jianmu model api copilot/<model> chat` (or `responses`, `anthropic`) asks the model on that API only; `auto` hands the choice back to jianmu.
- **Tool schemas for Gemini..** Copilot turned some of Codex’s tool schemas away for its Gemini models with 400 “invalid request body”. jianmu rewrites the ones it can prove safe to rewrite, so those tools reach the model.

## Copilot Auto

`copilot/auto` is the model Copilot chooses for your account. It isn’t in Copilot’s `/models`, so jianmu always adds it. On a Student plan it is the only model you may choose.

- jianmu asks Copilot for a pick with the turn’s prompt, at Copilot Chat’s default setting, and keeps a pick for at most an hour.
- If Copilot has no Auto for the account, or picks a model the account was refused, a model the account may pick by hand stands in for 10 minutes: Copilot’s base model, its default, `gpt-4.1`, a model that isn’t premium, then the rest.
- If Copilot then refuses the model Auto picked, jianmu picks another and sends the request again.
- The model Auto chose is noted on the request’s route, so you can see what answered.

## Premium requests, usage and cost

Each Copilot account has a card with three allowances, as GitHub reports them: Premium requests, Chat requests and Completions, each as used / allowance. `jianmu accounts copilot` prints the same.

- **Monthly..** The allowances renew each month, on the date GitHub gives.
- **Unlimited.** shows as Unlimited. A window GitHub gives no figure for is left off the card, never shown as unlimited.
- **One request a turn..** A turn you type is billed as one request; the tool replies that carry it on are not.
- **Business and Enterprise..** A seat that uses up its allowance is paused, so jianmu counts the account as used up and moves on to the next one. An organization’s pooled premium allowance shows as used up once the pool is spent.
- **Other plans..** When your plan lets you pay past the premium allowance, using it up doesn’t stop the account. Completions are counted too, but no request through jianmu uses them.
- **No allowance..** Copilot’s base model, `gpt-4.1`, is billed to no allowance on any plan.

The Usage tab counts tokens, cache hits and cost for each agent and model that went through jianmu. Cost on a subscription is an estimate at the model maker’s list price, or at the price you set for the model. One difference from Anthropic’s own pricing: Copilot bills a cache write at one price however long it is kept, so jianmu prices a 1-hour write at the 5-minute rate. For `claude-opus-5.5` that is $5 per million tokens, where Anthropic’s 2× input would be $8.

## Several accounts and failover

- **Add another..** Click the Copilot tile again, or run `jianmu accounts add copilot` again. The one in use is listed first, then the rest in the order you added them.
- **Choose which goes first..** `jianmu accounts switch copilot <login>`; `jianmu accounts forget copilot <login>` removes one. With the same login on github.com and GHE.com, name it in full (`you@acme.ghe.com`) or add `--host`.
- **Spread requests..** Tick the accounts to use on Copilot’s row. Routing sets how requests spread over them, Smart by default; the provider’s Fallback lists models to use when every account is out, rate limited or down. See [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/subscriptions#accounts).
- **One model from two subscriptions..** Claude Opus from your Claude subscription and from Copilot become one group by themselves, `auto/<model>`. To set the order yourself: `jianmu group add "Opus anywhere" models=claude/claude-opus-5-5,copilot/claude-opus-5.5 routing=order`.
- **A stale editor sign-in..** When GitHub refuses the token Copilot’s editors keep, an account you signed in to jianmu with the same login is kept and used.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub refused this Copilot sign-in; sign in again | GitHub turned the account’s token away. Sign in again from its row: the account is signed in again in place, and its settings stay. A network error or a 5xx from GitHub never marks an account, and the mark goes when a request is served. |
| the GitHub token Copilot’s editors keep in … was refused | The editors’ sign-in has lapsed. Sign in to Copilot again in your editor or in jianmu, or move that file aside. |
| <login> has no Copilot subscription | The GitHub account you approved has no Copilot plan. Sign in with the account that has the seat. |
| Copilot doesn’t serve this model on Anthropic’s Messages API; it isn’t about your plan | Copilot serves that model on other APIs only. `jianmu model api copilot/<model> chat` sends it on Chat Completions. |
| The requested model is not supported. | Copilot won’t serve that model to this account now. jianmu leaves it out of the account’s models and the agents’ pickers for 6 hours, then tries it again. Under Auto, another model is picked and the request is sent again. |
| Copilot doesn’t offer Auto to this account … | Copilot made no pick and the account lists no model it may pick by hand. Check the plan at `github.com/settings/copilot`. |
| the code expired; start again · the sign-in was declined on GitHub | The device code ran out before it was entered, or the request was declined on GitHub’s page. Start the sign-in again. |
| Copilot signs in on github.com or an enterprise’s <name>.ghe.com, not … | The `--host` given isn’t github.com or a GHE.com address. |
| subscription accounts are off in jianmu | Settings → Privacy → Subscription accounts is off (or `jianmu accounts discovery off` was run), so jianmu reads no sign-in and serves no subscription, Copilot included. Turn it on, or run `jianmu accounts discovery on`. |

## FAQ

### How do I use GitHub Copilot in Claude Code?

Sign in to Copilot in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, Copilot; GitHub gives you a code to enter), then pick a `copilot/…` model such as `copilot/claude-opus-5.5` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude copilot/claude-opus-5.5`. jianmu writes Claude Code’s `settings.json`. Copilot’s Claude models get Claude Code’s Anthropic requests as they are; its GPT and Gemini models get them translated.

### Can Codex use Copilot’s models?

Yes. Codex speaks OpenAI Responses, and jianmu asks Copilot’s OpenAI models on Responses too, so they pass through, web search included. Copilot’s Claude and Gemini models are translated. Pick one on Codex’s row or run `jianmu codex copilot/gpt-5.4`; it shows in Codex’s `/model` list.

### Can I use Copilot in Gemini CLI and OpenCode?

Yes. Run `jianmu gemini model copilot/gpt-5.4-mini` or `jianmu opencode copilot/claude-opus-5.5`, or pick the model on the agent’s row. jianmu translates Gemini CLI’s requests, and writes the model into OpenCode’s `opencode.json`.

### Do I need VS Code or another editor signed in to Copilot?

No. jianmu signs in to GitHub itself with a device code. If Copilot’s editor plugins or the Copilot CLI are already signed in on this computer, jianmu reads that sign-in too, and never changes it.

### Does it spend my premium requests?

Requests go to Copilot on your account, so they count against your plan as Copilot counts them. A turn you type is billed as one request; the tool replies that carry it on are not. jianmu shows each account’s Premium requests, Chat requests and Completions as used out of the allowance.

### Does it work with Copilot Business, Enterprise and GHE.com?

Yes. jianmu reads the plan from GitHub: Free, Pro, Pro+, Max, Education, Business or Enterprise. An enterprise on GHE.com signs in with `jianmu accounts add copilot --host <name>.ghe.com`. A Business or Enterprise seat that uses up its allowance is paused, and jianmu counts the account as used up until it renews.

### Why is a Copilot model missing from my list?

jianmu lists what Copilot’s `/models` gives the account: chat models only, without the ones no model picker offers or the account can’t turn on. A model Copilot answered with “The requested model is not supported.” is left out for 6 hours, then tried again in case your plan changed.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm) · [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openrouter) · [Ollama](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Copilot CLI on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot-cli). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.
