Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini

# Gemini in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Google serves Gemini on the Gemini Developer API, the one an AI Studio key opens, and on Vertex AI in your own Google Cloud project. Add either to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Gemini 3 models such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` through jianmu’s gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent on a model of its own.

## Add a Gemini API key

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey).
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Google Gemini, paste the key and save. jianmu asks Google which models it serves.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Gemini model such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`.

```
jianmu provider add google AIza…
jianmu provider test google
```

Model ids in jianmu are `provider/model`, so the Gemini API’s read `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`: the provider, then Google’s own id. The key is kept in jianmu’s settings; jianmu doesn’t take it from your shell.

## Endpoints

| API | Base URL | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions (OpenAI-compatible) | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | the model list, and requests from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other agents |
| Gemini API | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta` | Gemini CLI’s requests, Google Search, image models |

The preset fills in the Gemini API URL once. If you clear it, it stays empty. Every request that doesn’t come from a Gemini client goes to Chat Completions.

## Model list

- **Where it comes from..** jianmu asks the OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the list once. It is the Gemini API’s list too, so jianmu doesn’t ask twice. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from the `google` catalog on models.dev.
- **Image models..** At Google, a Gemini image model draws on the Gemini API. Choose one in Settings → Models → Images.

## In each agent

Pick the model on an agent’s row in the Agents tab, or from a terminal. Each guide says what jianmu writes in that agent’s config and how to switch back.

```
jianmu claude google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
jianmu codex google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
jianmu gemini model google/gemini-3.8-flash
jianmu opencode google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages. jianmu translates each request to Gemini’s Chat Completions and the reply back to Messages, streaming and tool calls included. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks only OpenAI Responses. jianmu translates it to Chat Completions the same way, and the reply comes back to Codex as Responses. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Gemini’s own API, so its requests go to the Gemini API as it sends them, and its Google Search runs there. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Google as they are. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## Thinking

- **Visible thoughts..** Gemini’s OpenAI-compatible API gives the model’s thoughts only when asked in `thinking_config`. When an agent asks for visible reasoning, jianmu asks for the thoughts with `include_thoughts`, so a long think shows as thinking instead of a first word that comes late.
- **Levels and budgets..** Gemini 3 and later are sent a thinking level. Gemini 2 models are sent a budget instead: 1024 tokens for minimal and low, 8192 for medium and 24576 for high. xhigh and max are sent as high, and an effort with no level is left to the model.
- **Reasoning off..** Gemini 3 can’t stop thinking. When an agent turns reasoning off, jianmu asks for the model’s lowest level instead.
- **A level the model doesn’t have..** Not every Gemini 3 has every level: `gemini-3.8-flash` has no minimal. When Google turns a level away with a 400, jianmu asks again at the nearest level the model has and remembers it until jianmu restarts.
- **`thinking_config` turned away..** That is a different 400: a server in front of Gemini that refuses the field itself. jianmu asks again with `reasoning_effort` alone and stops sending `thinking_config` there.
- **Proxies..** A Gemini model behind a proxy on this computer or your network, such as one on `localhost` or a private address, is handled the same way.

## Thought signatures and tools

- **Thought signatures..** Gemini 3 signs the first function call of each step, and the next request fails with 400 “Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts” if the signature is gone. Agents don’t keep it. jianmu carries it in the call id the agent gets, as a short reference to a file in jianmu’s folder, and puts it back on the way to Gemini. Signatures are kept for 90 days.
- **Calls Gemini didn’t sign..** A call from another model earlier in the conversation, or one whose id an agent shortened, goes with Google’s documented `skip_thought_signature_validator`, so a conversation can move to Gemini halfway.
- **One provider’s signature..** A signature goes back only to the provider that gave it. In a routing group of Vertex AI and the Gemini API, the other provider gets the call as unsigned history instead of answering “Corrupted thought signature”.
- **Tool schemas..** jianmu gives each untyped schema in an agent’s tools a type, which Vertex AI needs, and removes boolean schemas and `x-` keywords such as MCP’s `x-mcp-header`. Tools that need none of this go as they came.
- **The end of a stream..** Gemini’s OpenAI-compatible API sends a whole function call in one chunk and its `finish_reason` in the next. If that reason is lost after the usage arrived, jianmu fills it in; without the usage, the reply is reported as cut off rather than passed on as complete.

## Cache, cost and search

- **Prompt cache..** Gemini keeps a prompt cached without saying so on that turn. jianmu counts such a turn as a cache write and keeps the next turn on the same provider and key, and remembers which one answered across restarts.
- **Cached and thinking tokens..** jianmu reads cached tokens and reasoning tokens from each reply, on Chat Completions and on the Gemini API alike, and the Usage tab counts them.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call from the `google` catalog on models.dev.
- **Web search..** Gemini runs Google Search on the Gemini API only for a request that declares no function tools. Claude Code’s and Codex’s requests declare tools, so their web search is jianmu’s own, which the Google provider answers itself on your key: those searches spend your Gemini API credit.

## Several keys and rate limits

One Google Gemini provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over. The provider’s routing can also rotate, weight or drain them instead.

- **Per-minute 429s..** Gemini’s 429 “You exceeded your current quota … Please retry in 33s” for a per-minute limit is read as a rate limit, not a used-up plan, and so is Vertex AI’s `requests_per_minute_per_project`. The key rests from a minute, doubling, up to `rest-cap`.
- **Holding to a rate..** `rpm` holds each key to a number of requests a minute: one request more waits for room, up to 2 minutes, then gets a 429.
- **Out of quota..** `quota-rest` sets how long a key rests once its quota is spent: 15 minutes by default, up to 8 days, or until a time of day.
- **Spend caps and fallbacks..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, and `fallback` names where requests go when Gemini is out of quota or down.

```
jianmu provider rpm google 10
jianmu provider spend-cap google <key> 20 month
jianmu provider fallback google google-vertex/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
```

## Vertex AI

The Google Vertex AI preset asks Gemini in your Google Cloud project, with no API key. Give it the project’s id; the project in each request is the one billed.

```
gcloud auth application-default login
jianmu provider add google-vertex project=my-project
jianmu claude google-vertex/gemini-3.1-pro-preview
```

- **Credentials..** jianmu signs with gcloud’s Application Default Credentials, or with the file `credentials=` names by its full path: a user sign-in, a service account key or an impersonated service account. `impersonate=` takes a service account’s email, and needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on it. The metadata server, workload identity federation and Vertex AI’s express-mode API keys aren’t read.
- **Location..** `location=` is `global` (the default), `us`, `eu` or a region such as `us-central1`.
- **Models..** The preset has its own list, among them `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, partner models such as `zai-org/glm-5.2-maas`, and Claude models such as `claude-opus-5-5`. Gemini goes to Vertex AI’s Gemini API, a partner model to its OpenAI-compatible chat completions, and Claude to Anthropic’s Messages API, all in your project.
- **Thinking on Vertex AI..** A Gemini 3 level is fitted to the levels that model has, and reasoning off asks for its lowest. Gemini 2.5 takes a budget: Pro from 128 to 32768 tokens (128 when off), Flash up to 24576 (0 when off), Flash-Lite from 512 to 24576 (0 when off).

## Google sign-ins

Two Google sign-ins give Gemini models without a key. They are subscriptions, set up as on [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/subscriptions).

- **Gemini (Code Assist)..** Gemini CLI’s Google sign-in, as `gemini/…`: `jianmu accounts add gemini`. Google answers it only for a Code Assist Standard or Enterprise account with a Google Cloud project of its own; `jianmu accounts project gemini <email> <project>` names the project.
- **Antigravity..** As `antigravity/…`: `jianmu accounts add antigravity`. Its sign-in gives Antigravity’s Claude and Gemini models.

## Troubleshooting

- **“Thinking level MINIMAL is not supported for this model”..** The model has no minimal level. jianmu asks again at the nearest level it has, so the agent gets its answer, and remembers the level until jianmu restarts. Only when no level is left does the error reach the agent as Google sent it.
- **“Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts”..** A Gemini 3 call lost its signature. Through jianmu the signature rides in the call id and is put back, and a call with none goes with `skip_thought_signature_validator`.
- **“Corrupted thought signature”..** The signature was cut short or came from another provider. jianmu sends a signature only to the provider that gave it.
- **429 with “Please retry in 33s”..** A per-minute limit, not a spent plan. The key rests for a short while, and `rpm` keeps requests under the limit from then on.
- **Vertex AI: a schema “didn’t specify the schema type field”..** jianmu types every untyped tool schema it sends to Gemini, so this shouldn’t reach the agent.
- **Vertex AI won’t save..** “Google Vertex AI needs the id of your Google Cloud project”: add `project=`. A credentials file has to be given by its full path.
- **Checking a key..** `jianmu provider test google` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use Gemini in Claude Code?

Add a Gemini API key in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, Google Gemini), then pick a model such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. jianmu writes Claude Code’s `settings.json` and translates each Messages request to Gemini’s Chat Completions, tool calls and streaming included.

### Can Codex use Gemini models?

Yes. Codex speaks only the Responses API. jianmu translates each Codex request to Gemini’s Chat Completions and the reply back to Responses. Run `jianmu codex google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, or pick the model on Codex’s row.

### Does Gemini 3 Pro keep working across tool calls in Claude Code?

Yes. Gemini 3 signs its function calls and refuses the next request without the signature. jianmu carries each signature in the call id the agent gets and puts it back on the way to Gemini, so tool loops keep going, and a call from another model is sent as unsigned.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use my Gemini key through jianmu?

Yes. Gemini CLI’s requests go to the Gemini API as it sends them, Google Search included. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Gemini’s OpenAI-compatible API as they are.

### Why does Gemini answer 429 with “Please retry in 33s”?

That is a per-minute limit, not a spent quota. jianmu reads it as a rate limit and rests the key briefly. Run `jianmu provider rpm google 10`, with your own limit, and jianmu holds requests to that rate.

### Can I use Gemini through Vertex AI instead of an API key?

Yes. Add the Google Vertex AI preset with your project’s id, for example `jianmu provider add google-vertex project=my-project`. jianmu signs with gcloud’s Application Default Credentials or a credentials file, and your project is billed.

### Can I use my Gemini Code Assist or Antigravity sign-in instead?

Yes. Both are subscriptions: `jianmu accounts add gemini` or `jianmu accounts add antigravity`, then pick a `gemini/…` or `antigravity/…` model. Code Assist needs a Standard or Enterprise account with a Google Cloud project of its own.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openai) · [Grok](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models). To run Google’s Antigravity app on other models, see [Antigravity on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/antigravity). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok

# Grok in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

xAI serves its Grok models on three APIs at once: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. Add an xAI API key to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Grok through jianmu’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own.

## Add xAI

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [console.x.ai](https://console.x.ai).
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick xAI, paste the key and save. jianmu asks xAI which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Grok model such as `grok-4.7`.

```
jianmu provider add xai xai-…
jianmu provider test xai
```

Model ids in jianmu are `provider/model`, so xAI’s read `xai/grok-4.7`: the provider, then xAI’s own id. The key is kept in jianmu’s settings; jianmu doesn’t take it from your shell.

## Endpoints

| API | Base URL | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api.x.ai/v1` | the model list, OpenCode’s requests, and every request jianmu translates, Gemini CLI’s among them |
| Responses | `https://api.x.ai/v1` | Codex’s requests, and web search that xAI runs itself |
| Anthropic Messages | `https://api.x.ai` | Claude Code’s requests |

An agent whose API xAI serves is passed on to that API. When jianmu has to translate, it uses Chat Completions: it keeps Responses first only for OpenAI’s own models at OpenAI, and Messages first only for Claude models, and Grok is neither.

## Model list

jianmu fetches the list from xAI, at `https://api.x.ai/v1/models`, so agents see the models your key can use. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from models.dev’s `xai` catalog. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
jianmu provider models xai +grok-4.7
jianmu provider refresh-every xai 1d
```

## In each agent

```
jianmu claude xai/grok-4.7
jianmu codex xai/grok-4.7
jianmu gemini model xai/grok-4.7
jianmu opencode xai/grok-4.7
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does xAI at `https://api.x.ai`, so its requests go there as they are, with the fixes below. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which xAI serves at `https://api.x.ai/v1`, so its requests go there as they are too. If xAI turns away Codex’s custom tools (“unknown variant `custom`”), jianmu translates that model’s Codex requests from then on and offers those tools as ordinary functions. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API, which xAI doesn’t serve. jianmu translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back, streaming and tool calls included. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to xAI as they are. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

Grok Build, xAI’s own CLI, can take jianmu’s models too: jianmu adds them to `~/.grok/config.toml`, so they join its `/model` picker.

## What jianmu fixes for xAI

xAI’s API turns away a few things that agents send. jianmu changes them on the way, on requests it passes on and on those it translates alike, so the agent never sees these errors:

- **Tool patterns..** xAI reads a tool’s `pattern` with a different regex engine, so a pattern such as Claude Code’s `^[^\s[\]]+$` on Windows failed with “Schema validation failed: … is not a "regex"”. jianmu escapes it so xAI reads it as JavaScript does.
- **Tool roots..** A tool whose parameters start with `anyOf`, `oneOf` or `allOf`, such as a Codex desktop automation tool, is folded into an object from the first request. xAI otherwise answers “tool parameter root must be an object type”.
- **Empty fields..** `"required": null` in a tool’s schema, and `"content": null` on a Codex reasoning item, are left out. xAI otherwise answers “/required: null is not of type "array"” or “Could not decode the compaction blob”.
- **System turns..** Claude Code’s system turns in the middle of a conversation are folded into the top-level system prompt. xAI otherwise answers “Invalid request content: Invalid message role.”
- **A tool choice with no tools..** A request that sets `tool_choice` but offers no tools, such as Codex’s compaction summary, goes without it. xAI otherwise answers “A tool_choice was set on the request but no tools were specified”.
- **Codex’s added tools..** xAI’s Responses API doesn’t know Codex’s `additional_tools` items, so jianmu puts their tools in the request’s `tools`.
- **Whole numbers..** Grok writes whole numbers in tool-call arguments with a fraction, such as `2500.0`, which Codex’s whole-number fields refuse. jianmu writes `2500`, in streamed replies too.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** The effort an agent asks for is fitted to the nearest level the model has, as the catalog lists them. A model whose levels aren’t known is asked as the agent asked.
- **Reasoning off..** When an agent whose requests jianmu translates, such as Gemini CLI, turns reasoning off and the model lists `none` among its levels, jianmu asks for none.
- **Switching models mid-conversation..** xAI reads only the sealed reasoning it wrote itself. When a Codex conversation moves to Grok from GPT or from another account, xAI answers “Could not decrypt the provided encrypted_content”. jianmu asks again without those items at once, and leaves them out for the rest of that conversation.

## Web search

- **Codex..** xAI runs web search itself on its Responses API, so Codex’s `web_search` is done by xAI.
- **Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode..** xAI’s Messages and Chat Completions APIs don’t search, so jianmu gives the model its own search tool, answered by the searcher chosen in Settings, or by one jianmu picks when none is chosen.
- **xAI as the searcher..** Because xAI searches by itself, jianmu can pick an xAI key to search for models that can’t.

## Cache, cost and usage

- **Cache tokens..** jianmu reads the cached tokens xAI reports in each reply, so the Usage tab counts cache hits apart from the rest of the prompt.
- **Keeping the cache..** With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is worth keeping, 1,024 tokens or more, and still warm, read within the last five minutes, so a turn isn’t sent to a key with a cold cache.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each Grok call with xAI’s prices from models.dev.
- **Balance..** jianmu reads no balance from xAI. Type it in yourself with `key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what jianmu has priced the key’s calls at since.

## Several keys and failover

One xAI provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when xAI is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.
- **A request xAI can’t read..** When xAI answers 422 “Failed to deserialize the JSON body … unknown item type”, the request goes to the next member of the routing group, and the key isn’t rested for it.

```
jianmu provider spend-cap xai <key> 20 month
jianmu provider key-balance xai <key> 25
jianmu provider fallback xai deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## Troubleshooting

- **“maximum prompt length is …”..** The conversation is longer than the model takes. jianmu tells the agent so the way it understands, `context_length_exceeded` or Anthropic’s “prompt is too long”, so the agent compacts and tries again.
- **“Could not decrypt the provided encrypted_content”..** Codex moved to Grok mid-conversation with another vendor’s reasoning in it. jianmu asks again without it; see Reasoning.
- **“unknown variant `custom`”..** xAI turned away Codex’s custom tools. jianmu translates that model’s Codex requests from then on; the first refusal is the last.
- **Checking a key..** `jianmu provider test xai` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use Grok in Claude Code?

Add your xAI API key in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, xAI), then pick a Grok model such as `grok-4.7` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude xai/grok-4.7`. Claude Code’s requests go through jianmu’s gateway to xAI’s Anthropic Messages endpoint, `https://api.x.ai`.

### Can Codex use Grok 4?

Yes. xAI serves the Responses API that Codex speaks, so `jianmu codex xai/grok-4.7` sends Codex’s requests to `https://api.x.ai/v1` as they are, with what xAI would refuse fixed on the way: tool schemas, a tool choice with no tools, and whole numbers Grok writes as `2500.0`.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use Grok?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s API, so jianmu translates its requests to xAI’s Chat Completions and the replies back. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to xAI as they are. Run `jianmu gemini model xai/grok-4.7` or `jianmu opencode xai/grok-4.7`.

### Does web search work with Grok?

Yes. Codex’s web search is run by xAI itself on its Responses API. For Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, jianmu gives the model its own search tool, answered by the searcher chosen in Settings, or by one jianmu picks.

### Why did Codex fail after switching from GPT to Grok mid-conversation?

xAI can’t read reasoning that another vendor sealed, and answers “Could not decrypt the provided encrypted_content”. jianmu asks again without those items and leaves them out for the rest of the conversation.

### Does jianmu show my xAI balance?

No. The Usage tab counts tokens, cache and cost for every Grok call, priced from models.dev, but jianmu reads no balance from xAI. You can type the balance in with `jianmu provider key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what jianmu has priced since.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini) · [Mistral](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mistral

# Mistral in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Mistral serves its models on one API, OpenAI-style Chat Completions, at `api.mistral.ai`. Add a Mistral API key to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Mistral through jianmu’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own. Agents that speak another API are translated on the way.

## Add Mistral

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [console.mistral.ai](https://console.mistral.ai/api-keys). A Le Chat plan’s Vibe key goes in the same provider.
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Mistral, paste the key and save. jianmu asks Mistral which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Mistral model such as `mistral-large-4`.

```
jianmu provider add mistral <key>
jianmu provider test mistral
```

Model ids in jianmu are `provider/model`, so Mistral’s read `mistral/mistral-large-4`: the provider, then Mistral’s own id. The key is kept in jianmu’s settings; jianmu doesn’t take it from your shell.

Already set Mistral up in OpenCode or Alma? jianmu’s import from those apps brings it in as the Mistral provider. An app that keeps one entry per key (“Mistral #0001”, “Mistral #0002”…) becomes one Mistral provider with that many keys, listed once in every agent’s picker.

## Endpoints

| API | Address | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | the model list and every agent’s requests: OpenCode’s as they are, Claude Code’s, Codex’s and Gemini CLI’s translated |
| Billing | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/billing/budget`, `/v1/billing/subscription` | a key’s month of Vibe or API budget, and the plan it is on |

jianmu’s Mistral provider has no Anthropic Messages or Responses address, so an agent that speaks either is translated to Chat Completions and the reply translated back, streaming and tool calls included.

## Model list

jianmu fetches the list from Mistral, at `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/models`, so agents see the models your key can use. Names, reasoning levels and prices come from models.dev’s `mistral` catalog, and Devstral, Codestral and Magistral models carry Mistral’s logo in every picker. Mistral also serves models from other labs, such as GLM and DeepSeek’s `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`; they come through the same key, and the fixes below apply to them too. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
jianmu provider models mistral +mistral-large-4 +mistral-medium-3.5
jianmu provider refresh-every mistral 1d
```

## In each agent

```
jianmu claude mistral/mistral-large-4
jianmu codex mistral/mistral-large-4
jianmu gemini model mistral/mistral-large-4
jianmu opencode mistral/mistral-large-4
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, which Mistral doesn’t serve. jianmu translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back; a reasoning model’s thinking reaches Claude Code as thinking, then the text. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which Mistral doesn’t serve either, so its requests are translated too. Codex’s custom tools, such as `apply_patch`, are offered to the model as functions, and its calls come back as the custom tool calls Codex runs. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API. jianmu translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Mistral as they are, with the fixes below. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## What jianmu fixes for Mistral

Mistral’s API is strict about what it takes and sends a reasoning model’s thinking in a shape of its own. jianmu changes both on the way, on requests it passes on and on those it translates alike:

- **Thinking in typed parts..** Mistral sends a reasoning model’s thinking as typed parts in `content`, thinking and text sometimes in one chunk, where the Chat contract has a string. OpenCode turned the first such chunk away (“Invalid … stream event”). jianmu moves the thinking to `reasoning_content` and the text to a plain string, streamed or not.
- **Thinking sent back..** OpenCode sends an earlier turn’s thinking back in `reasoning_content`, which Mistral refuses with 422 `extra_forbidden`. jianmu puts it in the thinking part Mistral itself returns, ahead of the turn’s text, so the thinking stays in context. Translated requests get the same, so a Codex tool loop keeps going on a DeepSeek model served by Mistral.
- **Fields Mistral doesn’t know..** OpenCode’s `store` and Kimi Code’s thinking switch got 422 `extra_forbidden`. jianmu asks again without the optional fields Mistral named, and doesn’t send them to it again once that works.
- **Ollama options..** An agent that took the gateway for an Ollama server, such as Hermes Agent, sends Ollama’s `options` (its `num_ctx`) beside the Chat fields. jianmu leaves them out, so Mistral never sees them.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** The effort an agent asks for is fitted to the nearest level the model has, as the catalog lists them. A model whose levels aren’t known is asked as the agent asked.
- **Reasoning off..** When an agent whose requests jianmu translates, such as Gemini CLI, turns reasoning off and the model lists `none` among its levels, jianmu asks for none.
- **Thinking across turns..** Each agent sees a reasoning model’s thinking in its own shape: `reasoning_content` for OpenCode, thinking blocks for Claude Code, reasoning for Codex. When it comes back in a later turn, Mistral gets it as a thinking part; see What jianmu fixes.

## Web search

Mistral’s Chat Completions API doesn’t search the web for jianmu, so jianmu gives the model its own search tool in every agent, answered by the searcher chosen in Settings, or by one jianmu picks when none is chosen.

## Vibe, cost and usage

- **Vibe month..** A Le Chat plan (Pro, Student or Team) comes with a month of Mistral Vibe. Its Vibe key’s row shows how much of the month’s budget is used, in the currency Mistral bills in, when it resets, and the plan’s name.
- **API month..** A Studio key made in the console shows the organization’s API budget, as “API · Month”, apart from a Vibe month. The budget is the organization’s, so every key of one organization shows the same numbers. A key with no budget has no card.
- **Pay as you go..** With pay-as-you-go on, what goes past the budget is billed rather than stopped, so a used-up month doesn’t stop the key’s models.
- **Cache tokens..** When a reply reports cached prompt tokens, the Usage tab counts them apart from the rest of the prompt.
- **Keeping the cache..** With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is worth keeping, 1,024 tokens or more, and still warm, read within the last five minutes.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call with Mistral’s prices from models.dev. jianmu reads no balance from Mistral; type it in with `key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what jianmu has priced the key’s calls at since.

## Several keys and failover

One Mistral provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when Mistral is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.

```
jianmu provider spend-cap mistral <key> 20 month
jianmu provider key-balance mistral <key> 25
jianmu provider fallback mistral deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## Troubleshooting

- **422 `extra_forbidden`, “Extra inputs are not permitted”..** Mistral turned away a field it doesn’t know. jianmu fixes the ones agents are known to send and asks again without an optional field Mistral names; see What jianmu fixes.
- **“Invalid … stream event” in OpenCode..** That was Mistral’s thinking in typed parts. jianmu sends OpenCode the thinking in `reasoning_content` and the text as a string.
- **No Vibe card..** jianmu shows the month only for a key Mistral says is a Vibe key or a Studio key, and only when its budget is more than zero.
- **Checking a key..** `jianmu provider test mistral` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use Mistral in Claude Code?

Add your Mistral API key in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, Mistral), then pick a Mistral model such as `mistral-large-4` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude mistral/mistral-large-4`. Mistral serves Chat Completions only, so jianmu translates Claude Code’s Anthropic Messages requests to `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` and the replies back, thinking included.

### Can Codex use Devstral and other Mistral models?

Yes. Codex can use any model your Mistral key lists, Devstral among them. Codex speaks OpenAI Responses, which Mistral doesn’t serve, so jianmu translates each request to Chat Completions, offers Codex’s custom tools such as apply_patch as functions, and gives the calls back the way Codex runs them.

### How do I use Codestral or other Mistral models in OpenCode?

Pick the model in jianmu, or run `jianmu opencode mistral/mistral-large-4`; Codestral and Devstral work the same way when your key lists them. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Mistral as they are, with what Mistral would refuse fixed on the way: OpenCode’s `store` field, and earlier turns’ thinking sent back in `reasoning_content`.

### Can Gemini CLI use Mistral?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s Gemini API, so jianmu translates its requests to Mistral’s Chat Completions and the replies back, streaming and tool calls included. Run `jianmu gemini model mistral/mistral-large-4`.

### Why does Mistral answer 422 extra_forbidden?

Mistral turns away any field it doesn’t know. jianmu sends an earlier turn’s thinking as the thinking part Mistral takes, leaves out Ollama options some agents add, and asks again without an optional field Mistral names, such as OpenCode’s `store`, then stops sending it.

### Does jianmu show my Le Chat plan’s Vibe budget?

Yes. A Vibe key from a Le Chat plan (Pro, Student or Team) shows how much of the month’s Vibe budget is used, in the currency Mistral bills in, and when it resets, with the plan’s name. A Studio key made in the console shows the organization’s API budget instead, as “API · Month”.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok) · [OpenRouter](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ollama)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ollama

# Ollama in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Ollama serves the models you pull on two APIs, OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages, at `http://localhost:11434`. Ollama Cloud serves its models the same way at `ollama.com`, with an API key. Add either to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use them through jianmu’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own.

## Add Ollama

1. **Pull a model.** Pull a model in Ollama, such as `qwen3`, and leave the server running.
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider and pick Ollama under On this machine. No key is needed. jianmu asks the server which models it has, and they show as `ollama/…`.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose an Ollama model.

```
ollama pull qwen3
jianmu provider add ollama
jianmu provider test ollama
```

Model ids in jianmu are `provider/model`, so a model you pulled as `qwen3` reads `ollama/qwen3`. A tag stays in the id, as in `ollama/qwen3:8b`. In the terminal UI, jianmu asks for the server’s address when you add it. LM Studio, oMLX, vLLM and llama.cpp’s server are in [Local models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/local-models).

## Another port or another computer

If Ollama listens on another port, or runs on another computer such as a GPU box or a NAS, change Server address in the provider’s editor. Only the scheme, host and port change; each API keeps its path. The scheme can be left out, and `http` is taken; a path pasted with the address, such as `/v1`, is dropped.

```
jianmu provider set ollama address=192.168.1.20:11434
jianmu provider set ollama address=     # back to the default
```

- **Proxies..** A server on your own network is reached directly, whatever proxy Settings or the system name. A proxy you set on the provider itself is still used.
- **HTTPS..** An Ollama behind HTTPS with a self-signed certificate can be reached with Don't check its certificate in the editor. It applies to that provider’s own hosts only.

## Ollama Cloud

1. **Get a key.** Make one at [ollama.com/settings/keys](https://ollama.com/settings/keys).
2. **Add the provider.** In the Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Ollama Cloud, paste the key and save. jianmu asks Ollama Cloud which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** Choose an Ollama Cloud model, such as `deepseek-v4-pro`, on the agent’s row.

```
jianmu provider add ollama-cloud <key>
jianmu claude ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4-pro
```

Names, reasoning levels and prices come from models.dev’s `ollama-cloud` catalog. The key is kept in jianmu’s settings.

## Endpoints

| Provider | Chat Completions | Anthropic Messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ollama | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `http://localhost:11434` |
| Ollama Cloud | `https://ollama.com/v1` | `https://ollama.com` |

An agent whose API Ollama serves is passed on to that API. jianmu uses no Responses endpoint for either, so when it has to translate, it uses Chat Completions: it keeps Responses first only for OpenAI’s own models, and Messages first only for Claude models.

## Model list

jianmu asks the server for its list at the Chat Completions base: `http://localhost:11434/v1/models`, or `https://ollama.com/v1/models` for Ollama Cloud. A model shows in jianmu once Ollama has it. After you pull another, press Fetch models in the provider’s editor, or run `jianmu provider refresh ollama`. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
jianmu provider refresh ollama
jianmu provider models ollama +qwen3
```

Ollama 0.35.0 and later (0.40.5 for its cloud models) also serves decision models, such as Nimble, Clef and Tev. jianmu reads Ollama’s `/api/tags` as well, and a model marked there as a decision model becomes one of the provider’s decision models for [intent routing](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/intent), never an agent’s model. An older Ollama lists none.

## In each agent

```
jianmu claude ollama/qwen3
jianmu codex ollama/qwen3
jianmu gemini model ollama/qwen3
jianmu opencode ollama/qwen3
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, and so does Ollama at `http://localhost:11434`, so its requests go there as they are. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which jianmu doesn’t send to Ollama. jianmu turns each request into Chat Completions and the reply back, streaming and tool calls included. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API. jianmu translates each request to Chat Completions and the reply back. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Ollama’s `/v1` as they are. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

Inside the agent, Claude Code’s and Codex’s `/model` list jianmu’s models too, so you can move between a local model and a cloud one there. To go back to the agent’s own models, run `jianmu claude default` or `jianmu codex default`.

## Context window and num_ctx

Agents plan around how long a request the model takes. Claude Code takes a model it doesn’t know for 200K, and Codex compacts a conversation at 90% of the window it is told. jianmu doesn’t read an Ollama chat model’s window, so tell it the real one: Context window under Advanced in the provider’s editor, for every model or one of them. jianmu passes it on to the agents.

```
jianmu provider set ollama context=32k
jianmu provider set ollama context.qwen3=128k
```

- **`num_ctx`..** Some clients send Ollama’s per-request options, such as `{"num_ctx": …}`, beside the Chat Completions fields. jianmu leaves them out of every request it sends on: no Chat Completions API reads them, Ollama’s own `/v1` included. The window the model runs with is Ollama’s to set; give jianmu the same number.
- **Too long..** When a conversation outgrows the window, Ollama answers “exceeded max context length”. jianmu tells the agent so the way it understands, `context_length_exceeded` or Anthropic’s “prompt is too long”, so the agent compacts and tries again.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** The effort an agent asks for is fitted to the nearest level the model has, as the catalog lists them. A model whose levels jianmu doesn’t know is asked as the agent asked.
- **Reasoning off..** When an agent whose requests jianmu translates, such as Codex or Gemini CLI, turns reasoning off and the model lists `none` among its levels, jianmu asks for none.
- **Your own levels..** `jianmu model efforts` offers only the levels you name, or sends a model no reasoning field at all.

```
jianmu model efforts ollama/qwen3 low,medium,high
jianmu model efforts ollama/qwen3 off
```

## Tool calls

Claude Code’s and OpenCode’s tool calls reach Ollama as the agent wrote them. For Codex and Gemini CLI, jianmu translates the tools, the model’s calls and their results to Chat Completions and back, in streamed replies too.

## Privacy masking

jianmu’s [privacy masking](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/masking) replaces keys, tokens and other secrets with placeholders before a request leaves the gateway, a request to a local Ollama too. When the model runs on your own computer or network, you can turn on Send requests unmasked in its editor, or run `jianmu provider set ollama unmasked=yes`.

- **Cloud models..** Ollama’s cloud models pass a request on to a vendor whatever the address, so it is your call. The editor warns you while it is on for a provider that isn’t local, such as Ollama Cloud.
- **Tool arguments..** In a request in Ollama’s own format, a tool call’s arguments are masked as tool arguments, as in every other API.
- **Anonymous stats..** jianmu’s daily stats name an Ollama model only when models.dev knows it; any other counts as “other”. See [Privacy](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/privacy).

## Usage and cost

- **Usage..** The Usage tab counts the tokens of every Ollama call. A model is priced at the price jianmu finds for its id, which for a local model can be its maker’s list price. To count a local model at nothing, give it your own price.
- **Free first..** `free=yes` counts every model of the provider as free, so a Free first routing spends it before paid ones. Prices and Usage’s costs stay as listed.
- **Ollama Cloud’s allowance..** jianmu reads the account’s balance from Ollama Cloud. The included allowance shows as a plan, in dollars used, with when it resets; an older plan shows its session and weekly limits instead. Credits you bought show as a balance. Past the allowance Ollama Cloud draws on those credits, so a spent allowance with credits left doesn’t stop the key.
- **Peak hours..** On Ollama Cloud, `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` (with their tags) cost double from 12:00 to 18:00 UTC, Monday to Friday. models.dev lists the off-peak price; the Usage tab doubles it in those hours, and a Cheapest first routing counts it.
- **Out of allowance..** When Ollama Cloud says a key is out without saying when it comes back, as its weekly limit does, jianmu rests the key for 15 minutes. `quota-rest` sets how long, up to 8 days. With several keys (Add another key) the next one takes over; when every key is out, the gateway answers at once with Retry-After.

```
jianmu model price ollama/qwen3 0,0,0,0
jianmu provider set ollama free=yes
jianmu provider quota-rest ollama-cloud 7d
jianmu provider fallback ollama-cloud ollama/qwen3
```

## jianmu as an Ollama server

Some apps take a custom model only as an Ollama server: VS Code’s Copilot Ollama provider, Visual Studio’s Copilot BYOK, Zed’s Ollama provider and the `ollama` CLI. Point them at jianmu’s gateway, `http://127.0.0.1:3425`, and they see jianmu’s models, from every provider, not only Ollama.

- **Routes..** jianmu answers `/api/version`, `/api/tags`, `/api/show`, `/api/chat` and `/api/generate`.
- **The same path..** A chat there is served as `/v1/chat/completions` is, so key limits, routing, fallbacks and usage are the same. A gateway key held to some models lists only those.
- **What it tells..** `/api/tags` and `/api/show` mark tools, vision when the model reads images, and thinking when it reasons. `/api/show` also gives the model’s window, or 32768 for one jianmu doesn’t know. The `ollama` CLI’s `name:latest` finds a model called `name`.

## Troubleshooting

- **A model you pulled isn’t listed..** The list comes from the server. Press Fetch models, or run `jianmu provider refresh ollama`, and pick it in the provider’s model list. Use the name Ollama lists, tag included.
- **Ollama isn’t running..** `jianmu provider test ollama` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name; add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would. Start Ollama, or check Server address. `fallback` names where requests go while it is down.
- **“exceeded max context length”..** The conversation is longer than the model was loaded for. Set the real Context window on the provider, and the agents compact before they reach it.
- **Another computer can’t be reached..** Check the address and port in Server address; for HTTPS with a self-signed certificate, turn on Don't check its certificate.

## FAQ

### How do I use Ollama in Claude Code?

Add Ollama in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, Ollama under On this machine), then pick one of its models on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude ollama/qwen3`. Claude Code’s requests go through jianmu’s gateway to Ollama’s Anthropic Messages API at `http://localhost:11434` as they are.

### Can Codex use Ollama?

Yes. Codex speaks only the Responses API, so jianmu turns its requests into Chat Completions for Ollama, and the replies back, tool calls included. Run `jianmu codex ollama/qwen3`.

### Can Gemini CLI and OpenCode use Ollama?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s API, so jianmu translates its requests to Ollama’s Chat Completions and the replies back. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions, so its requests go to Ollama as they are. Run `jianmu gemini model ollama/qwen3` or `jianmu opencode ollama/qwen3`.

### How do I run qwen3-coder from Ollama in Claude Code?

Pull it in Ollama, press Fetch models in the provider’s editor in jianmu (or run `jianmu provider refresh ollama`), and pick it on Claude Code’s row. Its id in jianmu is `ollama/` and the name Ollama lists it under, tag included. Set its Context window too: Claude Code takes a model it doesn’t know for 200K.

### Can jianmu use Ollama on another computer?

Yes. Set the provider’s Server address to that computer, such as `jianmu provider set ollama address=192.168.1.20:11434`. A server on your own network is reached directly, not through a proxy set in Settings or the system.

### Does jianmu work with Ollama Cloud?

Yes. Add Ollama Cloud with a key from `ollama.com/settings/keys`. jianmu lists the models the key can use, prices them from models.dev, and shows the account’s included allowance and the credits you bought.

### Do I need an API key for a local Ollama?

No. The Ollama preset takes none. Ollama Cloud needs one.

Other local servers, such as LM Studio, oMLX, vLLM and llama.cpp’s server, are in [Local models](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/local-models). To let a local model classify each request for routing, see [Intent routing](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/intent).

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax) · [Anthropic](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/anthropic) · [OpenAI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot)

Every agent: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models). Ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues) if you get stuck.

# Anthropic in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

Anthropic serves Claude on its Messages API, at `api.anthropic.com`. Add an Anthropic API key to jianmu once, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and every other agent you connect can use Claude models through jianmu’s local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425`, each agent with a model of its own. Agents that speak another API are translated on the way.

## Add Anthropic

1. **Get a key.** Make one on [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys). An API key starts with `sk-ant-api`.
2. **Add the provider.** In jianmu’s Providers tab, press ＋ Add provider, pick Anthropic, paste the key and save. jianmu asks Anthropic which models the key can use.
3. **Pick it for an agent.** In the Agents tab, click the model on the agent’s row and choose a Claude model such as `claude-opus-5-5`.

```
jianmu provider add anthropic <key>
jianmu provider test anthropic
```

Model ids in jianmu are `provider/model`, so Anthropic’s read `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`: the provider, then Anthropic’s own id. The key is kept in jianmu’s settings; jianmu doesn’t take it from your shell.

Already set Anthropic up in OpenCode or Alma? jianmu’s import from those apps brings it in as the Anthropic provider.

This page is about an API key. A Claude Pro or Max subscription is signed in to separately; see [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/subscriptions).

## Endpoints

| API | Address | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Messages | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` | every agent’s requests: Claude Code’s as sent, Codex’s, Gemini CLI’s and OpenCode’s translated |
| Models | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models` | the model list |

jianmu’s Anthropic provider has no Chat Completions or Responses address, so an agent that speaks either, or Google’s Gemini API, is translated to Messages and the reply translated back, streaming and tool calls included.

## Model list

jianmu fetches the list from Anthropic, at `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models`, every page of it, so agents see the models your key can use. Names, context windows and prices come from models.dev’s `anthropic` catalog. Pick the models agents see in the provider’s model list, or from the terminal:

```
jianmu provider models anthropic +claude-opus-5-5 +claude-sonnet-5-5 +claude-haiku-5-5
jianmu provider refresh-every anthropic 1d
```

Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 take 1M tokens. On a window that long, Codex compacts a conversation at 272K rather than send ever more of it on every turn; `jianmu model compact off` lets it run to the whole window. In Claude Code a Claude model runs to its own window, as Anthropic runs it: 200K unless a `[1m]` one is picked.

## In each agent

```
jianmu claude anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
jianmu codex anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
jianmu gemini model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
jianmu opencode anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
```

- **Claude Code.** speaks Anthropic Messages, so its requests go to Anthropic as Claude Code sent them, its own cache marks, thinking and betas included, with the fixes below. [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models).
- **Codex.** speaks OpenAI Responses, which Anthropic doesn’t serve. jianmu translates each request to Messages and the reply back, marks the prompt for Anthropic’s cache, and keeps Claude’s signed thinking across a tool loop. [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models).
- **Gemini CLI.** speaks Google’s Gemini API. jianmu translates each request to Messages and the reply back. [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models).
- **OpenCode.** speaks Chat Completions to jianmu, so its requests are translated to Messages too. [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models).

## What jianmu does for Anthropic

A request jianmu translates is built the way Anthropic’s Messages API wants it, and a few things Anthropic would refuse are fixed on Claude Code’s requests too:

- **Prompt caching..** Anthropic caches a prompt only up to a block marked with `cache_control`, and a request from another API has no marks. jianmu marks the system prompt (or the last tool, when there is no system prompt) and the conversation’s last block, two marks at most, so the next turn reads what came before from the cache. A request that brings `cache_control` of its own keeps its marks, and jianmu adds none.
- **An hour’s cache for Codex..** Codex’s turns are often more than five minutes apart, so the marks jianmu adds to its requests last an hour, unless Codex asks `prompt_cache_retention` `in_memory`. An upstream that turns the hour’s `ttl` away is asked again with five-minute marks, and jianmu remembers it.
- **Signed thinking..** Claude signs its thinking and wants it back on a tool loop’s next turn. Codex gets each thinking block, signature included, in its reasoning item’s `encrypted_content`, and jianmu sends it back to Anthropic as it was; redacted thinking goes back sealed. Thinking with no signature is left out, and so is thinking another vendor signed, such as DeepSeek’s earlier in a routing group, which Claude refuses.
- **Tool calls..** A call an interrupted turn left unanswered gets a result saying it is unavailable, and a result for a call Anthropic never saw becomes text, where Anthropic would refuse the request. A history with calls but no tools declared declares them, with `tool_choice` none. A required tool goes as `any`, a named one as `tool`, and parallel calls turned off as `disable_parallel_tool_use`.
- **Sampling..** Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5 refuse `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k`, which Claude Code’s auto mode classifier sends. jianmu leaves them out for those models.
- **Betas..** The betas an agent asks in `anthropic-beta` go on to Anthropic, save Claude Code’s own sign-in beta (`oauth-…`), which names a credential that never leaves jianmu.
- **Structured output..** A request for JSON in a schema goes to Anthropic as `output_config.format`.

## Reasoning

- **Effort..** Claude models from 4.6 on think adaptively. A translated request’s effort goes as `output_config.effort`, with thinking adaptive and its summary shown (`display: summarized`), since Opus 4.7 and later leave the thinking text out unless asked. Opus and Sonnet 4.6 have no xhigh, so xhigh is asked as max.
- **Budgets..** Older Claude models get a thinking budget: 4,096 tokens at low, 10,000 at medium, 24,000 at high, 32,000 at xhigh and max, fitted under the request’s `max_tokens`.
- **A budget to a newer model..** A request with a thinking budget to a model from 4.6 on, which Claude Opus 5.5 refuses (“requires adaptive thinking”), goes as adaptive thinking, the budget asked as the nearest effort.
- **Reasoning off..** Codex’s or a Chat client’s effort none turns thinking off, not down to a low budget. Each model takes off its own way: Sonnet 5.5 is sent `between_tools`, an effort above high asked as high; Opus 5.5 and Fable 5 always think, so thinking is left out; Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5 are asked high in place of xhigh or max; older Claudes take it as sent. Claude Code’s requests with thinking off are fitted the same way.

## Web search

Anthropic searches the web itself. Claude Code’s WebSearch goes to Anthropic as it is. When Codex, Gemini CLI or a Chat client asks to search, jianmu offers Claude Anthropic’s own `web_search_20250305` tool, up to five searches a request, rather than jianmu’s searcher.

## Cost and usage

- **Cache tokens..** The Usage tab counts cache reads, five-minute cache writes and hour-long cache writes apart from the rest of the prompt, as Anthropic reports them.
- **Cost..** The Usage tab prices each call with Anthropic’s prices from models.dev. An hour-long write is priced at twice the input price where the catalog gives none, as Anthropic bills it. jianmu reads no balance from Anthropic; type it in with `key-balance`, and the Usage page shows it less what jianmu has priced the key’s calls at since.
- **Keeping the cache..** With several keys, a conversation stays on its key while its cache is worth keeping, 1,024 tokens or more, and still warm: read within the last five minutes, or within the hour when it was written for an hour.

## Several keys and failover

One Anthropic provider can hold several keys: press Add another key under it, or paste several at once. Requests go to the first key that’s on, and when it runs out or is rate limited the next one takes over.

- **Spend caps..** `spend-cap` stops a key at a dollar amount a day, a month or in all, as the Usage tab prices its calls; routing then goes on to the other keys and the fallbacks.
- **Fallbacks..** `fallback` names where requests go when Anthropic is out of quota or down: another provider’s model or a routing group.
- **Workspaces..** A key that reaches several workspaces names the one each request is for with the `anthropic-workspace-id` header. Add the provider again under an id of its own, with the header set in its Headers field or from the terminal; its models then read `anthropic-ws2/…`.

```
jianmu provider spend-cap anthropic <key> 20 month
jianmu provider key-balance anthropic <key> 25
jianmu provider fallback anthropic deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
jianmu provider add anthropic <key> id=anthropic-ws2 name="Anthropic WS2" header.anthropic-workspace-id=wrkspc_…
```

## Troubleshooting

- **“requires adaptive thinking”..** A thinking budget sent to a model from 4.6 on. jianmu sends it as adaptive thinking with the nearest effort; see Reasoning.
- **400 when thinking is turned off..** Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5 each refuse `disabled`, and Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5 refuse it at xhigh and max. jianmu sends each model off the way it takes it.
- **“`temperature` is deprecated for this model”..** jianmu leaves `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` out for the models that refuse them.
- **“`tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks”..** An interrupted turn left a call unanswered. In a request jianmu translates, the call gets a result saying it is unavailable.
- **“Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block”..** The conversation ran on another vendor first. jianmu leaves thinking another vendor signed, or left unsigned, out of what goes to Claude.
- **A 400 about `cache_control` and `ttl`..** The upstream doesn’t take the hour-long marks jianmu adds for Codex. jianmu asks again with five-minute marks and keeps to them for that provider.
- **“this is an Anthropic API key, not a setup-token”..** The key went to the Claude subscription’s sign-in. Add it as the Anthropic provider instead.
- **Checking a key..** `jianmu provider test anthropic` sends a tiny request through each endpoint, or to each model you name. Add `--as codex` or `--as claude-code` to send it the way that agent would.

## FAQ

### How do I use an Anthropic API key in Claude Code?

Add your Anthropic API key in jianmu (Providers, Add provider, Anthropic), then pick a Claude model such as `claude-opus-5-5` on Claude Code’s row, or run `jianmu claude anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. Claude Code speaks Anthropic Messages, so its requests go to `https://api.anthropic.com` as it sent them, with what the model would refuse fixed on the way.

### Can Codex use Claude models?

Yes. Codex speaks OpenAI Responses, which Anthropic doesn’t serve, so jianmu translates each request to the Messages API and the reply back. It marks the prompt for Anthropic’s cache with marks that last an hour, and keeps Claude’s signed thinking across a tool loop in Codex’s `encrypted_content`. Run `jianmu codex anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.

### How do I use Claude in OpenCode through jianmu?

Pick the model in jianmu, or run `jianmu opencode anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`. OpenCode speaks Chat Completions to jianmu, so jianmu translates its requests to Anthropic’s Messages API, marks the prompt for the cache and fits the reasoning effort to the model.

### Can Gemini CLI use Claude?

Yes. Gemini CLI speaks Google’s Gemini API, so jianmu translates its requests to Anthropic’s Messages API and the replies back, streaming and tool calls included. Run `jianmu gemini model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`.

### Does jianmu keep Anthropic’s prompt cache for agents it translates?

Yes. A request from Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode has no cache marks of its own, so jianmu marks the system prompt and the conversation’s last block, two marks at most, and the next turn reads what came before from the cache. A request that brings its own `cache_control` keeps its marks. Codex’s marks last an hour, the rest five minutes.

### Why does Claude answer 400 when thinking is turned off?

Newer Claude models don’t all take `thinking` `disabled`. jianmu sends Sonnet 5.5 `between_tools`, leaves thinking out for Opus 5.5 and Fable 5, which always think, and asks Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5 at high in place of xhigh or max. Older Claudes get it as sent.

**By provider:** [DeepSeek](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/deepseek) · [Kimi and Kimi Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi) · [GLM Coding Plan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/glm) · [Volcengine Ark](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/volcengine) · [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud) · [Baidu Qianfan](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/baidu-qianfan) · [SiliconFlow](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/siliconflow) · [ModelScope](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/modelscope) · [Huawei Cloud MaaS](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/huaweicloud) · [Xiaomi MiMo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/xiaomi-mimo) · [StepFun](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepfun) · [LongCat](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/longcat) · [Qwen](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen) · [MiniMax](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/minimax) · [OpenAI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openai) · [Gemini](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini) · [Grok](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok) · [Mistral](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mistral) · [OpenRouter](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openrouter) · [GitHub Copilot](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot) · [Ollama](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ollama)
