Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/crush

# Crush on any model

Crush, Charm’s coding agent for the terminal, runs on the providers in its config. jianmu adds itself to Crush as a provider, so Crush can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, with no key pasted into Crush.

Crush’s config is `~/.config/crush/crush.json` (under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` if set; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\crush` on Windows). jianmu adds `providers.jianmu` there, with the gateway’s address, a key of Crush’s own and jianmu’s models, and sets the models Crush runs on. The gateway translates each request for the model’s provider, tool calls and reasoning included. A Crush in WSL is set up the same way, reaching the gateway as the distro sees it.

## Connect Crush

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Crush’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose Crush’s large model, and its small one if you like.
3. **Start crush.** jianmu’s models are in Crush’s own model picker too, under jianmu.

```
jianmu crush deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro     # Crush's large model on DeepSeek
jianmu crush small deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
jianmu crush                              # what Crush runs on now
```

## Large, small and effort

Crush has two model slots: `large` for the work and `small` for lighter tasks. Each can be any model, jianmu’s or one of your own providers’. The row also sets the large model’s `reasoning_effort`: low, medium or high.

```
jianmu crush effort high
jianmu crush effort default    # back to Crush's own
```

## The two files

Crush saves the models its own picker chooses to a data file, `~/.local/share/crush/crush.json` (under `$XDG_DATA_HOME` if set), which wins over the config. So jianmu writes the picks there too, where Crush writes them, and its provider stays in the config. When jianmu picks a model, settings Crush’s picker saved for the previous model, such as its `max_tokens`, are dropped, so a limit meant for one model doesn’t reach another. Keys you added to jianmu’s provider yourself stay when jianmu rewrites the models.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own providers’ models for both slots, take the row off jianmu, or run `jianmu crush default`. Once neither slot uses a model of jianmu’s, jianmu removes its provider from crush.json.

## FAQ

### Can Crush use my ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in jianmu and pick a GPT model on Crush’s row. Crush sends its requests to jianmu, which uses the subscription.

### Which wins, a pick in jianmu or one in Crush?

The latest. Both are saved to Crush’s data file, so the last model picked, on Crush’s row or in Crush’s own picker, is the one Crush uses.

### What is Crush’s small model for?

Lighter tasks next to the main work. Set it on Crush’s row as small, to any model.

### Does it work with Crush in WSL?

Yes. jianmu sets up a Crush in a WSL distro too, with the gateway’s address as the distro reaches it.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Zed on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/zed), [Raycast on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/raycast) and [jcode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/jcode). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/raycast

# Raycast on any model

Raycast AI takes models of your own as custom providers (Raycast Pro, on Mac and Windows). jianmu adds itself to Raycast as one, so Quick AI, AI Chat and AI Commands can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, with no key pasted into Raycast.

Raycast reads its custom providers from `~/.config/raycast/ai/providers.yaml` in your user folder, on Mac and on Windows. jianmu adds one entry to its `providers` list, with the id `jianmu`: the gateway’s OpenAI-compatible address, a key of Raycast’s own and jianmu’s models. Raycast watches the file, so the models show up without a restart. The gateway translates each request for the model’s provider, tool calls and reasoning included.

## Connect Raycast

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Put jianmu on Raycast’s row.** In the Agents tab, set Raycast’s provider to jianmu.
3. **Pick a model in Raycast.** Open Raycast’s model picker in Quick AI, AI Chat or an AI Command. jianmu’s models are listed under jianmu.

```
jianmu raycast jianmu     # jianmu's models in Raycast AI's picker
jianmu raycast            # what Raycast is set to now
```

On Windows, Raycast makes its config folder when you open Reveal Providers Config in its settings; jianmu finds Raycast by that folder there.

## Which models it lists

The model is picked in Raycast, not in a file, so Raycast’s picker lists the models picked for Raycast on the Agents page. Hide one there and it leaves Raycast’s list. Each model comes with its name, context window and abilities, all spelled out, because Raycast assumes tools and vision off when they aren’t:

- **Tools.** on for every model, so AI Extensions work.
- **Vision.** on for a model that takes images.
- **Reasoning effort.** on for a model with effort levels.
- **Temperature.** off for a model that refuses it.

## Your providers.yaml

jianmu writes only its own entry. Your other providers, the top-level `tools` block and your comments stay. So do keys you add to jianmu’s entry yourself, such as `include_user_email`, `additional_parameters` or a model’s `description`. The file is written only when jianmu’s entry would change.

## Switch back

Take Raycast’s row off jianmu, or run `jianmu raycast default`. jianmu removes its entry, the `providers` list too if it was the only one, and the file if nothing else is left in it.

## FAQ

### Do I need Raycast Pro?

Yes. Custom providers are a Raycast Pro feature, so jianmu’s models show in Raycast’s picker on a Pro plan.

### Can Raycast use my ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in jianmu and put jianmu on Raycast’s row, then pick a GPT model in Raycast. Raycast sends its requests to jianmu, which uses the subscription.

### Do I need to restart Raycast?

No. Raycast watches providers.yaml and picks up jianmu’s entry when it changes.

### Do AI Extensions work?

Yes. Every model is listed with tools on, and the gateway carries tool calls to each model’s provider.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Obsidian on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/obsidian), [Crush on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/crush) and [Copilot CLI on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot-cli). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot-cli

# Copilot CLI on any model

GitHub Copilot CLI can run on model providers of your own (bring your own key), which needs no GitHub sign-in. jianmu adds itself to Copilot CLI as one, so `copilot` can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI key, or a ChatGPT subscription, with no key pasted into Copilot.

Copilot CLI keeps its folder in `~/.copilot` (or `$COPILOT_HOME`). Its own providers are in `providers.json` there (or `$COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG`). jianmu adds a provider named `jianmu` to that file, OpenAI-compatible, with the gateway’s address and a key of Copilot’s own, and adds jianmu’s models beside it, each with its name, context window and output limit. Then it sets `model` in `settings.json` to `jianmu/<model>`. The gateway translates each request for the model’s provider, tool calls and reasoning included.

## Connect Copilot CLI

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Copilot CLI’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under jianmu.
3. **Start copilot.** It runs on that model. Copilot’s own `/model` lists jianmu’s models too.

```
jianmu copilot deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # settings.json: jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
jianmu copilot                             # what Copilot CLI runs on now
```

The row also lists Copilot’s own models and `auto`, Copilot’s own choice, for when you want GitHub’s models back.

## Effort

The row sets `effortLevel`, which Copilot saves beside the model: the model’s own levels, or low, medium, high and xhigh when Copilot’s list doesn’t name them. Copilot clears it when its own `/model` changes the model.

```
jianmu copilot effort high
jianmu copilot effort default
```

## Your providers.json

jianmu owns only the provider named jianmu and the models that name it. Your other providers, their models and any other key in the file stay where they are, and so does a key you add to jianmu’s provider yourself. A providers.json that isn’t valid JSON is left alone, never written over. When jianmu’s models change, jianmu brings its entries up to date, and writes the file only when they would change.

## Switch back

Pick one of Copilot’s own models on the row, or run `jianmu copilot default`. That removes `model` from settings.json and takes jianmu’s provider and models out of providers.json, leaving the rest.

## FAQ

### Do I need a GitHub Copilot subscription?

No. Copilot CLI’s own providers need no GitHub sign-in, so jianmu’s models work without a Copilot plan.

### Can Copilot CLI use my ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in jianmu and pick a GPT model under jianmu on Copilot CLI’s row. Copilot sends its requests to jianmu, which uses the subscription.

### Why does settings.json say jianmu/deepseek/…?

Copilot names a model of one of its providers as provider/model, and jianmu’s provider is called jianmu. On the command line you can leave the jianmu/ out.

### Can I keep my own BYOK providers?

Yes. jianmu only touches its own provider and models in providers.json; yours stay as they are.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Raycast on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/raycast) and [Qwen Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen-code). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen-code

# Qwen Code on any model

Qwen Code, the `qwen` coding agent from the Qwen team, takes models of your own in its settings. jianmu adds its models there, so qwen can run on any model you have in jianmu, not only Qwen: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, with no key pasted into qwen.

Qwen Code keeps its settings in `~/.qwen/settings.json` (under `$QWEN_HOME` if set). jianmu appends one entry per model to `modelProviders.openai` there, each with the gateway’s address, the model’s id, its name as qwen’s `/model` shows it, and its context window. Then it points `model` at your pick. The gateway translates each request for the model’s provider, tool calls and reasoning included. A Qwen Code in WSL is set up the same way.

## Connect Qwen Code

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Qwen Code’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under jianmu.
3. **Start a new qwen session.** Qwen Code reads a session’s model when it starts, so start a new session, or pick the model again with `/model`, where jianmu’s models are listed too.

```
jianmu qwen deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # Qwen Code on DeepSeek
jianmu qwen                             # what Qwen Code runs on now
```

## The key and /auth

Every jianmu entry takes its key from `JIANMU_QWEN_API_KEY`, which jianmu sets in the settings’ `env` object. The name is Qwen Code’s own, so a variable you exported in your shell or in `~/.qwen/.env` is unlikely to shadow it. jianmu also sets `security.auth.selectedType` to `openai`, so qwen starts without asking `/auth`.

## Your own models

Your own `modelProviders` entries stay as they were, in front of jianmu’s, so their ids don’t move, and they are listed on Qwen Code’s row beside jianmu’s. When you pick a model of jianmu’s, the model and auth type you had, with their address, are kept aside to be put back.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own models on the row, take the row off jianmu, or run `jianmu qwen default`. jianmu puts back the model and auth type you had before, and removes its entries and its key once no model of jianmu’s is in use.

## FAQ

### Can Qwen Code run on models other than Qwen?

Yes. Any model you have in jianmu is in qwen’s list: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, GPT, Claude and more.

### Can Qwen Code use my ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in jianmu and pick a GPT model under jianmu on Qwen Code’s row. qwen sends its requests to jianmu, which uses the subscription.

### Why doesn’t a running session change model?

Qwen Code reads a session’s model when the session starts. Start a new one, or pick the model with /model.

### Does it work with Qwen Code in WSL?

Yes. jianmu sets up a Qwen Code in a WSL distro too.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Copilot CLI on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/copilot-cli) and [Kimi Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi-code). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi-code

# Kimi Code on any model

Kimi Code, Moonshot’s `kimi` coding agent, takes providers and models of your own in its config. jianmu adds its models there, so kimi can run on any model you have in jianmu, not only Kimi: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, with no key pasted into kimi. For Kimi’s own models in other agents, see [Kimi in Claude Code, Codex and more](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi).

Kimi Code keeps its settings in `~/.kimi-code/config.toml` (`$KIMI_CODE_HOME`). jianmu adds a provider named `jianmu`, of Kimi’s own type, with the gateway’s address and a key of its own, then one `[models."jianmu/<provider>/<model>"]` table per model, so jianmu’s models join kimi’s `/model` picker. Then it sets `default_model` to your pick. Thinking travels both ways as `reasoning_content`, and the gateway translates each request for the model’s provider. The old Python `kimi-cli` is set up in `~/.kimi` (`$KIMI_SHARE_DIR`) only where there is no Kimi Code folder, since Kimi Code reads `~/.kimi-code` alone once it has taken over. A Kimi Code in WSL is set up the same way.

## Connect Kimi Code

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Kimi Code’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under jianmu.
3. **Use it in kimi.** Kimi Code picks the change up as it runs. Every model of jianmu’s is in `/model` too.

```
jianmu kimi deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # Kimi Code on DeepSeek
jianmu kimi                             # what Kimi Code runs on now
```

## What each model gets

- **Name and context.** The name kimi’s picker and status line show, and `max_context_size`, so kimi compacts in time.
- **Thinking levels.** A model with levels gets `thinking`, with `support_efforts` and a `default_effort` for Kimi Code’s thinking picker. A model that always thinks gets `always_thinking`.
- **Images and tools.** `image_in` for models that take images, `tool_use` on Kimi Code, and `max_output_size` where jianmu knows the model’s reply limit.

A value you set in one of jianmu’s tables yourself, such as a `default_effort`, stays there on the next sync.

## When it takes effect

Kimi Code 2.x watches its config, so an open session has the new models at once. In its web or desktop app, open Settings › Providers again, or reload the page, to see them in the picker. The old `kimi-cli` reads its config at start-up: restart open kimi sessions.

## Your own settings

Your Kimi Code sign-in, your own providers and models stay, and are listed on Kimi Code’s row beside jianmu’s. Keys you added to the `jianmu` provider table, such as `custom_headers` or `env`, stay too. The `default_model` you had is kept aside to be put back.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own models on the row, take the row off jianmu, or run `jianmu kimi default`. jianmu puts back the default model you had, if Kimi still has it, then removes its model tables and its provider.

## FAQ

### Can Kimi Code run on models other than Kimi?

Yes. Any model you have in jianmu is in kimi’s /model list: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Can Kimi Code use my ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in jianmu and pick a GPT model under jianmu on Kimi Code’s row. kimi sends its requests to jianmu, which uses the subscription.

### Does it work with the old Python kimi-cli?

Yes. Where there is no ~/.kimi-code, jianmu writes to kimi-cli’s ~/.kimi, without the keys only Kimi Code reads. Restart open sessions after a change.

### Does it work with Kimi Code in WSL?

Yes. jianmu sets up a Kimi Code in a WSL distro too, its provider pointing at the gateway as the distro reaches it.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Qwen Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen-code) and [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi

# Pi on any model

Pi, the `pi` coding agent, takes providers of your own in its `models.json`. jianmu adds itself there, so pi can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, with no key pasted into pi.

Pi keeps its settings in `~/.pi/agent`, or in the folder `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` names. jianmu adds a provider named `jianmu` to `models.json`, with the gateway’s address, a key of its own and the models you have in jianmu, so they join pi’s model picker. Then it sets `defaultProvider` and `defaultModel` in `settings.json` to your pick. A Pi in WSL is set up the same way.

## Connect Pi

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Pi’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under jianmu.
3. **Run pi.** It starts on that model, and every model of jianmu’s is in its model picker.

```
jianmu pi deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # Pi on DeepSeek
jianmu pi                             # what Pi runs on now
```

## What each model gets

- **Its own API.** Each model is asked on its provider’s native API: GPT and ChatGPT models on Responses, Claude on Messages, the rest on Chat Completions. A Claude model that thinks only adaptively gets `forceAdaptiveThinking`.
- **Name, context and replies.** The name pi shows, `reasoning` for models that think, `contextWindow`, image input where the model takes images, and `maxTokens`. A `maxTokens` you typed in yourself stays.
- **Thinking level.** The level you pick in jianmu goes in `defaultThinkingLevel`, held to the levels Pi offers.

Pi sends its session with each request (`sendSessionAffinityHeaders`), so jianmu’s usage shows each pi session and Record gateway conversations keeps them. A value you set there yourself stays.

## The Ctrl+P list

Pi cycles models with Ctrl+P through `enabledModels`, the list `/scoped-models` edits. If you have such a list, jianmu adds the model you picked to it. If you don’t, jianmu never makes one, so Ctrl+P keeps cycling every model.

## Decision and image models

jianmu also puts an extension, `extensions/jianmu.ts`, in Pi’s folder. It adds jianmu’s decision models and image models, for codemode. It is there while the `jianmu` provider is, and goes with it.

## Your own files

Before its first write, jianmu copies `settings.json` and `models.json` to `.before-jianmu` files beside them. Your own providers and settings stay as they are, and Pi’s row lists your models beside jianmu’s.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own models on the row, take the row off jianmu, or run `jianmu pi default`. If you changed nothing since, jianmu puts both files back byte for byte. Otherwise it removes only its own provider and keeps your changes.

## FAQ

### Can Pi run on DeepSeek or GLM?

Yes. Any model you have in jianmu is in pi’s model picker: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Can Pi use my ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Sign in to ChatGPT in jianmu and pick a GPT model under jianmu on Pi’s row. pi sends its requests to jianmu, which uses the subscription on the Responses API.

### Where does jianmu write if I set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR?

In that folder, with ~ expanded. A relative path is ignored, and jianmu uses ~/.pi/agent.

### Does it work with Pi in WSL?

Yes. jianmu sets up a Pi in a WSL distro too, its provider pointing at the gateway as the distro reaches it.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Kimi Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi-code), [Cursor Private Inference on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference) and [Prime Agent on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/prime-agent). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference

# Cursor Private Inference on any model

Cursor Private Inference is a build of Cursor whose agent runs on your own machine and asks a model endpoint of yours instead of Cursor’s backend. jianmu is such an endpoint, so its agent can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

The build takes its endpoint from `CURSOR_LOCAL_AGENT_BASE_URL` and `CURSOR_LOCAL_AGENT_API_KEY`. jianmu sets the two for your user, to the gateway’s `/v1` and a key of its own: through launchctl on the Mac, the registry’s Environment on Windows and environment.d on Linux. So the app has them when you open it from the Dock or the Start menu. jianmu writes none of Cursor’s files, since regular Cursor shares them, and only this build reads the two variables. jianmu finds the build by its `product.json`, in your apps folders, and on Linux as its AppImage where you downloaded it.

## Connect it

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick jianmu on its row.** In the Agents tab, set Cursor Private Inference’s provider to jianmu.
3. **Quit it and open it again.** Quit the app, not only its window, then open it. jianmu’s models are in its model picker.

To start it from a shell instead, the row gives the command that starts it with both variables set.

## Its models

Its model picker lists the gateway’s models, the ones its key is shown. The row’s Models button picks which. For each model the gateway also says which APIs it is served on and its limits, so the build asks Claude on Anthropic Messages, GPT on Responses and the rest on Chat, with the right context.

## Effort

Neither the build’s environment nor, for most models, its app says how hard a model should reason. Pick the effort on the row instead, among the levels its models have, and the gateway asks each request for it. Left on the default, requests go as the app sends them.

## When it takes effect

The build keeps the model list it was first given until it quits, so quit it and open it again after a change. On the Mac, launchctl’s variables are gone after a restart: jianmu sets them again when it starts, with the gateway’s address then, and the app takes them the next time it opens.

## Settings that come first

A base URL or API key set in the build’s Open configuration dialog, or in a model’s own settings, comes before the variables. Leave both empty, or set them to the gateway’s `/v1` address and the key the row shows.

## Switch back

Take the row off jianmu. jianmu clears both variables for your user. Quit the app and open it again.

## FAQ

### Can Cursor’s agent run on DeepSeek or GLM?

Yes, in Cursor Private Inference. Any model you have in jianmu can be in its model picker: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Does it change my regular Cursor?

No. jianmu writes none of Cursor’s settings. It sets two variables that only the Private Inference build reads.

### Why don’t the new models show?

The build keeps its first model list until it quits. Quit the app itself, not only its window, and open it again. Check that no base URL or key is set in its Open configuration.

### Does it work on Windows and Linux?

Yes. jianmu sets the variables in the registry’s Environment on Windows and in environment.d on Linux, and finds the Linux AppImage where you downloaded it.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi) and [Antigravity on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/antigravity). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/antigravity

# Antigravity on any model

Antigravity, Google’s agent app, can send its requests to a gateway of yours instead of Google, through its Enterprise Gateway setting. jianmu is such a gateway, so Antigravity and its CLI, `agy`, can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

Antigravity 2.15 and later reads a `gateway` block from its settings file: `~/.antigravity/settings.json` up to 2.29, `~/.gemini/config/config.json` from 2.30. jianmu writes that block, turned on, with its gateway’s address, a key that names the app and the `openai` wire protocol, and sets `models.defaultModelId` to the model you pick. The app then lists the gateway’s models in its picker and sends its chats to jianmu, which translates each one for the model’s provider. Your own gateway, default model, model list and catalog are kept aside and put back when jianmu steps out.

## Connect the app

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Antigravity’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under jianmu.
3. **Restart Antigravity.** It reads its gateway at start-up. jianmu’s models are then in its model picker.

```
jianmu antigravity deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # the app on DeepSeek
jianmu agy deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro            # agy on DeepSeek
```

## Its models

The picker lists the gateway’s models, the ones the app’s key is shown, under the names jianmu’s catalog gives them. On its own the app gives every model it doesn’t know a 200K window. jianmu points its `models.listSource` at the gateway’s catalog, which gives each model its real context window, so long sessions compact when they should.

## Effort

The catalog lists a model at each of its reasoning levels, so the app’s own picker offers them, and the level picked there goes with the request. The effort on jianmu’s row is the level the app starts on, and what a model with no levels in the picker is asked for. Left on the default, requests go as the app sends them.

## Your Google sign-in

On a gateway, Antigravity uses no Google sign-in and its backend asks Google for nothing. What Google turns on for your account, its experiments and commands such as `/boost`, `/teamwork`, `/plugin` and `/generative_ui`, is gone while it is on jianmu. Taking the row off jianmu gives it back.

## The agy CLI

`agy` follows the app’s gateway unless it is connected on its own row. Connected there, it runs on jianmu through the Gemini API: jianmu keeps its models in `jianmu-settings.json`, beside agy’s own `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, and starts agy with that file, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `--model` for that session. So that typing `agy` just works, jianmu adds a function named `agy` to each shell’s profile while agy is on one of its models. A terminal opened before takes the command from the row. Your `settings.json` stays yours, so `agy remote-control` still runs on your Google sign-in.

## Settings that come first

An `admin_settings.json` your organisation installs, and the `AGY_LLM_GATEWAY_*` variables, win over the settings file field by field. If either sets a gateway of its own, Antigravity doesn’t reach jianmu, and the row says so.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own models on the row, or take the row off jianmu. jianmu puts back your own gateway, default model, model list and catalog. For agy, it removes the shell function too. Restart Antigravity.

## FAQ

### Can Antigravity run on models other than Gemini?

Yes. Any model you have in jianmu is in its picker: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Do I still need to sign in with Google?

No. On a gateway Antigravity uses no Google sign-in. What Google turns on for your account, such as /boost and /teamwork, is off while it is on jianmu.

### Why does every model show a 200K context?

That is the app’s default for models it doesn’t know. jianmu points its catalog at the gateway, which gives each model its real window. Restart Antigravity after connecting.

### Does the agy CLI work too?

Yes. agy follows the app’s gateway, or runs on its own row through the Gemini API, with an agy shell function so the command just works.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Cursor Private Inference on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference) and [Snow CLI on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/snow-cli). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/snow-cli

# Snow CLI on any model

Snow CLI (`snow`, the npm package `snow-ai`) keeps each API setup as a profile. jianmu adds one of its own that points Snow at jianmu’s gateway, so Snow can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

Snow keeps its settings in `~/.snow` (or `$SNOW_CONFIG_DIR`). Each profile is a file in `profiles/`, `active-profile.json` names the one in use, and `config.json` is a copy of it. jianmu writes `profiles/jianmu.json`: a copy of the profile you were on, with jianmu’s gateway as its base URL, a key that names Snow, Chat Completions as its protocol and the model you pick as its model. It makes that profile the active one and copies it to `config.json`, as Snow’s own profile switch does. The gateway then sends each request to the model’s provider.

## Connect Snow

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Snow CLI’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under jianmu.
3. **Restart open snow sessions.** Snow reads its profile at start-up.

```
jianmu snow deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # Snow on DeepSeek
jianmu snow default                     # back to your own profile
```

It works the same for Snow in a WSL distro on Windows: the profile there names the gateway as the distro reaches it.

## Your profiles

Your own profiles are not changed. jianmu’s copies your other settings from the one you were on, but leaves out a subscription sign-in of yours (`snowcfg.oauth`). A profile of your own that happens to be named `jianmu` is kept and put back. On the row, the models of your own profiles are listed too: picking one makes Snow switch to that profile.

## Windows and images

jianmu sets `maxContextTokens`, `maxTokens` and `supportsVision` from its catalog for the model you pick, so Snow knows its real window and whether it takes images. A model jianmu knows no limits for gets Snow’s own defaults, 200K and 64K. If you change one of these in Snow’s settings, it stays as you set it. A vision model of your own is kept only with an endpoint and key of its own. Images for a model that can’t see go through jianmu’s Vision, which describes them at the gateway.

## The light model

Snow asks a light model (`basicModel`) for summaries, compaction and file search. On jianmu’s profile it follows the main model, unless you pick another jianmu model in the row’s small field. That pick stays when you change the main model.

## Thinking

The row’s thinking field sets `chatThinking` on jianmu’s profile: a level sends `reasoning_effort` with each request, and off is Snow’s default. Only models that list reasoning levels offer it.

## Snow App

Snow App keeps API setups of its own. Its Sync Snow CLI API config button copies Snow CLI’s profiles into it, jianmu’s among them, so the app can use jianmu’s models too.

## Switch back

Pick one of your own models on the row, run `jianmu snow default`, or take the row off jianmu. Snow goes back to the profile you were on, `profiles/jianmu.json` is removed, and `config.json` is a copy of your profile again.

## FAQ

### Can Snow CLI use DeepSeek, GLM or Qwen?

Yes. Any model you have in jianmu can be Snow’s model: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Does jianmu change my own Snow profiles?

No. It adds a profile of its own, profiles/jianmu.json, and makes it the active one. Switching back makes your profile active again.

### Why does Snow show the wrong context size?

jianmu sets maxContextTokens and maxTokens from its catalog for the model you pick. A value you changed in Snow yourself stays as you set it.

### Which protocol does Snow use with jianmu?

Chat Completions (requestMethod chat). The row warns when jianmu’s profile is set to another one.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Gemini CLI](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/gemini-cli-models), [Cursor Private Inference on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cursor-private-inference), [Antigravity on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/antigravity) and [JetBrains Air on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/jetbrains-air). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/jetbrains-air

# JetBrains Air on any model

JetBrains Air runs its own agents (Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, Junie) on accounts signed in under its settings, with no base URL to point elsewhere. It also takes any agent that speaks the Agent Client Protocol. jianmu adds one, named Jianmu, so Air can run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

Air lists custom ACP agents from `acp.json` in its config folder: `~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/Air` on macOS, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/JetBrains/Air` on Linux, `%APPDATA%\JetBrains\Air` on Windows. jianmu adds an entry named `Jianmu` there that starts `opencode acp`, OpenCode’s ACP server, with `OPENCODE_CONFIG` set to `jianmu-opencode.json`, a file jianmu keeps beside `acp.json`. That file holds jianmu’s provider, its models, the model a task starts on, and `enabled_providers` narrowed to jianmu. OpenCode merges it over your own config and leaves your plugins, agents and MCP servers as they are. Air’s own agents, and the accounts they run on, aren’t touched.

## Connect Air

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on JetBrains Air’s row.** In the Agents tab, choose a model under jianmu.
3. **Start a new task in Air.** Pick Jianmu in its agent menu. jianmu’s models and routing groups are in its model menu.

```
jianmu air deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro        # the Air app
jianmu air-ide deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro    # Air in JetBrains IDEs
```

## OpenCode

The Jianmu agent is OpenCode, so OpenCode has to be installed. jianmu gives Air its full path, since an app may not have your shell’s PATH: the one on PATH, else `~/.opencode/bin`, else one a JetBrains IDE or Zed installed from the ACP registry. If none is found, the row says to install it:

```
npm i -g --allow-scripts=@opencode/cli @opencode/cli
```

## The model menu

Air’s model menu for the Jianmu agent is the list OpenCode reports, which is jianmu’s models and routing groups and nothing of OpenCode’s own. The model picked on the row is the one a new task starts on, and also OpenCode’s small model for titles and summaries. You can pick another in Air’s menu for each task.

## Air in JetBrains IDEs

Air is also a plugin in JetBrains IDEs: bundled with 2026.3, and installed from JetBrains Marketplace in 2026.2. The plugin reads custom agents from `~/.jetbrains/acp.json` on every system, so it has a row of its own, Air (JetBrains IDEs), which adds the same Jianmu agent there. Restart the IDE if Jianmu isn’t listed yet. In the IDE, Air’s own Codex and Claude Agent, on their own login, run this computer’s `codex` and `claude`, so they are on jianmu too while Codex and Claude Code are connected in jianmu. The model on Air’s row is the Jianmu agent’s alone.

## WSL projects

An IDE on Windows starts the agent of a project that lives in a WSL distro inside that distro, and refuses a Windows command there. So each running distro with OpenCode gets an entry of its own, such as `Jianmu (WSL Ubuntu)`, with OpenCode’s path in the distro and a config that names the gateway as the distro reaches it.

## Provider keys in the environment

One gap is OpenCode’s: when a provider’s key is set in the environment Air starts it with (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and so on, not empty), its ACP server lists that provider and none from its config, so jianmu’s models don’t show. Unset the variable, or keep the key in OpenCode’s `auth.json` instead.

## Switch back

Take the row off jianmu. jianmu removes the Jianmu entry from `acp.json` and deletes `jianmu-opencode.json`. Air’s own agents were never changed. If the Jianmu entry is removed by hand, the row says Air no longer reaches jianmu.

## FAQ

### Can JetBrains Air use DeepSeek, GLM or Qwen?

Yes. Pick the Jianmu agent in a new Air task, and every model you have in jianmu is in its model menu: DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, GPT, Claude and more.

### Does jianmu change Air’s own agents or accounts?

No. It adds one ACP agent, Jianmu, to acp.json. Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie keep their own accounts.

### Why doesn’t the Jianmu agent show jianmu’s models?

Usually a provider key such as OPENAI_API_KEY is set in the environment Air starts with. OpenCode then lists only that provider. Unset it, or keep the key in OpenCode’s auth.json.

### Does it work in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and other JetBrains IDEs?

Yes, through the Air plugin (bundled with 2026.3, from Marketplace in 2026.2). Connect the Air (JetBrains IDEs) row and restart the IDE.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Antigravity on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/antigravity), [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codebuddy) and [Snow CLI on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/snow-cli). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codebuddy

# CodeBuddy on any model

CodeBuddy is Tencent's AI coding tool: the CodeBuddy Code CLI (`codebuddy`, `cbc`) and the CodeBuddy IDE. Both the international edition (codebuddy.ai) and the China one (codebuddy.cn) take custom models. jianmu writes your jianmu models into that list, so CodeBuddy runs on DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, and those models need no CodeBuddy sign-in.

CodeBuddy Code is one npm package, `@tencent-ai/codebuddy-code`, for both editions; the China one is told apart by `CODEBUDDY_INTERNET_ENVIRONMENT=internal`. Both read custom models from `~/.codebuddy/models.json` (or `$CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR`), and the CodeBuddy IDE reads the same file. So jianmu has one row, CodeBuddy, for the CLI and the IDE.

## Set up CodeBuddy

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on CodeBuddy's row.** On the Agents page, pick a model under jianmu. jianmu writes every model into models.json and the one you picked into settings.json's `model`.
3. **Start a new session.** CodeBuddy Code reads its model when a session starts: restart `codebuddy`, or run `/clear` in an open session.

```
jianmu codebuddy deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
jianmu codebuddy            # show what it is set to
```

## models.json

Each model jianmu writes points at the jianmu gateway on this computer and is asked under a Bearer key jianmu gives CodeBuddy. CodeBuddy calls that address itself, not through Tencent's servers, with no CodeBuddy sign-in.

```
{"models": [{
  "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Pro", "vendor": "jianmu",
  "apiKey": "…", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/chat/completions",
  "maxInputTokens": …, "maxOutputTokens": …,
  "supportsToolCall": true, "supportsImages": …, "reasoning": {…}
}, …]}
```

`maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` come from jianmu's catalog; without `maxOutputTokens` CodeBuddy caps every reply at its own default. A model that thinks carries its levels (`supportedEfforts`, `defaultEffort`) and `canDisableThinking` when thinking can be turned off; a model with a window over 200K offers two sizes in `contextWindow`. CodeBuddy picks up a change to the file without a restart.

## CodeBuddy Code

In the CLI, the model a session starts on is `settings.json`'s `model`: one of jianmu's ids from models.json, or one of CodeBuddy's own. jianmu tells CodeBuddy's requests apart by their key, so Usage counts them under CodeBuddy.

## CodeBuddy IDE

CodeBuddy.app (codebuddy.ai) and CodeBuddy CN.app (codebuddy.cn) read the same `~/.codebuddy/models.json`. They watch the file, sync their model list when it changes, and list jianmu's models in the IDE's own model picker. The IDE needs no CLI; with only the IDE installed, jianmu still shows the CodeBuddy row. Two differences: the IDE always reads `.codebuddy` in your home folder, whatever `CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR` says, and it doesn't read settings.json's `model`, so the model is picked in the IDE.

## Your own models

Models you added to models.json yourself stay as they are; jianmu updates only its own, in the place they were. A jianmu model you turned off in CodeBuddy stays off, and a default thinking level you set on one stays while the model still offers it. When the file has `availableModels` (the models to show), jianmu's are added to it and the rest you listed stay.

## WSL

On Windows, a WSL distro with CodeBuddy Code installed has its own row. It writes the distro's `~/.codebuddy/models.json`, naming the gateway as the distro reaches it, with the key it takes from there. `CODEBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR` isn't read there.

## Switching back

Pick one of CodeBuddy's own models on the row: jianmu takes its models out of models.json and sets settings.json's `model` to yours. Or from a terminal:

```
jianmu codebuddy default
```

## FAQ

### Can CodeBuddy use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu writes them as custom models into ~/.codebuddy/models.json, and they show in both CodeBuddy Code's and the CodeBuddy IDE's model list.

### Do jianmu's models need a CodeBuddy sign-in?

No. They call the jianmu gateway on this computer under the key jianmu gives CodeBuddy, not through a CodeBuddy account.

### Does the China edition and CodeBuddy CN work?

Yes. Both CLI editions are one npm package, and CodeBuddy.app and CodeBuddy CN.app read the same models.json, so one row covers them all.

### I changed the model and nothing happened.

CodeBuddy Code reads its model when a session starts. Restart codebuddy or run /clear. In the IDE, pick the model in its model picker.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Kimi Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi-code), [Qwen Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwen-code) and [T3 Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/t3-code). Tencent Cloud's models: [Tencent Cloud](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tencent-cloud). Notes on the same models: [Obsidian on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/obsidian). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/obsidian

# Obsidian on any model

Obsidian has no AI of its own; its community plugins bring it. jianmu wires Copilot for Obsidian (logancyang/obsidian-copilot), which takes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you name. jianmu adds a provider called jianmu in every vault that has Copilot, so Obsidian's AI chat runs on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up Obsidian

1. **Install Copilot in Obsidian.** Install and turn on Copilot from Obsidian's Settings › Community plugins. jianmu shows the Obsidian row once a vault has Copilot.
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick jianmu on Obsidian's row.** On the Agents page, pick jianmu. Then reload Copilot in Obsidian, and jianmu's models are in its model menu.

```
jianmu obsidian provider jianmu
```

## Vaults

Obsidian lists its vaults in `obsidian.json` in its config folder: `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian` on a Mac, `%APPDATA%\obsidian` on Windows, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/obsidian` on Linux, or the Flatpak's and the Snap's own folders. Copilot keeps its settings in each vault's `.obsidian/plugins/copilot/data.json`. jianmu wires every vault that has Copilot; after that it keeps the wired vaults up to date and wires none you haven't asked for.

## The model list

This is what jianmu writes into data.json. Only these keys change; everything else in the file stays as written:

```
"providers": {"jianmu": {
  "providerType": "openai-compatible", "displayName": "jianmu",
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/agent/obsidian/v1",
  "requiresApiKey": false, …}},
"configuredModels": [{"providerId": "jianmu", "info": {"id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", …}}, …],
"backends": {"chat": {"enabledModels": […]}},
"defaultModelKey": "…"
```

Each model carries its context size, output limit, images and thinking levels from jianmu's catalog. A model new in jianmu comes on in chat; a jianmu model you turned off in Copilot stays off; one gone from jianmu leaves every backend. Models and providers you added in Copilot yourself are untouched. The first time, Copilot's default model becomes jianmu's first, and the one it had is kept to put back when you switch back.

## No key to enter

Copilot keeps API keys in Obsidian's keychain, which jianmu doesn't write. So jianmu's provider needs no key (`requiresApiKey: false`): its requests carry no Authorization, and the gateway takes a call with no key from this computer. Copilot calls it with fetch from Obsidian's window, so replies stream, and the gateway answers that window's CORS. The `/agent/obsidian` in the address is how jianmu knows it is Obsidian, since the window's User-Agent is a browser's.

## Reloading Copilot

While Obsidian runs, Copilot holds its settings and writes data.json whole when it saves. So after wiring, reload Copilot in Settings › Community plugins (or restart Obsidian) before changing Copilot's settings, or the old settings write over jianmu's. jianmu says so while Obsidian is running.

## Copilot 3

jianmu writes only Copilot 4's format (`providers` and `configuredModels`). Copilot 3 kept models in `activeModels`; jianmu leaves such a vault alone and names it in the error. Update Copilot to 4, which moves the settings itself when it first loads.

## Switching back

Turn the row off in jianmu. jianmu takes its provider, its models and their places in every backend out of each vault's data.json, and puts back the default model you had while jianmu's is still the default. A provider you added by hand under the name jianmu, at an address that isn't jianmu's Obsidian route, is yours and stays.

```
jianmu obsidian default
```

## FAQ

### Can Obsidian use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes, through the Copilot for Obsidian plugin. jianmu adds a jianmu provider in every vault with Copilot, and every model you have in jianmu is in Copilot's model menu.

### Do I enter an API key in Copilot?

No. jianmu's provider needs no key: requests go to the jianmu gateway on this computer, which calls the model with your key or subscription.

### Why doesn't Copilot show jianmu's models?

Reload Copilot in Obsidian's Settings › Community plugins, or restart Obsidian. A vault on Copilot 3 needs Copilot 4 first.

### Does Smart Connections work?

No. Its free plugin embeds with a local model only; its API providers are in the closed Pro plugin, with keys in the keychain jianmu can't write.

More apps on the same models: [Raycast](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/raycast), [Cherry Studio](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cherry-studio) and [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codebuddy). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/t3-code

# T3 Code on any model

T3 Code (pingdotgg/t3code) is a GUI that drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others. Each provider it lists is an instance of a driver, and it takes instances of your own. jianmu adds two: **jianmu**, on Claude Code, and **jianmu · Codex**, on Codex. So T3 Code's model picker lists every model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, on the harness you choose.

## Set up T3 Code

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick jianmu on T3 Code's row.** On the Agents page, pick jianmu. jianmu writes both instances into T3 Code's settings.json.
3. **Pick a model in T3 Code.** T3 Code's server watches the file and reloads it on an outside edit. In the model picker, models under jianmu run on Claude Code, those under jianmu · Codex on Codex.

```
jianmu t3code provider jianmu
```

The settings file is `~/.t3/userdata/settings.json` (`$T3CODE_HOME/userdata` when set). These are the two instances jianmu writes:

```
"providerInstances": {
  "jianmu": {"driver": "claudeAgent", "displayName": "jianmu",
    "environment": [{"name": "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "value": "http://127.0.0.1:3425", …}, …],
    "config": {"customModels": [{"slug": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": …,
      "capabilities": {"optionDescriptors": […]}}, …]}},
  "jianmu-codex": {"driver": "codex", "displayName": "jianmu · Codex",
    "config": {"launchArgs": […]}}
}
```

## jianmu, on Claude Code

The jianmu instance is a `claudeAgent` instance: T3 Code runs Claude Code through Anthropic's Agent SDK, reading your `~/.claude` settings, with the instance's environment added. jianmu sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to the gateway and the token Claude Code is routed with, so its requests are Claude Code's to the gateway. Every jianmu model is one of its custom models, a 1M one marked `[1m]` as jianmu marks it for Claude Code. A binary path or Claude home you gave T3's own Claude is carried over, so it runs the same Claude Code.

## jianmu · Codex, on Codex

T3 Code runs each thread on the harness of the instance its model is picked from, so with the Claude Code instance alone every jianmu model ran there. So jianmu adds a `codex` instance, jianmu · Codex. Its `launchArgs`, which T3 passes to `codex app-server` and `codex exec`, are Codex's own `-c` overrides: jianmu as its model provider, and `jianmu-codex-models.json` beside settings.json as its catalog, so T3 lists every jianmu model under it from Codex's model list. Your `~/.codex/config.toml` isn't written, and T3's own Codex stays as it is. If you remove the instance in T3, a sync doesn't bring it back; turning T3 Code's row on again in jianmu does.

## Reasoning

Without capabilities, T3 Code shows no picks beside a custom model and sends no effort. So each of jianmu's custom models gets a Reasoning pick of the Claude Code levels it takes, medium first (else the lowest), which T3 hands to Claude Code as it is. A model that thinks also gets a Thinking switch, on at first; T3 sets Claude Code's `alwaysThinkingEnabled` by it, and with it off requests ask for no thinking.

## Your own settings

The instances' names, whether they are on, and every key jianmu doesn't write (such as `autoCompactWindow` and `accentColor`) are yours, and what you change in T3 Code stays. Environment variables you add on jianmu's instance stay too. Your own instances, their custom models and T3's other settings are untouched. jianmu's are only the custom models, the gateway's variables, and the Codex instance's launch arguments and catalog.

## Claude Code's own routing

The `env` in `~/.claude/settings.json` is applied over the process', so a Claude Code routed elsewhere in its own settings takes the jianmu instance's requests there; one routed through jianmu or not routed at all asks the gateway. A provider switch on there, such as `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, takes it to that cloud, and jianmu's check says so.

## Switching back

Turn the row off in jianmu. jianmu takes out only its two instances; your others and your settings stay.

```
jianmu t3code default
```

## FAQ

### Can T3 Code use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu adds two provider instances to T3 Code's settings.json, and every model you have in jianmu is in T3's model picker, on Claude Code or on Codex.

### What is the difference between jianmu and jianmu · Codex?

The same models on a different harness: those under jianmu run on Claude Code, those under jianmu · Codex on Codex.

### Does it change my ~/.codex/config.toml or T3's own Claude and Codex?

No. Codex's settings are launch arguments of the jianmu · Codex instance alone; T3's own instances and yours stay as they are.

### Why don't requests go through jianmu?

Check the env in ~/.claude/settings.json: a Claude Code routed elsewhere there, or with a cloud switch such as Bedrock on, takes the jianmu instance's requests there.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [Models in Codex](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codex-models), [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codebuddy), [Craft Agents on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/craft-agents) and [Every jianmu model in Paseo](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/paseo). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/craft-agents

# Craft Agents on any model

Craft Agents (lukilabs/craft-agents-oss) is an Electron app that runs Claude and Pi sessions. Its models come from connections, and a custom endpoint is one. jianmu adds a connection named jianmu and makes it the one new sessions start on, so Craft Agents runs on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up Craft Agents

1. **Open Craft Agents once.** Craft Agents won't load a config.json without its workspaces, so jianmu never makes one. It is there once Craft Agents has run.
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on Craft Agents' row.** On the Agents page, pick a jianmu model for Craft Agents. Craft Agents watches config.json, so a running app takes it at once, from its next new session.

```
jianmu craft-agents deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## The jianmu connection

Connections are in `config.json` in Craft Agents' config folder (`CRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.craft-agent`). jianmu's is a `pi_compat` connection on OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions; its `models` are the models picked for Craft Agents in jianmu, and `defaultModel` is the one you chose.

```
"llmConnections": [
  …,
  {"slug": "jianmu", "name": "jianmu", "providerType": "pi_compat",
   "authType": "none",
   "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/agent/craft-agents/v1",
   "customEndpoint": {"api": "openai-completions"},
   "models": [{"id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": …}, …],
   "defaultModel": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"}
],
"defaultLlmConnection": "jianmu"
```

Craft Agents resets a `defaultModel` that isn't in `models` to the first one there, so jianmu always puts the model you picked in the list. A name or other field you give the connection in Craft Agents is kept when jianmu syncs it.

## No key to enter

Craft Agents keeps keys apart from config.json, sealed in `credentials.enc`, which jianmu doesn't open. jianmu's connection has `authType: none`, which is what Craft Agents itself saves for an endpoint on this computer with no key ("Local Model"); its Pi server then sends a placeholder key, which the gateway takes from this computer. Craft Agents sends no User-Agent of its own, so `/agent/craft-agents` in the address tells the gateway which agent is asking.

## New and open sessions

New sessions start on the connection `defaultLlmConnection` names; a workspace's own default goes over it. A session keeps the connection it started on, so start a new one after switching to jianmu. jianmu says so while Craft Agents is running.

## Your own connections

Your connections and every other key in config.json stay as written. Before taking over the default, jianmu stashes the one you had and puts it back when it steps out, where that connection is still there (else Craft Agents picks its first). If you delete the jianmu connection in Craft Agents, jianmu's check says it no longer reaches jianmu.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in jianmu: jianmu takes its connection out and puts your default back. Or pick a model of one of your own connections, and jianmu makes it that connection's default model.

```
jianmu craft-agents default
```

## FAQ

### Can Craft Agents use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu adds a jianmu connection to Craft Agents' config.json and makes it the default for new sessions; every model you picked in jianmu is in it.

### Do I enter an API key in Craft Agents?

No. jianmu's connection has authType none, as Craft Agents saves an endpoint on this computer with no key, and the gateway takes requests from this computer.

### Why is a session still on my old model?

A session keeps the connection it started on. Start a new session; a workspace's own default connection goes over the global one.

### jianmu says to open Craft Agents first?

Craft Agents won't load a config.json without its workspaces, so jianmu never makes one. Run Craft Agents once, then set it up.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [T3 Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/t3-code) and [CodeBuddy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/codebuddy). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openchamber

# OpenChamber on any model

OpenChamber is a desktop, web and VS Code front end for OpenCode. It runs an OpenCode of its own (the desktop app bundles OpenCode 2) on your OpenCode config. jianmu sets OpenChamber's default model to one of jianmu's and puts jianmu's provider in the OpenCode config, so OpenChamber runs on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up OpenChamber

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on OpenChamber's row.** On the Agents page, pick OpenChamber's default model, and a small model if you like.
3. **Start a new session.** OpenChamber takes the new model for new sessions.

```
jianmu openchamber deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro          # new sessions
jianmu openchamber small deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash  # titles, commit messages
```

OpenChamber's settings are under `$OPENCHAMBER_DATA_DIR`, `~/.config/openchamber` by default (not moved by `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). jianmu writes its profile, `preferences.json`, and the copy in `settings.json` that older builds read, where that file is:

```
// ~/.config/openchamber/preferences.json
{"version": 1, "fields": {
  "defaultModel": {"value": "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "updatedAt": …},
  "smallModelUseDefault": {"value": false, …},
  "smallModelOverride": {"value": "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", …}
}}
```

## Which model a session gets

OpenChamber sends each new session the model it picks, in this order: the project's `defaultModel` (settings.json's projects), the profile's `defaultModel`, the agent's own, and only then OpenCode's `model`. So setting OpenCode's model alone doesn't reach OpenChamber; jianmu sets the profile's `defaultModel`. A project with a default model of its own keeps it there, and jianmu names the project and its model. On a new model jianmu also clears the old one's `defaultVariant`, as OpenChamber's own picker does.

## The small model

OpenChamber's small model writes session titles and commit messages. It is `smallModelOverride` once `smallModelUseDefault` is false, else OpenCode's `small_model`. Picking a small model in jianmu writes those two keys; switching back takes both out and leaves it to OpenCode.

## The OpenCode config

A model in OpenChamber is OpenCode's `provider/model`, so one of jianmu's needs jianmu's provider in the OpenCode config: `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`. A provider of your own that already sends that model to jianmu's gateway is used instead of a second list of the same models. An OpenCode 2 config is written in OpenCode 2's words. Once OpenChamber steps off jianmu, jianmu's provider goes too, when nothing else in the OpenCode config names one of its models. Its requests count as OpenCode's, since OpenChamber's OpenCode sends them.

## New and open sessions

OpenChamber takes the new model for new sessions; sessions already open keep theirs. jianmu says so while OpenChamber is running.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in jianmu: jianmu takes out the profile's `defaultModel` and `defaultVariant`, and OpenChamber goes back to the OpenCode config's model.

```
jianmu openchamber default
```

## FAQ

### Can OpenChamber use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu sets OpenChamber's default model to the one you pick in jianmu and puts jianmu's provider in the OpenCode config.

### OpenCode is on jianmu already; why is OpenChamber still on my old model?

OpenChamber takes a project's and its profile's own defaultModel before OpenCode's model. Pick a model on OpenChamber's own row in jianmu.

### One project is still on the old model?

That project has a default model of its own in settings.json, which goes first there. jianmu names the project.

### Which model writes session titles and commit messages?

The small model: smallModelOverride once smallModelUseDefault is false, else OpenCode's small_model.

More agents on the same models: [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [T3 Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/t3-code) and [Craft Agents on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/craft-agents). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).
