Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/nanobot

# nanobot on any model

nanobot (HKUDS/nanobot, `pip install nanobot-ai`) is a personal AI assistant that answers in chat apps, its CLI and its WebUI. Its model comes from `~/.nanobot/config.json`, where any key under `providers` that isn't one of its own is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. jianmu adds a jianmu provider there and sets the default model to one of jianmu's, so nanobot runs on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up nanobot

1. **Run nanobot once.** `nanobot onboard` or its first run makes `~/.nanobot`.
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on nanobot's row.** On the Agents page, pick a jianmu model for nanobot. A nanobot in WSL is set up there too.

```
pip install nanobot-ai && nanobot onboard   # nanobot makes ~/.nanobot
jianmu nanobot deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## What goes in config.json

jianmu adds `providers.jianmu` at the gateway's `/v1`, with the gateway's key and a User-Agent of `nanobot` (the OpenAI SDK's otherwise, which tells it from no one), and sets `agents.defaults` to provider jianmu, model `jianmu/<model id>` and the context window jianmu knows the model to take. nanobot strips the `jianmu/` prefix before it sends the model.

```
// ~/.nanobot/config.json
{
  "providers": {
    …,
    "jianmu": {"apiBase": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1", "apiKey": "…",
               "extraHeaders": {"User-Agent": "nanobot"}}
  },
  "agents": {"defaults": {
    "provider": "jianmu",
    "model": "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
    "contextWindowTokens": …
  }}
}
```

nanobot's pydantic models read camelCase and snake_case keys alike. jianmu writes nanobot's own camelCase, and takes out a snake_case spelling of the same key, so no two settings disagree.

## modelPreset

When `agents.defaults.modelPreset` names one of `modelPresets`, it goes over both provider and model. So jianmu stashes it and takes it out while jianmu's model is on, and puts it back when it steps out; your `modelPresets` stay as they are.

## When it takes effect

nanobot's gateway (`nanobot gateway`, the WebUI's) watches the file and takes a change at its next reply. `nanobot agent` reads it once, so restart an open `nanobot agent` chat. jianmu says so while nanobot is running.

## Your own settings

The provider, model, context window and modelPreset you had under `agents.defaults` are stashed and put back when jianmu steps out. Your other providers, presets and keys stay as they are. A config.json jianmu made goes again once nothing is left in it. If you delete the jianmu provider in nanobot, jianmu's check says it no longer reaches jianmu.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in jianmu: jianmu takes out `providers.jianmu` and puts `agents.defaults` back. Or pick a model of your own, and jianmu puts things back and then sets it as the model.

```
jianmu nanobot default
```

## FAQ

### Can nanobot use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu adds an OpenAI-compatible jianmu provider to ~/.nanobot/config.json and sets the default model to the one you pick in jianmu.

### Why is nanobot still on the old model?

nanobot's gateway and WebUI take the change at their next reply; nanobot agent reads its config once, so restart the chat.

### Do I lose my modelPreset?

No. jianmu stashes agents.defaults.modelPreset and takes it out (it would go over jianmu's model), and puts it back when it steps out; modelPresets stay.

### Does it work for nanobot in WSL?

Yes. jianmu sets up a nanobot in a WSL distro too.

More agents on the same models: [OpenClaw on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openclaw), [Hermes Agent on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/hermes), [OpenChamber on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openchamber) and [AstrBot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/astrbot). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/astrbot

# AstrBot on any model

AstrBot (AstrBotDevs/AstrBot) is a chatbot framework that puts a model on QQ, Telegram, Discord, Lark and other platforms. It keeps every setting in one file, `data/cmd_config.json`. jianmu adds an OpenAI-compatible jianmu source there, an entry for each of jianmu's models, and makes the one you pick AstrBot's default chat model. So your bot runs on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, with no key typed into AstrBot's WebUI.

## Set up AstrBot

1. **Start AstrBot once.** Its first start writes `data/cmd_config.json`. It needs 4.10 or later (a config with `provider_sources`).
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on AstrBot's row.** On the Agents page, pick a jianmu model for AstrBot.
4. **Restart AstrBot.** AstrBot reads its config at start-up only; after a restart the bot is on the new model.

```
jianmu astrbot deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
# then restart AstrBot
```

jianmu finds AstrBot's root in this order: `ASTRBOT_ROOT`; the desktop app's `~/.astrbot`; a folder where `astrbot init` was run, either your home, `~/astrbot` or `~/AstrBot` (where its README and a clone of its source put it). For AstrBot run anywhere else, start jianmu with `ASTRBOT_ROOT` set to that folder.

## What goes in cmd_config.json

Since 4.10 AstrBot splits a chat provider into two lists: `provider_sources` holds endpoints and keys, and each entry of `provider` is one model of a source. jianmu adds a source with id `jianmu` (OpenAI Compatible, at the gateway's `/v1`, with a key naming AstrBot, so its requests count as AstrBot's in jianmu's usage), an entry `jianmu/<provider>/<model>` for each model, and sets `agent_runner.config.model.provider_id` to the one you pick (`provider_settings.default_provider_id` in a file from before agent_runner).

```
// /data/cmd_config.json
{
  "provider_sources": [
    …,
    {"id": "jianmu", "provider": "openai", "type": "openai_chat_completion",
     "provider_type": "chat_completion", "enable": true,
     "key": ["…"], "api_base": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1", …}
  ],
  "provider": [
    …,
    {"id": "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "provider_source_id": "jianmu",
     "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
     "modalities": ["text", "tool_use"], "max_context_tokens": …}
  ],
  "agent_runner": {"runner_type": "local",
    "config": {"model": {"provider_id": "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"}}}
}
```

Every model is marked `tool_use`: without it AstrBot drops the model's tools, and the gateway passes a tool call on whatever the model. Images are marked as jianmu knows the model sees them. A context window jianmu doesn't know is 0, and AstrBot looks it up itself.

## Why it needs a restart

AstrBot reads the whole file into memory at start, and its WebUI writes the whole of it back on every save. So jianmu's change needs AstrBot restarted, and a WebUI save made before that restart writes over it. jianmu's check notices that its source is gone and asks you to connect again.

When `agent_runner.runner_type` isn't `local` (an outside agent runner), AstrBot doesn't ask its chat model, and jianmu's check says so.

## Your own settings

Before it first writes the file, jianmu copies it to `cmd_config.json.before-jianmu`. Your own sources and models stay byte for byte, and so do changes you make to jianmu's entries in the WebUI (a source's timeout or proxy, a model switched off, its extra body). A model picked for one chat with `/provider` lives in AstrBot's own database; it is yours and stands. AstrBot writes the file with a UTF-8 BOM, which jianmu keeps.

## AstrBot in Docker

AstrBot in Docker isn't one jianmu wires: its data folder is a volume jianmu can't know, and the gateway on this machine's loopback isn't the container's.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in jianmu: jianmu takes its source and models out and puts the default chat model back to the one AstrBot was on, unless you have picked another in AstrBot since, which stands. Or pick a model of your own; jianmu's models stay in the list beside it until you disconnect. Restart AstrBot after either.

```
jianmu astrbot default
# then restart AstrBot
```

## FAQ

### Can AstrBot use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu adds an OpenAI-compatible jianmu source to cmd_config.json, an entry for each of jianmu's models, and sets the one you pick as the default chat model. Restart AstrBot to use it.

### Why is my bot still on the old model?

AstrBot reads cmd_config.json at start-up only, so restart it. Don't save anything in the WebUI before that, or it writes over jianmu's change.

### jianmu's source is gone. What now?

A WebUI save most likely wrote the whole file back. Connect AstrBot again in jianmu, then restart AstrBot.

### Does it work for AstrBot in Docker?

Not on its own: jianmu can't know the container's data volume, and this machine's loopback isn't the container's.

More agents on the same models: [nanobot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/nanobot), [QwenPaw on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwenpaw), [OpenClaw on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openclaw) and [Every model in Cherry Studio, through jianmu](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cherry-studio). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aionui

# AionUi on any model

AionUi is an Electron desktop app that runs Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, and has a chat of its own. It keeps its model providers in its own database, their keys encrypted, so jianmu writes nothing there. It opens AionUi's own add-provider link instead, which brings up AionUi's add-model form with jianmu filled in, for you to confirm in AionUi. AionUi then has every model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, and the Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot subscription you signed in to.

## Add jianmu to AionUi

1. **Open AionUi once.** Once AionUi has run, its data folder has an `aionui` folder and jianmu's Agents page lists it.
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Click Add jianmu.** On AionUi's row, click Add jianmu. AionUi opens Settings → Model's add form with jianmu filled in: name jianmu, platform custom (OpenAI-compatible), the gateway's address and a key.
4. **Confirm it in AionUi.** Nothing is added until you do.

The link jianmu opens looks like this:

```
aionui://add-provider?api_key=…&base_url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A3425%2Fv1&name=jianmu&platform=custom
```

If nothing opens, nothing on this computer handles AionUi's links yet: open AionUi once or install it again, then click Add jianmu again.

## Picking models

The jianmu provider's address ends in `/v1`, as AionUi's own OpenAI preset does, and it lists every model in jianmu from the gateway, named provider/model (for example `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`). A provider you add to jianmu later shows up when AionUi fetches the list again, with nothing changed in AionUi. Several accounts behind one model, the rest after a 429 and fallback work as they do for every other agent.

## From the command line

```
jianmu aionui add      # opens AionUi to add jianmu; confirm it there
```

## How jianmu knows it was added

jianmu reads AionUi's database (`aionui/aionui-backend.db` in AionUi's data folder: `~/Library/Application Support/AionUi` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\AionUi` on Windows, `~/.config/AionUi` on Linux) read-only, for a provider at the gateway's address. It can read it while AionUi runs, and never writes it. Once there is one, the row says it's added, and you can click again to add it again. When the database can't be read, jianmu says it doesn't know, not that it isn't added.

## Usage and keys

The key in the link is AionUi's own, so its requests are counted as AionUi's in jianmu's usage, apart from other agents.

## FAQ

### Do I need an API key to use Claude or ChatGPT in AionUi?

No. Sign in to a Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot subscription in jianmu and its models show up under AionUi's jianmu provider.

### Does jianmu change AionUi's settings?

No. jianmu opens AionUi's own add-model form, and you confirm it. It only reads AionUi's database to show whether jianmu was added.

### What address and platform does the jianmu provider use?

Platform custom (OpenAI-compatible), at http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1, or the gateway address you set in jianmu.

### AionUi isn't on jianmu's Agents page.

jianmu lists AionUi once it has run on this computer. Open AionUi once, then look again.

More desktop apps on the same models: [Every model in Cherry Studio, through jianmu](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cherry-studio) and [AstrBot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/astrbot). Using coding agents too? See [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/subscriptions). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/qwenpaw

# QwenPaw on any model

QwenPaw (agentscope-ai/QwenPaw, formerly CoPaw) is a personal assistant app with agents of its own. jianmu adds an OpenAI-compatible jianmu provider to QwenPaw with every model in jianmu listed, and sets the model you pick as an agent's `active_model`. So QwenPaw's agents run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription, a different one for each agent if you like.

## Set up QwenPaw

1. **Start QwenPaw once.** Run `qwenpaw app` so it writes its agents' settings (`agent.json`).
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Pick a model on QwenPaw's row.** On the Agents page, pick a jianmu model for QwenPaw, and an effort if you want one.
4. **Restart QwenPaw after the first connect.** QwenPaw reads its provider files at start-up only; after one restart it is on jianmu.

```
jianmu qwenpaw deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro          # the default agent
jianmu qwenpaw#writer deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash  # the agent named writer
jianmu qwenpaw effort high                        # thinking_level
```

## What jianmu writes

QwenPaw's working folder is `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR`; without it, a legacy `~/.copaw` when there is one, else `~/.qwenpaw`. Its secret folder is `QWENPAW_SECRET_DIR` (which the working folder's `.env` may set too), else `<working folder>.secret`, such as `~/.qwenpaw.secret`.

jianmu writes `<secret folder>/providers/custom/jianmu.json`, the way QwenPaw's console saves a provider from Add provider: OpenAI Chat Completions (`OpenAIChatModel`) at the gateway's `/v1`, a key naming QwenPaw, and each of jianmu's models in `extra_models`. It then sets `active_model` in the agent's `agent.json` to provider jianmu and the model you pick; the effort goes in `thinking_level` (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or empty for inherit, the model's own).

```
// ~/.qwenpaw.secret/providers/custom/jianmu.json
{"id": "jianmu", "name": "jianmu", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
 "api_key": "…", "chat_model": "OpenAIChatModel", "is_custom": true,
 "extra_models": [{"id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", …}, …]}

// ~/.qwenpaw/workspaces/default/agent.json
{"active_model": {"provider_id": "jianmu", "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"},
 "thinking_level": "high", …}
```

QwenPaw keeps keys encrypted (starting `ENC:`). jianmu writes the key in plain text and QwenPaw encrypts it at its next start, which is how its own files hold a key, so the key goes nowhere QwenPaw doesn't keep it. The provider file is readable by you alone (0600).

## When it takes effect

QwenPaw reads its provider files once, at start, so restart it after the first connect and after jianmu's models change; until then a turn on jianmu's model fails with `Provider 'jianmu' not found`. A model picked for an agent after that needs no restart: QwenPaw reads `agent.json` again when it changes and asks for the model on every turn, so the new one is used from the next message.

## Several agents

Each of QwenPaw's agents is a row in jianmu: `qwenpaw` is the default agent, which is always there, and any other is `qwenpaw#<id>`. Only an agent on QwenPaw's own backend (qwenpaw, the default) runs that model; one on an ACP backend runs another program, so jianmu doesn't wire it and asks you to switch it to QwenPaw's own backend first.

## Your own settings

The agent's `active_model` from before is stashed and put back when jianmu steps out. `fallback_models` and `subagent_model` are left alone. What you change in jianmu's provider in QwenPaw's console (a model's window, its generation settings, the provider's headers) stays. If you switch jianmu's provider off or delete it in QwenPaw, jianmu's check says it no longer reaches jianmu.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in jianmu: jianmu puts the agent's `active_model` back. It removes `custom/jianmu.json` only once no agent names jianmu's provider any more, in a fallback or subagent model either. Or pick a model of one of your own providers; jianmu's provider stays in the list until you disconnect.

```
jianmu qwenpaw default
```

## FAQ

### Can QwenPaw use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu writes an OpenAI-compatible jianmu provider into QwenPaw's secret folder and sets the model you pick as the agent's active_model. Restart QwenPaw once after the first connect.

### Why does it say Provider 'jianmu' not found?

QwenPaw reads its provider files at start-up only. Restart QwenPaw once after connecting; after that a new model is used from the next message, with no restart.

### Does it work for CoPaw?

Yes. QwenPaw was CoPaw; with a legacy ~/.copaw there, jianmu uses it as the working folder, as QwenPaw does.

### Can each agent use a different model?

Yes. The default agent is the qwenpaw row in jianmu and any other is qwenpaw#, each with its own model and effort.

More agents on the same models: [AstrBot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/astrbot), [nanobot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/nanobot) and [OpenClaw on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openclaw). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/zoo-code

# Zoo Code on any model

Zoo Code (Zoo-Code-Org/Zoo-Code, the VS Code extension ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code, a fork of Roo Code) keeps its provider profiles in VS Code's secret storage, encrypted and out of reach. But on every start it imports the file its `zoo-code.autoImportSettingsPath` setting names, as its own Settings → Import does. jianmu writes that file: one OpenAI-compatible profile named jianmu, at the local gateway, on the model you pick. So Zoo Code runs on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up Zoo Code

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on Zoo Code's row.** With the Zoo Code extension installed, jianmu's Agents page has a Zoo Code row; pick a model.
3. **Reload the VS Code window.** Run **Developer: Reload Window** from the Command Palette; Zoo Code imports jianmu's profile as it starts and switches to it.

```
jianmu zoo-code deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
# VS Code: Developer: Reload Window
```

## What jianmu writes

jianmu writes the file to import in Zoo Code's own folder in VS Code's User folder, `globalStorage/zoocodeorganization.zoo-code/settings/jianmu-import.json`, beside the settings files Zoo Code keeps itself. It then points `zoo-code.autoImportSettingsPath` at it in VS Code's `settings.json`. A value of your own is kept aside and put back on Disconnect.

```
// /globalStorage/zoocodeorganization.zoo-code/settings/jianmu-import.json
{"providerProfiles": {"currentApiConfigName": "jianmu",
  "apiConfigs": {"jianmu": {"id": "jianmu", "apiProvider": "openai",
    "openAiBaseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1", "openAiApiKey": "…",
    "openAiModelId": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "openAiStreamingEnabled": true,
    "openAiCustomModelInfo": {"contextWindow": …, "maxTokens": …, "supportsImages": …}}}}}

// /settings.json
"zoo-code.autoImportSettingsPath": "…/jianmu-import.json"
```

The profile uses Zoo Code's OpenAI Compatible provider on the gateway's Chat Completions (`/v1`), with a key naming Zoo Code; its requests say `ZooCode/<version>` as their User-Agent, so jianmu's usage counts them under Zoo Code. `openAiCustomModelInfo` carries the model's window (Zoo Code trims a conversation to it; 128K when it isn't told), what a reply may take, and whether it sends images. Imported profiles are merged over yours, which stay.

## When it takes effect

Zoo Code reads the file only when it starts, so reload the window once after you pick. While connected it imports the file again on every start, so each start puts it back on jianmu's profile; a profile you switch to inside Zoo Code meanwhile is one jianmu can't see, and the next start comes back. When jianmu's models or the key change, jianmu updates the file, used from the next start.

## VS Code profiles

VS Code's default profile and each profile you made has its own `settings.json`; jianmu points the setting at its file in every one, and in a profile made later too. If any of them can't be written, all are put back as they were.

## Zoo Code for JetBrains

Zoo Code for JetBrains runs the same extension in its own extension host, which is handed an empty configuration on every start, so the setting can't reach it; and it keeps its secrets in `~/.zoo-code/secrets.json`, a store of its own with no lock and no documented format. jianmu writes neither, so the JetBrains build isn't wired.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in jianmu: jianmu puts the setting back in every `settings.json` and removes the import file. A profile once imported lives in Zoo Code's secret storage, which jianmu can't write, so the jianmu profile stays in Zoo Code's list; switch from it or delete it in Zoo Code.

```
jianmu zoo-code default
```

## FAQ

### Can Zoo Code use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu writes a jianmu profile Zoo Code imports when it starts, on the local gateway's Chat Completions and the model you pick in jianmu. Reload the window once after you pick.

### Why didn't Zoo Code change after I picked a model?

Zoo Code imports profiles only when it starts. Run Developer: Reload Window from VS Code's Command Palette.

### Does it work in Zoo Code for JetBrains?

No. The JetBrains build is handed an empty configuration on every start, so the import setting can't reach it, and its secrets file has no documented format; jianmu writes neither.

### Why is the jianmu profile still there after Disconnect?

An imported profile lives in Zoo Code's encrypted secret storage, which jianmu can't write. jianmu stops the import and puts the setting back; the profile is yours to switch from or delete in Zoo Code.

More agents on the same models: [Cline on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cline), [Goose on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/goose) and [Hermes Agent on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/hermes). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/jcode

# jcode on any model

jcode (1jehuang/jcode) is a coding agent in Rust that keeps its settings in `config.toml`. A provider of your own is a named profile, `[providers.<name>]`, as `jcode provider add` writes it. jianmu adds itself as the profile jianmu, at the local gateway, with every jianmu model listed, and starts jcode on the model you pick. So jcode runs on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a ChatGPT or Copilot subscription.

## Set up jcode

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model on jcode's row.** With jcode installed, jianmu's Agents page has a jcode row; pick a model.
3. **Start jcode.** A new jcode starts on that model; restart a session that is already open.

```
jianmu jcode deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
jcode   # /model lists every jianmu model, /effort its levels
```

## What jianmu writes

jcode's folder is `$JCODE_HOME`, else `~/.jcode`. In its `config.toml` jianmu writes `[providers.jianmu]`: `type = "openai-compatible"` (jcode's Chat Completions client), `base_url` at the gateway's `/v1`, an `api_key` naming jcode, and `requires_api_key = true`. That last one is there because jcode takes a gateway on loopback as needing no key and then sends none, and the key is how the gateway knows the request is jcode's. It then sets `default_provider` and `default_model` in `[provider]` to jianmu and the model you pick.

```
# ~/.jcode/config.toml
[provider]
default_provider = "jianmu"
default_model = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"

[providers.jianmu]
type = "openai-compatible"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
api_key = "…"
requires_api_key = true
models = [
  { id = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", context_window = …, input = ["text"], reasoning = true },
  …
]
```

## /model and /effort

Each of jianmu's models is an entry in `models`, so jcode's `/model` picker lists them all and switches between them. Each entry carries the context window (128K when jianmu doesn't know it; jcode would take 200K) and whether it takes images; a model with effort levels gets `reasoning = true`, so jcode's `/effort` offers them. A `reasoning_effort` you set on one of jianmu's models stays while the model has that level. When jianmu's models change, jianmu updates the list.

## When it takes effect

jcode reads its settings at start-up, so restart an open jcode session to use a new model or list; jianmu says so while jcode is running.

## Your own settings

The profile and model `[provider]` named before are stashed and put back when jianmu steps out. Every other key of the file is yours and stays as written, your own keys in jianmu's profile too (headers, extra_body, a model's reasoning_effort). A `config.toml` that doesn't parse is an error and left as it is, never taken as empty. When jcode saves its settings itself it writes the models as `[[providers.jianmu.models]]` tables; jianmu folds them back into one array on its next write.

## Switching back

Set the row back to default in jianmu: when jcode still starts on jianmu, jianmu puts `[provider]` back as it was; a pick you made in jcode since is yours and stands. Then the whole `[providers.jianmu]` goes, with your own keys in it. Or pick one of jcode's own models, and jianmu sets `default_model` to it.

```
jianmu jcode default
```

## FAQ

### Can jcode use DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi or Qwen?

Yes. jianmu writes an openai-compatible [providers.jianmu] profile into jcode's config.toml at the local gateway, and starts jcode on the model you pick.

### Can I switch jianmu's models in jcode's /model?

Yes. Every jianmu model is in the jianmu profile's models, so /model lists and switches them; a model with effort levels offers them in /effort.

### Why didn't jcode change after I picked a model?

jcode reads its settings at start-up. Restart the open jcode session.

### Do my settings stay after switching back?

Yes. jianmu removes only [providers.jianmu], and puts [provider] back when jcode still starts on jianmu; every other key stays as written.

More agents on the same models: [Crush on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/crush), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models), [Goose on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/goose) and [Reasonix Studio on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/reasonix). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/paseo

# Every jianmu model in Paseo

Paseo (getpaseo/paseo) is an app that runs Claude Code, Codex and others for you. It starts the same Claude Code, so a Claude Code connected to jianmu goes through jianmu in Paseo too. But Paseo lists models itself, and most of the models jianmu serves aren't in its picker. jianmu writes them into Paseo's own `additionalModels`, so Paseo's Claude model picker offers every model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Paseo

1. **Connect Claude Code to jianmu first.** On jianmu's Agents page, pick a jianmu model for Claude Code. The ids Paseo lists are served by a Claude Code that is on jianmu.
2. **Switch Paseo's row on.** With a `~/.paseo` folder, jianmu has a Paseo row. Pick jianmu: every jianmu model in Paseo's Claude model picker.
3. **Restart Paseo's daemon.** Paseo reads its model list when its daemon starts; after a restart jianmu's models are there.

```
jianmu claude deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro   # Claude Code on jianmu first
jianmu paseo jianmu                      # every jianmu model in Paseo's picker
```

## Why Paseo needs its own switch

Claude Code's own `/model` reads modelPicker in `~/.claude/settings.json`, where jianmu writes every model when it connects Claude Code. Paseo never reads modelPicker: its list is its own first-party models plus settings.json's `model` and a few `ANTHROPIC_*_MODEL` tier variables. So with only Claude Code connected, jianmu's models other than the main one and the tiers aren't in Paseo's picker. Paseo also appends `agents.providers.claude.additionalModels` from its own config, each id passed to Claude Code as written, and that is where jianmu writes.

## What jianmu writes

Paseo's folder is `PASEO_HOME`, else `~/.paseo`. In `config.json` jianmu adds one `{id, label, description}` entry per model to `agents.providers.claude.additionalModels`: the same ids, [1m] marks and names as Claude Code's `/model`, with a description ending `via jianmu`, which is how jianmu knows its own entries.

```
// ~/.paseo/config.json
{"agents": {"providers": {"claude": {"additionalModels": [
  {"id": "my-own-model", "label": "…", "description": "…"},
  {"id": "…", "label": "…", "description": "via jianmu"},
  {"id": "…", "label": "…", "description": "1M context · via jianmu"}
]}}}}
```

Your own entries keep their place and come first. An id you listed yourself stays yours, and jianmu doesn't add it again. A list jianmu can't read is left as it is. When jianmu's models change, jianmu updates its entries.

## When it takes effect

Paseo reads its model list when its daemon starts, so restart Paseo's daemon to see jianmu's models; jianmu says so while Paseo is running. Claude Code itself must be connected to jianmu too, for those ids to be served.

## Switching back

Set Paseo's row back to default in jianmu: jianmu takes out only the entries whose description ends `via jianmu`, and yours stay; with none left, `additionalModels` goes.

```
jianmu paseo default
```

## FAQ

### Why doesn't Paseo's model picker show jianmu's models?

Paseo doesn't read Claude Code's modelPicker; it lists its own models, settings.json's model and a few ANTHROPIC_*_MODEL variables. Switch Paseo's row on in jianmu and jianmu writes every model into Paseo's additionalModels.

### Does Claude Code need to be connected first?

Yes. Paseo passes those ids as written to the Claude Code it starts, and jianmu serves them once Claude Code is connected to jianmu.

### I switched it on and still see nothing. Why?

Paseo reads its model list when its daemon starts. Restart Paseo's daemon.

### Will my own additionalModels be changed?

No. jianmu adds and removes only entries whose description ends via jianmu; yours come first and keep their place.

More agents on the same models: [Models in Claude Code](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/claude-code-models), [T3 Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/t3-code) and [Craft Agents on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/craft-agents). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/reasonix

# Reasonix Studio on any model

Reasonix Studio 2.x and its CLI share one `config.toml` and `.env`. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu there, pointing at jianmu's local gateway, so Reasonix's executor and planner can each be any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription. Your other providers, keys and project or session settings are left alone.

## Set up Reasonix

1. **Open jianmu's Agents page.** Find the Reasonix Studio row. Its model field is called executor.
2. **Pick a jianmu model.** The list has two groups: Reasonix Studio's own models and the ones via jianmu. Pick one of the latter; jianmu writes the provider and key, then sets `default_model` to `jianmu/<model>`.
3. **Set effort and a planner if you want.** A model with effort levels can take an effort. The planner can be a different model, or off to turn the separate planner off.

```
jianmu reasonix jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro   # executor
jianmu reasonix effort high
jianmu reasonix planner jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash # a separate planner, or: off
```

## What jianmu writes

Reasonix's folder is `REASONIX_HOME`; without it, `%APPDATA%\reasonix` on Windows and `~/.reasonix` elsewhere. A Reasonix in WSL uses Linux's `~/.reasonix`, with the gateway as the distro reaches it. jianmu writes:

```
# ~/.reasonix/config.toml
default_model = "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"

[[providers]]
name = "jianmu"
kind = "openai"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
api_key_env = "JIANMU_REASONIX_API_KEY"
models = ["…", "…"]
default = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
reasoning_protocol = "openai"
no_proxy = true

[providers.model_overrides."deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"]
supported_efforts = ["…"]
context_window = …
max_output_tokens = …

# ~/.reasonix/.env
JIANMU_REASONIX_API_KEY=…
```

Each model carries its context window, max output, image support and effort levels; a model with no effort levels gets `reasoning_protocol = "none"`. When jianmu's models change, jianmu updates the provider. When Studio has a `[desktop] provider_access` list, jianmu adds jianmu to it. The key goes only in `.env`; config.toml names the variable.

jianmu only touches its own entry. If there is already a jianmu provider jianmu didn't make, another provider uses `JIANMU_REASONIX_API_KEY`, or `.env` sets it twice, jianmu stops with an error rather than overwrite. jianmu keeps a restore record in its own config folder (settings only, never an upstream credential) to put your `default_model` back when you switch back.

## Executor and planner

The executor is `default_model` and the planner is `[agent] planner_model`; each can come from jianmu or from one of Reasonix's own providers. While the planner still uses jianmu, jianmu's provider stays, even with the executor back on your own model.

## When it takes effect

Reasonix Studio 2.x and the native 1.39.x/2.x CLI read global settings at startup, so start a new process after a change. A model set for a project or session overrides the executor and planner.

## Switching back

Switching back undoes only what jianmu added: the jianmu provider goes, `default_model` returns to what it was before (or goes if there was none), jianmu leaves `provider_access`, and jianmu's key leaves `.env`; a file jianmu created is removed once empty. A model you picked later, and edits to other providers and keys, stay. You can also just pick a model from the Reasonix Studio group.

```
jianmu reasonix default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in Reasonix Studio?

On jianmu's Agents page, pick a via-jianmu model as Reasonix Studio's executor. jianmu adds a jianmu provider to config.toml, the key to .env, and sets default_model to jianmu/.

### Can the planner be a different model?

Yes. The planner field writes [agent] planner_model: another jianmu model, one of Reasonix's own, or off.

### I changed it and Reasonix didn't notice. Why?

Reasonix reads global settings at startup. Start a new Studio or CLI process; a model set for a project or session also overrides the global one.

### Will my own providers and keys change?

No. jianmu adds and removes only the provider named jianmu and JIANMU_REASONIX_API_KEY, and stops with an error on a same-named entry it didn't make.

More agents on the same models: [jcode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/jcode), [Crush on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/crush), [Models in OpenCode](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/opencode-models) and [AtomCode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/atomcode). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/atomcode

# AtomCode on any model

AtomCode is a Rust terminal coding agent on AtomGit (atomgit.com/atomgit_atomcode/atomcode). Its models live in `config.toml`: a `[models."…"]` table names a `[provider_accounts.…]` table, the shape AtomCode's own CodingPlan sign-in writes since 5.0.7. jianmu writes the same shape, a jianmu account and one table per model, so AtomCode can use any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up AtomCode

1. **Open jianmu's Agents page.** Find the AtomCode row. Its list has the models you set up in AtomCode yourself, and the ones via jianmu.
2. **Pick a jianmu model.** jianmu writes the account and model tables and points `default_provider` and `default_model` at your pick; with both set, AtomCode goes by `default_model`.
3. **Restart atomcode.** AtomCode reads its settings at start-up, so reopen any running session.

```
jianmu atomcode deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
jianmu atomcode effort high
```

## What jianmu writes

AtomCode's folder is `ATOMCODE_HOME` (an absolute path), else `~/.atomcode`. An AtomCode in WSL uses Linux's `~/.atomcode`, with the gateway as the distro reaches it. jianmu writes:

```
# ~/.atomcode/config.toml
default_provider = "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
default_model = "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"

[provider_accounts."jianmu"]
provider = "openai-compatible"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
api_key = "…"

[models."jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"]
account = "jianmu"
model = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
context_window = …
max_tokens = …
supports_vision = false
reasoning_effort_levels = ["…"]
```

The account uses `openai-compatible`, AtomCode's documented preset for a custom endpoint, at jianmu's gateway `/v1`, with a key jianmu issues to AtomCode alone. A model table's key is `jianmu/<provider>/<model>`, and its `model` goes to the gateway as written. Each carries the context window (AtomCode compacts as it nears it; 128000 when jianmu doesn't know it), the output limit (never above the window), image support and the effort levels on offer. When jianmu's models change, jianmu rewrites its own tables; your own model tables and legacy `providers.*` entries are left alone.

Requests are Chat Completions with Bearer auth and a User-Agent of `atomcode/<version>`; the key is AtomCode's own, so jianmu knows a request is AtomCode's even when the header is changed.

## Effort

Effort is the current model table's `reasoning_effort`, sent with every request to it and kept per model. jianmu picks none for you, so the vendor's default stands until you do. Only the levels that model supports (some of low, medium, high, xhigh, max) are offered.

## When it takes effect

AtomCode reads its settings at start-up. While atomcode is running, jianmu tells you to restart open atomcode sessions.

## Switching back

Switching back removes jianmu's account and model tables and puts back the `default_provider` and `default_model` you had before, where AtomCode still has that model (otherwise they go). Picking one of your own AtomCode models in jianmu also removes jianmu's tables.

```
jianmu atomcode default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in AtomCode?

On jianmu's Agents page, pick a via-jianmu model for AtomCode. jianmu adds [provider_accounts."jianmu"] and one [models."jianmu/…"] table per model to ~/.atomcode/config.toml and points the defaults at your pick.

### What context window does AtomCode get?

jianmu writes each model's context_window, or 128000 when it doesn't know it. AtomCode compacts as it nears the window.

### I changed it and AtomCode didn't notice. Why?

AtomCode reads its settings at start-up. Restart the open atomcode sessions.

### Do my own defaults come back when I switch back?

Yes. jianmu stashes default_provider and default_model when it steps in and puts them back when it steps out, where AtomCode still has that model.

More agents on the same models: [Reasonix Studio on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/reasonix), [jcode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/jcode), [Crush on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/crush) and [Shelley on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/shelley). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/shelley

# Shelley on any model

Shelley (boldsoftware/shelley) is the coding agent for exe.dev, a web app that `shelley serve` runs. Its models live in its database, not in a file jianmu can edit, so jianmu tells it through the same API Shelley's own Models and Profiles pages use: a custom model at jianmu's gateway, made the default. New Shelley conversations then run on any model you have in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Shelley

1. **Start Shelley first.** jianmu talks to a running Shelley. When it isn't running, jianmu says so: start `shelley serve` and try again.
2. **Pick a model on jianmu's Agents page.** Shelley's row lists the models Shelley can use itself and the ones via jianmu. Pick one of the latter.
3. **Start a new conversation.** New conversations start on the default profile's model, the one you just picked.

```
shelley serve                              # Shelley must be running
jianmu shelley deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## How jianmu tells Shelley

Shelley opens a Unix socket for its CLI: `$SHELLEY_SOCKET`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shelley/shelley.sock` (`~/.config/shelley` by default, on a Mac too), or `shelley-2.sock` and on when a second server took the first. jianmu tries them in the order Shelley's CLI does and calls `/api/custom-models` and `/api/profiles`:

```
POST /api/custom-models   (over ~/.config/shelley/shelley.sock)
{
  "display_name": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (jianmu)",
  "provider_type": "openai",
  "endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
  "api_key": "…",
  "model_name": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
  "reasoning_support": "yes",
  "image_support": "no",
  "max_tokens": …
}
```

Each model you pick in jianmu is a custom model of type openai at the gateway's `/v1` (Shelley adds `/chat/completions`), with a key jianmu issues to Shelley alone. Shelley usually learns reasoning and image support from models.dev by endpoint and name, which jianmu's models aren't in, so jianmu says what it knows. Then jianmu sets the default profile's `model` to it; for a model that doesn't reason it clears `thinking_level`, which Shelley would refuse.

jianmu keeps the ids of the models it made, so a model you made by hand at the gateway stays yours. When the gateway's address changes, jianmu updates its models.

## Which conversations change

New conversations use the new model; an open one keeps its model until you pick another in its model menu. jianmu says so after the switch.

## Switching back

Switching back puts the default profile's model and thinking level back to what they were (or to the server's default when that model can't be used any more), then deletes every custom model jianmu made. You can also pick one of Shelley's own models in jianmu. If Shelley was uninstalled, jianmu notes it and takes its models out when Shelley runs again.

```
jianmu shelley default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in Shelley?

Run shelley serve, then pick a via-jianmu model for Shelley on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds an openai custom model at its gateway to Shelley and makes it the default profile's model.

### Why does jianmu say Shelley isn't running?

Shelley's models are in its database, which jianmu changes only through a running Shelley's socket. Start shelley serve and try again.

### Why is an open conversation still on the old model?

The default profile applies to new conversations. Change an open one in its own model menu.

### Will my own custom models be deleted?

No. jianmu deletes only the model ids it made; one you made by hand, even at the gateway, stays yours.

More agents on the same models: [AtomCode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/atomcode), [Reasonix Studio on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/reasonix), [jcode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/jcode) and [Cindy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cindy). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cindy

# Cindy on any model

Cindy is a desktop app that runs Claude Code, Codex and Pi. It keeps its providers in its own database, their keys encrypted, and takes a new one only through its own import link, which you confirm in Cindy. So jianmu writes nothing into Cindy: it gives Cindy an import link with jianmu as one custom provider, an endpoint for each runtime. Claude Code, Codex and Pi in Cindy then run on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, and the ChatGPT or Copilot subscription you signed in to.

## Add jianmu to Cindy

1. **Open Cindy once.** Once Cindy has run, its data folder is there (`~/Library/Application Support/Cindy` on a Mac, `CindyGlobal` for its global build) and jianmu's Agents page lists it.
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Click Add jianmu.** On Cindy's row, click Add jianmu; jianmu hands the import link to Cindy.
4. **Confirm it in Cindy.** Nothing is added until you do. Then pick a model from the Jianmu provider for Claude Code, Codex or Pi in Cindy.

If nothing happens, nothing on this computer opens Cindy's links (`cindy://`), or the program that registered them was moved. jianmu checks for that first and says why instead of doing nothing: open Cindy once or install it again, then click again.

## What the link holds

The link's `data` is base64url-encoded JSON. Decoded, it is:

```
cindy://provider/import?v=1&data=
{
  "kind": "custom", "name": "Jianmu", "id": "jianmu",
  "auth": {"method": "apiKey", "apiKey": "…"},
  "endpoints": [
    {"protocol": "anthropic-messages", "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425",
     "targets": ["claude-code"], "modelsUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models"},
    {"protocol": "openai-responses", "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
     "targets": ["codex"], "modelsUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models"},
    {"protocol": "openai-chat", "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
     "targets": ["pi"], "modelsUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models"}
  ]
}
```

Claude Code speaks Anthropic Messages at the gateway itself; Codex speaks OpenAI Responses and Pi OpenAI Chat, both at the gateway's `/v1`. Each endpoint lists its models from the gateway's `/v1/models`, so a provider you add to jianmu later shows up when Cindy fetches models again.

## From the command line

```
jianmu cindy add      # opens Cindy to add jianmu; confirm it there
```

The command prints the link it opened. When nothing here can open it, it says why rather than reporting success.

## How jianmu knows it was added

jianmu reads Cindy's databases read-only: one per account (`cindy-<account>.db`) once you sign in, `cindy-local-v1.db` before. When any of them has a custom provider with the id or name jianmu, or the gateway's address in its endpoints, the row says it's added. It can read them while Cindy runs, and never writes them. When a database can't be read, jianmu says it doesn't know, not that it isn't added.

## Usage and keys

The key in the link is Cindy's own, so its requests are counted as Cindy's in jianmu's usage, apart from other agents.

## FAQ

### Can Claude Code in Cindy use DeepSeek or GLM?

Yes. Once jianmu is added to Cindy, Claude Code uses any model in jianmu, DeepSeek and GLM included, through the Jianmu provider's Anthropic endpoint.

### Does jianmu change Cindy's settings?

No. Cindy takes a new provider only through its own import link, which you confirm in Cindy. jianmu only reads Cindy's databases to show whether jianmu was added.

### Add jianmu does nothing. What now?

Nothing on this computer opens cindy:// links, or the program that registered them is gone. Open Cindy once or install it again, then click again; jianmu says which it is.

### Cindy isn't on jianmu's Agents page.

jianmu lists Cindy once it has run on this computer and made its data folder. Open Cindy once, then look again.

More desktop apps on the same models: [AionUi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aionui), [Every model in Cherry Studio, through jianmu](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cherry-studio), [Shelley on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/shelley) and [Lody on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/lody). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/lody

# Lody on any model

Lody is a desktop app that runs coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Pi, dsh, Kimi Code, Grok and Bub. It adds a provider through its own import link, in a dialog you confirm. jianmu gives it that link, with jianmu as one custom provider named Jianmu and three endpoints by protocol, covering every runtime it supports. Once confirmed, those agents in Lody run on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, an OpenAI or Anthropic key, and the ChatGPT or Copilot subscription you signed in to.

## Add jianmu to Lody

1. **Open Lody once.** Once Lody has run, its home folder `~/.lody` (`~/.lody-oss` for its OSS build) or data folder (`~/Library/Application Support/Lody` on a Mac) is there, and jianmu's Agents page lists it. Lody OSS and Lody Nightly count too.
2. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
3. **Click Add jianmu.** On Lody's row, click Add jianmu; jianmu hands the import link to Lody.
4. **Confirm it in Lody.** Lody shows its local provider dialog, and nothing is added until you confirm. Then pick a model from the Jianmu provider for each agent in Lody.

```
jianmu lody add      # opens Lody to add jianmu; confirm it there
```

The row never says it's added: Lody has no public status API, and jianmu doesn't guess from a click, files it generates or Lody's private store. Click again whenever you need to.

## What the link holds

The link's `data` is base64url-encoded JSON. Decoded, it is:

```
lody://provider/import?v=1&data=
{
  "kind": "custom", "id": "jianmu", "name": "Jianmu",
  "auth": {"method": "apiKey", "apiKey": "…"},
  "endpoints": [
    {"protocol": "anthropic-messages", "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425",
     "targets": ["claude-code"], "modelsUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models"},
    {"protocol": "openai-responses", "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
     "targets": ["codex"], "modelsUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models"},
    {"protocol": "openai-chat", "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
     "targets": ["pi", "dsh", "kimi-code", "grok", "bub"],
     "modelsUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models"}
  ]
}
```

Claude Code speaks Anthropic Messages at the gateway itself; Codex speaks OpenAI Responses; Pi, dsh, Kimi Code, Grok and Bub speak OpenAI Chat, all at the gateway's `/v1`. Every endpoint lists its models from the gateway's `/v1/models`.

## Loopback addresses only

Lody takes only HTTP on a loopback address (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), and only its public attribution token as the key, never a LAN key or a vendor credential. So when the gateway isn't on loopback, say you set jianmu's address to a LAN one, jianmu doesn't open Lody and says why.

## Lody on Linux

On macOS and Windows, Lody's bundle and installer claim `lody://` themselves, and jianmu opens the link. On Linux, Lody's AppImage makes itself the default only for its own channel's scheme and leaves `lody://` to the desktop database, which nothing builds without update-desktop-database, so xdg-open and browsers turn the link away (“failed to open uri”). So on Linux jianmu runs Lody with the link, as its desktop entry (`ai.lody.desktop`, or the Nightly or OSS one) says; a Lody already running takes the link and the second one quits. With no entry of Lody's, it hands the link to the system.

## Usage and keys

The key in the link is Lody's own, so its requests are counted as Lody's in jianmu's usage, apart from other agents.

## FAQ

### Can Claude Code in Lody use DeepSeek or GLM?

Yes. Once jianmu is added to Lody, Claude Code uses any model in jianmu, DeepSeek and GLM included, through the Jianmu provider's Anthropic endpoint; Codex, Pi, Kimi Code and the rest do the same.

### Why does jianmu say Lody takes only a loopback address?

Lody accepts HTTP providers on loopback only. Set jianmu's gateway address back to 127.0.0.1 or localhost, then click Add jianmu again.

### On Linux, Add jianmu says failed to open uri.

That is xdg-open finding no handler for lody://. jianmu runs Lody from its desktop entry instead; if that still fails, open Lody once so it writes its entry, then click again.

### Why doesn't Lody's row say it's added?

Lody has no public status API, and jianmu doesn't guess. Once you've confirmed, Jianmu is in Lody's provider list.

More desktop apps on the same models: [Cindy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cindy), [AionUi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aionui), [Shelley on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/shelley) and [Empryo on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/empryo). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/empryo

# Empryo on any model

Empryo keeps its settings in `~/.empryo/config.json` (a project's `.empryo/config.json` goes over it). Its providers are a `providers` array of OpenAI-compatible endpoints that it lists models from and sends `/chat/completions` to. jianmu adds a provider of its own there and sets the model sessions start on to one of jianmu's. Empryo then runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Empryo

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Empryo on the Agents page.** Empryo's row lists your current Empryo model and the models via jianmu. Pick one of the latter.
3. **Restart empryo.** Empryo reads its settings at start-up, so reopen sessions that are already open.

```
jianmu empryo deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

On Windows, Empryo in a WSL distro is found too and set up the same way, at a gateway address that distro can reach.

## What gets written

```
{
  "providers": [
    …your own providers, left as they are…,
    {"id": "jianmu", "name": "Jianmu",
     "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
     "modelsAPI": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/models"}
  ],
  "defaultModel": "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
}
```

`defaultModel` is `<provider id>/<model id>`, split at the first `/`, so `jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` is `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` under the jianmu provider. Your own providers and other settings stay as they are.

jianmu checks the wiring: when config.json's jianmu provider is gone, or its `baseURL` isn't the gateway's address any more, Empryo's row says so.

## Why there is no envVar

An Empryo provider can name an `envVar` to read its key from; with none, Empryo sends no key of yours. jianmu's provider has none, so you put no key in your environment. With no `envVar`, Empryo lists a provider only when its `baseURL` answers (2xx, 401 or 403), which the gateway's `GET /v1` does.

## When it takes effect

Empryo reads its settings only at start-up. While empryo is running, jianmu reminds you to restart open empryo sessions.

## Switching back

Switching back puts `defaultModel` back to what it was and removes the jianmu provider. If jianmu made config.json and nothing is left in it, the file goes too. You can also pick your own Empryo model again.

```
jianmu empryo default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in Empryo?

Pick a via-jianmu model for Empryo on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds a provider with id jianmu to ~/.empryo/config.json and sets defaultModel to jianmu/provider/model. Restart empryo to use it.

### Do I need an API key environment variable?

No. jianmu's provider has no envVar, so Empryo sends no key of yours; the jianmu gateway forwards requests to the providers you added in jianmu.

### Does a project's .empryo/config.json matter?

Yes. A project's .empryo/config.json goes over ~/.empryo/config.json; if it sets its own defaultModel, that one wins in that project.

### Is my old model still there after switching back?

Yes. jianmu kept the defaultModel you had and puts it back; your own providers were never changed.

More agents on the same models: [Lody on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/lody), [AtomCode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/atomcode), [Crush on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/crush) and [miniQ on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/miniq). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/miniq

# miniQ on any model

miniQ is a desktop AI coworker with a `miniq` terminal client, both clients of one miniq-daemon. Its models come from one OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, the `provider` in `settings.json`. jianmu makes that provider the local gateway, so miniQ runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up miniQ

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for miniQ on the Agents page.** miniQ's row lists your current miniQ model and the models via jianmu. Pick one of the latter.
3. **Keep working.** A running daemon is told the new provider, and open chats move onto the new model, with no restart.

```
jianmu miniq deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

On Windows, miniQ in a WSL distro is found too and set up the same way.

## Where settings.json is

`settings.json` sits in the daemon's data folder, found as miniQ finds it. `MINIQ_DATA_DIR` comes first. Next is the folder named by `miniq-data-dir.json` beside the default, which exists when you moved the data folder in miniQ's Settings. Otherwise it is the default. macOS uses `~/.local/share/miniq` too.

```
macOS / Linux: ~/.local/share/miniq/settings.json
Windows:       %LOCALAPPDATA%\miniq\settings.json
MINIQ_DATA_DIR set: $MINIQ_DATA_DIR/settings.json
```

## What gets written

```
{
  "provider": {
    "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
    "apiKey": "",
    "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
    "apiProtocol": "chat_completions"
  }
}
```

`baseUrl` is the gateway's `/v1`. `apiKey` is jianmu's own key for miniQ: miniQ sends no User-Agent of its own, so the key is how jianmu knows the request is miniQ's. `model` is the model's catalog id. `apiProtocol` is `chat_completions`, because `auto` would guess Responses or Anthropic Messages from a model's name.

jianmu changes only `provider`. It stashes your own provider whole. The rest of settings.json stays as it is: MCP servers, approvals, hooks and remote access. Where there is no file, jianmu makes one with 0600 permissions, as miniQ does.

## A running daemon

The daemon reads settings.json once, when it starts, and writes its own copy back on every settings change. So after writing the file, jianmu also calls `settings.update` over the local WebSocket that `daemon.json` names, as miniQ's own Settings does. A daemon jianmu can't reach keeps the old provider until it restarts. jianmu then asks you to restart miniQ.

## Switching back

Switching back puts your own provider back whole and tells the daemon. If you had no provider, jianmu removes its own, and miniQ goes back to its default. If jianmu made settings.json and nothing is left in it, the file goes too. You can also pick your own miniQ model in jianmu; it goes into your restored provider.

```
jianmu miniq default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in miniQ?

Pick a via-jianmu model for miniQ on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu sets settings.json's provider to the local gateway's /v1 and tells the running miniq-daemon.

### Do I need to restart miniQ?

Usually not. jianmu tells a running daemon through settings.update, and open chats move onto the new model. Only a daemon jianmu can't reach needs a restart, and jianmu says so.

### Why chat_completions and not auto?

auto guesses the protocol from a model's name and could pick Responses or Anthropic Messages. The gateway's /v1 speaks Chat Completions, so jianmu names it.

### Are my MCP servers and other settings changed?

No. jianmu changes only settings.json's provider, and switching back restores the one you had.

More agents on the same models: [Empryo on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/empryo), [Lody on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/lody), [Cindy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cindy) and [OpenBot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openbot). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openbot

# OpenBot on any model

OpenBot is an Electron workspace that runs Codex, Claude, OpenCode and other agents. Its model picker lists the OpenAI-compatible endpoints you add yourself. jianmu adds one named jianmu, so the picker lists the models in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up OpenBot

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Set OpenBot's provider to jianmu on the Agents page.** jianmu writes its endpoint into OpenBot's custom endpoints file.
3. **Restart OpenBot and pick a model in its own picker.** jianmu's models show as `jianmu/<id>`.

```
jianmu openbot provider jianmu
```

## Where the file is

OpenBot keeps custom endpoints in Electron's userData folder:

```
macOS:   ~/Library/Application Support/OpenBot/openbot-custom-providers-v1.json
Windows: %APPDATA%\OpenBot\openbot-custom-providers-v1.json
Linux:   ~/.config/OpenBot/openbot-custom-providers-v1.json
```

## What gets written

```
{
  "version": 1,
  "providers": [
    …your own endpoints, left as they are…,
    {
      "id": "jianmu",
      "name": "jianmu",
      "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/agent/openbot/v1",
      "models": [
        {"id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Pro", "contextWindow": 1000000},
        …
      ],
      "secret": null
    }
  ]
}
```

`version` must be 1. A file OpenBot can't parse leaves it with no endpoints and refuses every save, so jianmu leaves alone a file it can't read either.

OpenBot keeps each endpoint's key and headers together in `secret`, sealed with Electron's safeStorage (the Keychain, DPAPI). jianmu doesn't open it, so jianmu's endpoint has no key (`secret` is `null`). OpenBot hands it to OpenCode keyless, and the gateway takes a request with no key from this computer.

OpenCode sends the requests, with OpenCode's User-Agent. The `/agent/openbot` in the address tells the gateway they are OpenBot's, and they are counted as OpenBot's. A name, harness or key you give jianmu's endpoint in OpenBot stays. Your other endpoints stay as written.

## Which models show

OpenBot's list check fails closed: one endpoint or model it wouldn't accept empties the whole list. So jianmu writes only the models picked for OpenBot in jianmu, and:

1. **At most 64.** That is OpenBot's limit for one endpoint; a longer list hides them all.
2. **Ids OpenBot accepts.** ASCII letters, digits and `._:/[],=-`, at most 160 characters with the `jianmu/` prefix.
3. **Context windows in range.** contextWindow is written only between 1,024 and 100,000,000.

## When it takes effect

OpenBot reads the file once, when it starts. It writes the file whole from what it holds only when an endpoint is saved, edited or removed there. So a change shows after a restart. An endpoint saved in OpenBot before the restart writes jianmu's endpoint out again. While OpenBot is running, jianmu reminds you to restart it before adding or editing an endpoint there.

MCP servers live in OpenBot's SQLite database, which jianmu doesn't write. To use jianmu's own MCP servers (`/mcp/jianmu/…`), add them in OpenBot by hand as HTTP servers.

## Switching back

Switching back removes only jianmu's endpoint. When nothing else is left in the file, jianmu removes the file, since OpenBot starts with an empty list without one.

```
jianmu openbot default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in OpenBot?

Set OpenBot's provider to jianmu on jianmu's Agents page, restart OpenBot, then pick a jianmu/ model in its model picker.

### Why does jianmu's endpoint have no API key?

OpenBot seals each endpoint's key with the system keychain, which jianmu doesn't open. The gateway takes keyless requests from this computer, and /agent/openbot in the address tells it they are OpenBot's.

### Why don't I see every jianmu model?

jianmu writes only the models picked for OpenBot, at most 64, and skips ids OpenBot wouldn't accept. One bad model would make OpenBot empty the whole list.

### Why hasn't the change shown up?

OpenBot reads custom endpoints only at start-up, so restart it. Don't save an endpoint in OpenBot before that, or it writes jianmu's endpoint out.

More desktop apps on the same models: [Lody on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/lody), [Cindy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cindy), [miniQ on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/miniq) and [Tuanjie Cowork on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tuanjie-cowork). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tuanjie-cowork

# Tuanjie Cowork on any model

Tuanjie Cowork is Unity China's AI coworker app, whose core runs Codely sessions. The Custom Models in its Settings are kept in `~/.codely/settings.json`. jianmu adds a provider and a model of its own there, so Cowork runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Tuanjie Cowork

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Tuanjie Cowork on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu; jianmu writes it into Cowork's custom models.
3. **Pick it in Cowork's model menu.** Once, as below.

```
jianmu tuanjie-cowork deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## What gets written

```
{
  "customModelProviders": [
    …your own providers, left as they are…,
    {"id": "jianmu", "name": "jianmu",
     "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
     "apiKey": "",
     "authType": "openai"}
  ],
  "customModels": [
    …your own models…,
    {"id": "jianmu", "providerId": "jianmu",
     "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
     "displayName": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
     "roles": ["model"], "wireApi": "chat",
     "supportsMultimodal": false}
  ]
}
```

The provider and the model both have the id `jianmu`. The provider is the gateway's `/v1` with jianmu's own key for Tuanjie Cowork, which is how the gateway knows the requests are Cowork's. The model is on Chat Completions (`wireApi` `chat`), with `supportsMultimodal` true when the model takes images.

Cowork reads the file afresh on every lookup and writes it whole, other keys kept. A session is started with its provider's `baseUrl` and key as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Your own providers and models stay as they are, and so does a name, roles or another field you give jianmu's entries in Cowork. Where there is no file, jianmu makes one with 0600 permissions, since it holds keys.

If you have a provider or a model of your own with the id `jianmu`, or the file isn't settings Cowork reads, jianmu says so and leaves the file alone. Cowork's start-up migrations only move models with no `providerId`, so jianmu's entries are left alone.

## Picking it in Cowork

Which model a chat is on is Cowork's own pick in its model menu, kept per workspace by model id. jianmu doesn't write that pick, so the first time you pick jianmu's model in Cowork's menu. The model's id stays `jianmu`, so a model you change in jianmu later is the one that pick sends, with no new pick.

While Cowork is running, jianmu reminds you to pick its model in the model menu, and to restart Tuanjie Cowork if it isn't there yet.

## Switching back

Switching back removes jianmu's provider and model. If jianmu made settings.json and nothing else is left in it, the file goes too. Your own models are picked in Cowork's model menu; jianmu doesn't set them.

```
jianmu tuanjie-cowork default
```

## FAQ

### How do I use DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription in Tuanjie Cowork?

Pick a via-jianmu model for Tuanjie Cowork on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds a jianmu provider and model to ~/.codely/settings.json. Then pick it once in Cowork's model menu.

### After changing the model in jianmu, do I pick it again in Cowork?

No. jianmu's model id is always jianmu, so Cowork's pick stays on it and sends the model you picked in jianmu.

### Are my own custom models changed?

No. jianmu adds and removes only entries with the id jianmu. If you have one of your own with that id, jianmu says so and leaves the file alone.

### jianmu's model isn't in the model menu. What now?

Restart Tuanjie Cowork. While it runs, jianmu says so too.

More desktop apps on the same models: [OpenBot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openbot), [miniQ on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/miniq), [Cindy on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cindy) and [DS Bot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ds-bot). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ds-bot

# DS Bot on any model

DS Bot (once DeepSeek Bot) is an Electron desktop app built on DSH. It ships its own DSH and runs the profile `ds-bot` on a data folder of its own, and its models are that DSH's llm-pi-ai routes. jianmu adds a route of its own there, so DS Bot runs on any model in jianmu: GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription, and DeepSeek too.

## Set up DS Bot

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for DS Bot on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu; jianmu writes its route and key into DS Bot's data folder.
3. **Make a new Bot in DS Bot.** New Bots start on that model, as below.

```
jianmu ds-bot deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

This is the DS Bot desktop app. DS Bot is also a DSH plugin: in DSH Desktop or `dsh web` it runs on `~/.dsh`, and its model follows jianmu's DSH row.

## Where the data folder is

jianmu looks for the data folder in DS Bot's own order:

1. **`DS_BOT_HOME`.** When it is set, as for a throwaway folder.
2. **`dataDir` in locations.json.** In Electron's userData: `DS_BOT_SHELL_DATA`, else `<config dir>/DS Bot`. The older `<config dir>/DeepSeek Bot` is used when it exists and DS Bot's folder has no locations.json.
3. **`~/.ds-bot`.** When there is no locations.json, the first run's default.

When locations.json can't be read, or has no `dataDir`, jianmu counts the folder as unknown and touches none.

## What gets written

```
/
  .env                              ← jianmu's key for DS Bot
  profiles/ds-bot/cordis.patch.yml  ← jianmu's llm-pi-ai route
  (DSH's key store)                 ← the same key
  agent-default-model               ← the model you picked
```

As for DSH: jianmu puts its route in the profile's patch list, `profiles/ds-bot/cordis.patch.yml`, the key in `.env` and DSH's key store, and sets agent-default-model. Your own routes stay as they are.

## New Bots and older ones

New Bots in DS Bot start on DSH's agent-default-model, so a Bot you make now is on the model you picked in jianmu, unless a default model for Bots is set in DS Bot. A Bot made before keeps its own model until you pick another for it. jianmu says so on the Agents page.

## Web search

DS Bot's web search goes through jianmu too. When jianmu has nothing to search with yet, it asks you to set up a provider that searches by itself (DeepSeek, Claude, Codex, …) or a search API under Settings › Web search.

## Before DS Bot is opened

You can set it up before DS Bot is ever opened; jianmu says it starts on this the first time it opens. DS Bot's first open writes the profile's files only where they are missing, so the patch list jianmu made is kept.

## Switching back

Switching back takes jianmu's route out. For a DS Bot that was never opened, jianmu removes the files it made.

```
jianmu ds-bot default
```

## FAQ

### Can DS Bot use models other than DeepSeek?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for DS Bot on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds a route to the DSH that DS Bot ships, so GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude, GPT or a ChatGPT subscription all work.

### Why are my existing Bots still on the old model?

A Bot made before keeps its own model. New Bots start on the default jianmu sets; pick another model for an older Bot in DS Bot.

### I moved DS Bot's data folder. Does jianmu find it?

Yes. jianmu reads dataDir from DS Bot's locations.json. When it can't be read, jianmu changes no folder.

### What about the DS Bot plugin in DSH Desktop?

The plugin runs on ~/.dsh, so its model follows jianmu's DSH row: pick a model for DSH on the Agents page.

More desktop apps on the same models: [Tuanjie Cowork on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tuanjie-cowork), [OpenBot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openbot), [miniQ on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/miniq) and [OpenHanako on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openhanako). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/prime-agent

# Prime Agent on any model

Prime Agent is Prime Intellect's open-source coding agent in Rust, the `prime-agent` command. It keeps Pi's settings.json and models.json in a folder of its own and reads them with Pi's fields and types. jianmu sets it up as it does [Pi](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi), so Prime Agent runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Prime Agent

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Prime Agent on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu.
3. **Run prime-agent.** A new session starts on that model, with every model of jianmu's in its list.

```
jianmu prime-agent deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## What gets written

```
~/.prime/agent/            (or $PRIME_AGENT_CODING_AGENT_DIR)
  settings.json            defaultProvider: "jianmu"
                           defaultModel:    "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
                           defaultThinkingLevel
  models.json              providers.jianmu: the gateway's /v1,
                           the key jianmu-prime-agent, jianmu's models
```

jianmu adds a provider named `jianmu` to models.json, at the gateway's `/v1` with jianmu's models, and sets `defaultProvider`, `defaultModel` and `defaultThinkingLevel` in settings.json. Your own providers and settings stay as they are.

Prime Agent's requests carry no User-Agent, so the key jianmu gives it names it, `jianmu-prime-agent`: that is how the gateway counts its requests as Prime Agent's.

## PRIME_AGENT_CODING_AGENT_DIR

Prime Agent's folder is `~/.prime/agent`, or `$PRIME_AGENT_CODING_AGENT_DIR` when it is set, `~` in it standing for home. A relative path is its working directory's, which jianmu can't know, so it isn't taken and jianmu writes `~/.prime/agent`. A Prime Agent in WSL is set up too.

## Settings left to you

Only the global settings.json is written, as for Pi. These are yours, and jianmu doesn't change them:

1. **A project's `.prime/agent/settings.json`.** Settings for that project.
2. **`allowedModels`.** Its daemon's allow-list; a model outside it fails loudly.
3. **`subagentDefaultModel`.** The model subagents start on.

So if you keep allowedModels, add jianmu's model to it.

## Switching back

Pick one of your own models on Prime Agent's row, or run the command below. jianmu copied both files before its first write: if nothing changed since, they go back byte for byte; otherwise only jianmu's provider is removed.

```
jianmu prime-agent default
```

## FAQ

### Can Prime Agent run on DeepSeek or GLM?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for Prime Agent on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds its provider to models.json, so DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen and Claude all work.

### Which folder does jianmu write to?

~/.prime/agent, or PRIME_AGENT_CODING_AGENT_DIR when it is set, with ~ expanded. A relative path isn't taken.

### jianmu's model fails as not allowed. Why?

Your allowedModels doesn't list it. jianmu leaves that list to you; add the model to it.

### How does jianmu know Prime Agent's requests?

By the key jianmu gives it, jianmu-prime-agent, since its requests carry no User-Agent.

More agents on the same models: [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi), [Kimi Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi-code), [DS Bot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ds-bot) and [Muse Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/muse-code). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openhanako

# OpenHanako on any model

OpenHanako (HanaAgent) is a desktop personal agent that keeps what it knows in `~/.hanako`, or the folder `$HANA_HOME` names. jianmu adds a provider, `jianmu`, there and makes your pick the primary agent's chat model, so OpenHanako runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up OpenHanako
