1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Open OpenHanako once.** It makes its agent the first time. Until it has one, jianmu asks you to open it.
3. **Pick a model for OpenHanako on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu; the primary agent chats on it.

```
jianmu hanako deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## What gets written

```
~/.hanako/                       (or $HANA_HOME)
  provider-catalog.json          providers.jianmu: the gateway's /v1,
                                 api openai-completions, jianmu's key, models
  provider-plugins/jianmu/...    the same provider, once OpenHanako moves it
  agents//config.yaml        models.chat: {id, provider: jianmu}
```

jianmu is one provider in OpenHanako, `jianmu`, spoken to as Chat Completions (`openai-completions`) at the gateway's `/v1`, with jianmu's catalog as its models: each with its context, max output, and whether it takes images and reasons. OpenHanako runs on Pi's SDK, so the effort goes as `reasoning_effort`.

The model set is the primary agent's `models.chat`: `primaryAgent` in `user/preferences.json`, else the first agent with a config, as OpenHanako picks at start-up.

## Changes while it runs

While OpenHanako runs, jianmu adds its provider and changes the chat model through OpenHanako's local API, which saves them and reloads its models at once, with no restart. Otherwise jianmu writes the files, which OpenHanako reads when it starts.

## The sealed catalog

Since 1.0 OpenHanako seals its provider catalog under a key kept in the system keychain: the file is then `HANA-SECRET-1.AES-256-GCM.…`, not JSON. jianmu can't read it or write it, and never writes over it.

A provider's definition is in its plugin file under `provider-plugins/jianmu`, out of the catalog, so jianmu still keeps that up to date; its key stays sealed. Adding or removing jianmu needs OpenHanako running, to do it through its API. When it isn't, jianmu says to open OpenHanako and try again.

## Switching back

jianmu stashes the primary agent's model when it first steps in and puts it back when it steps out. With none stashed, or one OpenHanako no longer has, the agent goes to the first of OpenHanako's own models, as since 1.0 its API takes no agent without a model. Then jianmu's provider is removed.

```
jianmu hanako default
```

## FAQ

### Can OpenHanako run on DeepSeek, GLM or Kimi?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for OpenHanako on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds the jianmu provider and makes it the primary agent's chat model.

### jianmu says OpenHanako keeps its providers encrypted. What now?

Since 1.0 OpenHanako seals its catalog, so jianmu can change it only through its API while it runs. Open OpenHanako and try again.

### Do I restart OpenHanako for the change?

Not while it runs: jianmu goes through its local API and the models reload at once. When it isn't running, the change is there the next time it opens.

### Does switching back give me my old model?

Yes. jianmu stashed it and puts it back; if OpenHanako no longer has it, the agent goes to OpenHanako's first model of its own.

More desktop apps on the same models: [DS Bot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ds-bot), [Tuanjie Cowork on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tuanjie-cowork), [OpenBot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openbot) and [Kun on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kun). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kun

# Kun on any model

Kun (KunAgent) is a local-first AI workbench: a desktop app (Code, Work, chats, agents) and a `kun` TUI, both clients of one runtime, `kun serve`. Its models come from the runtime's model connections. jianmu adds a connection of its own and makes it the default, so Kun runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription, in the desktop app and the TUI alike.

## Set up Kun

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Open Kun.** jianmu adds its connection through the running Kun, as below.
3. **Pick a model for Kun on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu; it becomes Kun's default.

```
jianmu kun deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## Through Kun's own API

Kun keeps its connections in `model-connections.v2.json` in its data folder (`$KUN_DATA_DIR`, else `~/.kun/data`), and a connection's key in its protected credential store, so a connection can't be written into a file by hand. jianmu adds and removes its connection as Kun's own Settings › Providers and its `kun provider` command do, through the runtime's admin API:

```
GET    /v1/model-connections              the connections, with a revision
POST   /v1/model-connections/connect      jianmu's connection
PATCH  /v1/model-connections/jianmu       its model list
POST   /v1/model-connections/select       Kun's default model
DELETE /v1/model-connections/jianmu       switching back
```

The address and token come from `runtime.json` in the data folder. jianmu's connection, `jianmu`, is an HTTP one at the gateway's `/v1`, spoken to as Chat Completions with jianmu's own key for Kun. jianmu remembers its id, so one you renamed to jianmu-2 in Kun is still jianmu's.

## The model list

The connection's models are the ones you tick for Kun on jianmu's Agents page, at most 500. A model picked or dropped there reaches the connection, and so does a gateway on a new port.

## Kun has to be running

Kun adds and changes model providers only while it runs. When it isn't running, jianmu says to open Kun, then try again.

## Switching back

jianmu stashes the default Kun had when it first steps in. Switching back picks that default again, then removes jianmu's connection. With no provider of your own in Kun to go back to, jianmu asks you to add one in Kun's Settings › Providers.

```
jianmu kun default
```

## FAQ

### Can Kun run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Open Kun and pick a via-jianmu model for Kun on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds a jianmu model connection and makes it the default.

### jianmu says open Kun, then try again. Why?

Kun takes provider changes only while it runs. Open the Kun desktop app or kun serve, and try again.

### Does the kun TUI get the models too?

Yes. The desktop app and the kun TUI are both clients of kun serve and share its model connections.

### Does switching back restore my default model?

Yes. jianmu stashed the default Kun had, picks it again, then removes its connection.

More desktop apps on the same models: [OpenHanako on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openhanako), [DS Bot on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ds-bot), [Tuanjie Cowork on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/tuanjie-cowork) and [Alma on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/alma). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/alma

# Alma on any model

Alma is a desktop AI chat app that keeps its providers and settings in the app, not in a file jianmu can edit. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu through the local API Alma serves while it runs, and makes it the default model, so Alma runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Alma

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Open Alma.** jianmu can change Alma's settings only through a running Alma. When it isn't open, jianmu says to open Alma and try again.
3. **Pick a model for Alma on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu; it becomes Alma's default model.

```
jianmu alma deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## Through Alma's local API

While it runs, Alma serves a local API at `http://localhost:23001`, and that is what jianmu uses:

```
GET  /api/providers              Alma's providers
POST /api/providers              jianmu's provider
PUT  /api/providers/:id/models   its model list
GET  /api/settings, PUT it back  chat.defaultModel, imageGen.model
```

jianmu's provider is of type openai at the gateway's `/v1`, with jianmu's own key for Alma. Alma's requests carry only the AI SDK's User-Agent, so the key is how the gateway knows them for Alma's. The default model is `chat.defaultModel`, as `providerId:model`; Alma takes only the whole settings, so jianmu puts the rest back as they were.

## Models and thinking levels

Alma works out a model's capabilities from models.dev by its id, and jianmu's ids (codex/gpt-5.5) aren't models.dev's, so such a model would show no thinking. jianmu tells Alma each model's capabilities: a model that reasons comes with the thinking levels Alma knows, and its window, output limit and images when jianmu knows them. One you set yourself in Alma's model options (tool calling) stays as you set it. Models added or dropped in jianmu reach Alma while it is open.

## Image generation

When jianmu has an image model and Alma's image generation model is Auto, picking one of jianmu's models for Alma makes jianmu's image model Alma's too. An image model you picked is left as it is.

## Switching back

Switching back clears Alma's default model when it is jianmu's, leaving it to Alma, puts an image generation model of jianmu's back to Auto, and removes jianmu's provider. If Alma has been uninstalled, jianmu remembers, and takes its provider out once Alma is installed again and answers.

```
jianmu alma default
```

## FAQ

### Can Alma run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Open Alma and pick a via-jianmu model for Alma on jianmu's Agents page. jianmu adds a jianmu provider and makes it the default model.

### jianmu says Alma isn't running. Why?

Alma's settings change only through the local API it serves while it runs. Open Alma and try again.

### Why do jianmu's models have thinking levels in Alma?

jianmu tells Alma each model's capabilities: whether it reasons, its thinking levels and its window.

### What happens when I switch back?

jianmu's provider is removed, a default model of jianmu's is cleared for Alma to pick, and the image generation model goes back to Auto.

More desktop apps on the same models: [Kun on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kun), [Every model in Cherry Studio, through jianmu](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cherry-studio), [OpenHanako on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openhanako) and [OpenPencil on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openpencil). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/openpencil

# OpenPencil on any model

OpenPencil (ZSeven-W/openpencil, the openpencil-desktop app) is a design canvas whose chat runs models through builtin agents of your own: an Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible endpoint, a key and a list of models, each listed in the chat's model picker. jianmu adds an entry named jianmu, so OpenPencil runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up OpenPencil

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Quit OpenPencil.** Why is below.
3. **Pick jianmu for OpenPencil on the Agents page.** Then tick the models it should list.
4. **Open OpenPencil and pick a jianmu model in its chat's model picker.** The model is picked in OpenPencil, not in a file.

```
jianmu openpencil jianmu
```

## The entry in settings.json

OpenPencil keeps its settings in one settings.json:

```
macOS    ~/Library/Application Support/openpencil/settings.json
Linux    ~/.config/openpencil/settings.json   ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME)
Windows  %APPDATA%\openpencil\settings.json
```

jianmu writes one entry of `builtin_agents`, id `jianmu`, of kind openai-compat, which posts to `/chat/completions` under the gateway's `/v1`. OpenPencil's User-Agent isn't known, so the gateway tells its requests apart by the key `jianmu-openpencil`:

```
{"version": 1,
 "builtin_agents": [{"id": "jianmu", "preset": "custom", "display_name": "jianmu",
   "kind": "openai-compat", "api_key": "jianmu-openpencil",
   "model": "", "models": ["", …],
   "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1", "enabled": true}]}
```

Your other entries and settings stay, and so do the name and the on/off you give jianmu's entry in OpenPencil. `version` has to be 1: without it OpenPencil sets the file aside as corrupt and then refuses to save at all. So jianmu writes version 1 in a file it makes, and leaves alone a file whose version it doesn't know.

## Quit OpenPencil first

OpenPencil reads settings.json once, when it starts, and writes all of it back from what it holds when a setting changes and when it quits. A change jianmu makes while it runs is written over when it quits, so jianmu refuses one then and says to quit OpenPencil and try again. On Windows, where jianmu can't tell it is running, a notice asks you to quit it first.

## The model list

The entry's models are the ones you tick for OpenPencil on jianmu's Agents page, each once, at most 64 (OpenPencil drops the rest when it next saves). The `models` list is written for two or more, with the first again as `model`; v0.8.4 knows only `model`, so it lists the first model alone. Changes in jianmu are synced to it.

## Switching back

Switching back takes jianmu's entry out of `builtin_agents`, and the file too when all that is left is the version and empty list jianmu wrote. Quit OpenPencil first here too.

```
jianmu openpencil default
```

open-pencil/open-pencil, the other app of the name, keeps its providers in its webview's localStorage, which jianmu can't write. It reaches jianmu through an agent jianmu sets up (Pi, an ACP agent) or a base URL typed in.

## FAQ

### Can OpenPencil run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Quit OpenPencil, pick jianmu for it on jianmu's Agents page, then open OpenPencil and pick a jianmu model in its chat's model picker.

### Why quit OpenPencil first?

OpenPencil writes its whole settings back to settings.json when it quits, over what jianmu wrote while it ran.

### Why does OpenPencil show only one jianmu model?

OpenPencil v0.8.4 reads only the model field, so it lists the first model; later versions read the models list, up to 64.

### Are my other builtin agents kept when I switch back?

Yes. jianmu removes only the entry with id jianmu and leaves the rest as it was.

More desktop apps on the same models: [Alma on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/alma), [Kun on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kun) and [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/muse-code

# Muse Code on any model

Muse Code is Meta's `muse` coding agent CLI. Where its requests go is `endpoint_transport` in its settings.json, and the model sessions start on is the top-level `model`. jianmu points both at the gateway, so Muse Code runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Muse Code

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Muse Code on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu.
3. **Restart open muse sessions.** Muse Code reads its settings at start-up.

```
jianmu muse deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## settings.json

Muse Code keeps its settings in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/muse/settings.json`, and refuses the file without `"schema_version": 1`. jianmu writes:

```
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "endpoint_transport": {
    "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
    "auth": "none"
  },
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
}
```

Muse Code streams to `/responses` under `base_url` (OpenAI's Responses API), where the gateway answers. The file's other keys are left as they are. With no file, jianmu makes one with the schema version. Muse Code in a WSL distro is set up the same way, in `~/.config/muse` there.

## Why auth is none

With `auth` `bearer`, Muse Code sends the Meta sign-in's token (auth.json, or META_API_KEY); with `none` it sends no Authorization and asks for no sign-in. jianmu uses none, so your Meta token is neither read by jianmu nor sent to the gateway.

## The model list

Muse Code lists its models from `/muse-code/models` on `base_url`'s host, which the gateway serves, so jianmu's models show in Muse Code's model choice.

## Switching back

When it first steps in, jianmu stashes the `endpoint_transport` and `model` you had. Switching back puts them back, or takes jianmu's out where you had none. A file jianmu made goes again once only the schema version is left.

```
jianmu muse default
```

## FAQ

### Can Muse Code run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for Muse Code on jianmu's Agents page, then restart open muse sessions.

### Does jianmu read my Meta sign-in token?

No. jianmu sets auth to none, so Muse Code sends no Authorization; the token is neither read nor sent to the gateway.

### Nothing changed in Muse Code. Why?

Muse Code reads settings.json at start-up. Restart open muse sessions.

### Does switching back restore my settings?

Yes. jianmu stashed the endpoint_transport and model you had and puts them back; the file's other keys were never touched.

More agents on the same models: [Prime Agent on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/prime-agent), [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi), [Kimi Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/kimi-code) and [Paimon on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/paimon). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/paimon

# Paimon on any model

Paimon (aisk/paimon, installed with `uv tool install paimon`) is a coding agent in the terminal, built on pydantic-ai. Its settings are one JSON file: the model is `provider:name`, and each provider keeps its own address and key. jianmu adds a provider at the gateway, so Paimon runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Paimon

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Paimon on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu.
3. **Restart Paimon.** Paimon reads its settings when it starts, so a running one keeps its model until it starts again.

```
jianmu paimon deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## config.json

The file is `$PAIMON_CONFIG_HOME/config.json`, else `~/.config/paimon/config.json` (on Windows too). jianmu changes three things:

```
{
  "model": "litellm:deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
  "providers": {
    "litellm": {
      "api_base": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
      "api_key": ""
    }
  },
  "compaction": { "context_window": 1000000 }
}
```

A model is sent with its own provider's key only. The rest of the file is left alone; with no file, jianmu makes one readable by you alone (it holds keys), as Paimon makes it. Paimon in a WSL distro is set up the same way.

## Why litellm

jianmu uses pydantic-ai's litellm provider, an OpenAI-compatible proxy that profiles a `vendor/model` name by its vendor, as jianmu's ids are spelled. Paimon's login doesn't offer it, so it is almost never one of your own. The gateway knows the provider for jianmu's by jianmu's own key for Paimon.

## Context window and compaction

For a name genai-prices doesn't know, which jianmu's ids aren't, Paimon compacts against `compaction.context_window` only, and doesn't compact at all without it. So jianmu writes the window it knows the model to take; for a model whose window it doesn't know, your own value, never the last model's.

## Switching back

When it first steps in, jianmu stashes the model, providers.litellm and compaction.context_window you had. Switching back puts all three back, takes out the empty objects it left, and removes a file it made once nothing is left in it. A model you picked in Paimon since, on a provider of your own, counts as yours and is the one put back.

```
jianmu paimon default
```

## FAQ

### Can Paimon run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for Paimon on jianmu's Agents page, then restart Paimon.

### Why does the model in config.json start with litellm:?

jianmu goes through pydantic-ai's litellm provider, an OpenAI-compatible proxy that reads jianmu's vendor/model ids.

### Does Paimon still compact its context?

Yes. jianmu writes the model's context window, which Paimon compacts against; without it Paimon doesn't compact.

### Does switching back restore my settings?

Yes. jianmu stashed the model, litellm provider and context window you had and puts them back; the rest of the file was never touched.

More agents on the same models: [Muse Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/muse-code), [Prime Agent on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/prime-agent), [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi) and [PenguinHarness on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/penguin). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/penguin

# PenguinHarness on any model

PenguinHarness (Prism-Shadow/penguin-harness, the `penguin` command, npm `@prismshadow/penguin-cli`, and a desktop app) keeps each Project's models in one TOML file. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu and its models there, so PenguinHarness runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription. The CLI and the desktop app read the same file.

## Set up PenguinHarness

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for PenguinHarness on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu. A running PenguinHarness moves to it at once, with no restart.

```
jianmu penguin deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## .project_config.toml

The file is under the data root: `$PENGUIN_HOME`, else `~/.penguin/data` on every system. The CLI works in the Project `$PENGUIN_PROJECT_ID`, else `default_project`, so the file is `~/.penguin/data/default_project/.project_config.toml`. What jianmu writes:

```
default_model = { provider = "jianmu", model_id = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro" }

[providers.jianmu]
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
client_type = "openai-responses"
api_key = ""

[[models]]
provider = "jianmu"
model_id = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
display_name = "…"
context_window = …
vision = …
max_tokens = …

[models.pricing]
unit = "usd_per_mtok"
cache_read = …
cache_write = …
output = …
```

A model is the pair of provider and model_id, and one without an address or key of its own takes its provider's. jianmu uses the `openai-responses` client: requests go to base_url plus `/responses`, with the thinking level as reasoning.effort, which the openai-chat client leaves out. Your own providers and models stay as they are. With no file, jianmu makes one readable by you alone (it holds keys), as PenguinHarness makes it. PenguinHarness in a WSL distro is set up the same way, in `~/.penguin/data` there.

## The model list

Each of jianmu's models is one `[[models]]` entry, with what PenguinHarness's own Models page records for one: the display name, context window, cap on a reply, whether it reads images, and its price per million tokens. `vision` is always written, since PenguinHarness takes a model to read images unless told not. PenguinHarness refuses a default_model naming no entry, so jianmu writes the entries before the default, and on the way back changes the default before taking them out.

## No restart

PenguinHarness's server reads the file again whenever its modification time moves, so a change needs no restart. Its own Models page and `penguin config model …` write the whole file back, and every key jianmu writes is one it knows, so none is lost. A sync with nothing new leaves the file, and its time, alone.

## Switching back

When it first steps in, jianmu stashes the default_model you had. Switching back picks it again if PenguinHarness still has it, takes out a vision_model picked among jianmu's, then removes jianmu's models and `[providers.jianmu]`. A file jianmu made is removed once nothing is left in it.

```
jianmu penguin default
```

## FAQ

### Can PenguinHarness run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for PenguinHarness on jianmu's Agents page; the CLI and the desktop app both use it.

### Which file does jianmu change?

The current Project's .project_config.toml under the data root ($PENGUIN_HOME, else ~/.penguin/data). The default Project is default_project.

### Do I need to restart PenguinHarness?

No. It reads its settings again whenever the file's modification time moves.

### Does switching back restore my model?

Yes. jianmu stashed the default_model you had, picks it again if PenguinHarness still has it, and removes the provider and models it added.

More agents on the same models: [Paimon on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/paimon), [Muse Code on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/muse-code), [Prime Agent on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/prime-agent) and [MothX on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mothx). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mothx

# MothX on any model

MothX (OSCHINA's oschina/mothx, the `mothx` command, formerly vibecoding) is a coding agent in the terminal, written in Go. Its providers and the model it starts on are in one settings.json. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu and makes it the default, so MothX runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up MothX

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for MothX on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu, and a thinking level if you want one.
3. **Restart MothX.** MothX reads its settings when it starts, so an open session keeps its model until it starts again.

```
jianmu mothx deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## settings.json

The config folder is `$MOTHX_DIR`, else `%APPDATA%\mothx` on Windows and `~/.mothx` elsewhere. What jianmu writes:

```
{
  "defaultProvider": "jianmu",
  "defaultModel": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
  "defaultThinkingLevel": "high",
  "providers": {
    "jianmu": {
      "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
      "api": "openai-chat",
      "apiKey": "",
      "thinkingFormat": "openai",
      "models": [
        { "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "name": "…", "reasoning": true,
          "input": ["text"], "contextWindow": …, "maxTokens": …,
          "cost": { "input": …, "output": …, "cacheRead": …, "cacheWrite": … } }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

MothX asks the default provider for the default model on that provider's api: `openai-chat` is baseUrl plus `/chat/completions`, under Bearer apiKey. Each of jianmu's models is one entry, with whether it reads images, its context window, its cap on a reply and its price per million tokens; without them MothX takes its own default window and cap, and can't count a turn's cost. Headers or an httpProxy you put in jianmu's provider stay, and your own providers aren't touched. MothX in a WSL distro is set up the same way, in `~/.mothx` there.

## Thinking levels

`defaultThinkingLevel` is the level a session starts at: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max, narrowed to the ones a model takes when jianmu knows them. MothX sends a level only for a model whose entry says `reasoning` is true. jianmu writes `thinkingFormat: "openai"`, so MothX asks every model as reasoning_effort, which the gateway carries to each vendor's own form. Without it MothX guesses the vendor from the model id and the address: a model named qwen… got Qwen's enable_thinking, a deepseek… one only thinking:{type:enabled}, whatever served it. A thinkingFormat you already set is left alone.

## Restart MothX

MothX reads settings.json at start-up, so a running MothX needs a restart; jianmu tells you when a mothx or vibecoding process is running. MothX's own /model and /auth dialogs write the whole file back, and jianmu's settings survive that. Its requests say `Vibecoding Client/<version>` as their User-Agent, and Usage counts them as MothX.

## Switching back

Switching back takes out defaultProvider, defaultModel and `providers.jianmu`, and a providers object left empty. When the file then says the same as before jianmu's first write, the original file is put back byte for byte.

```
jianmu mothx default
```

## FAQ

### Can MothX run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for MothX on jianmu's Agents page, then restart MothX.

### Does this work for vibecoding too?

Yes. vibecoding is MothX's old name; jianmu takes it for MothX, with the same settings.json.

### How does the thinking level reach the model?

jianmu sets thinkingFormat to openai, so MothX sends reasoning_effort, which the gateway turns into each vendor's own form.

### Does switching back restore my settings?

Yes. jianmu takes out the default and the provider it added; when the file says the same as before, the original is put back as it was.

More agents on the same models: [PenguinHarness on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/penguin), [Paimon on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/paimon), [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi) and [Avibe on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/avibe). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/avibe

# Avibe on any model

Avibe (avibe-bot/avibe, MIT, the `avibe-os` package and its `vibe` CLI) is a local agent OS. Its own agent, Vibey, and the Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode it runs all take their models from its Model Hub, a gateway of Avibe's own (CLIProxyAPI) in front of the model sources added on its Models page. jianmu is added as one such source, so every agent in Avibe runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Avibe

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Start Avibe.** Avibe adds and removes model sources only while it runs, so start it with `vibe start` first.
3. **Pick jianmu for Avibe on the Agents page.** jianmu shows up as a model source on Avibe's Models page, for Vibey and the agents it runs.

```
vibe start
jianmu avibe jianmu
```

## jianmu as a model source

Avibe's home is `$AVIBE_HOME`, else `~/.avibe` (`~/.vibe_remote` before 3.0), and its sources are `model_hub.sources` in `config/config.json` there. A source can't be written into config.json by hand: each is checked whole, its key lives in the Model Hub's store, and Avibe adds it to its agents' route chains as it is added. So jianmu adds and removes it as Avibe's Models page does, through Avibe's internal API: the socket `state/dispatch.sock` in its home on macOS and Linux, or on Windows the loopback port and bearer token `runtime/control-ipc/endpoint.json` gives. What jianmu sends:

```
POST /internal/model-hub
{
  "operation": "create_source",
  "payload": {
    "source": {
      "kind": "api_key",
      "vendor": "custom",
      "display_name": "jianmu",
      "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
      "key": "",
      "protocol": "openai_chat",
      "supply_channel": "hub",
      "billing": "metered",
      "save_unverified": true
    }
  }
}
```

jianmu keeps the source's id, so one you rename in Avibe is still jianmu's. A custom source at the gateway that you added by hand on the Models page counts as jianmu's too. When the gateway moves to another port, a sync removes the old source and adds it again at the new address, since the key is sealed with the address; one pointed at another machine, a local proxy's path or the way a WSL distro reaches Windows stays where it is.

## Why chat completions

The source's protocol is `openai_chat`, not Responses. For a Responses source the Model Hub runs Codex's executor, which names itself codex-tui and would be taken for Codex itself; for chat it passes each backend's own headers on. A hub source serves every backend, the Model Hub translating Claude's and Codex's requests. It is saved without Avibe's protocol probe, which can't tell the gateway's protocols apart, as it serves them all.

## The model list

Avibe lists its models from the gateway's `/v1/models` itself, so what it offers is the models you picked for Avibe on jianmu's Agents page. Avibe lists them again on its own only once the listing is half an hour old, so jianmu has it refresh the source when you add or drop one.

## Removing it

Switching back has jianmu delete the source through the same internal API and forget its id. When removing it would take a hop out of a route or interrupt work in progress, Avibe asks for that to be confirmed, as its Models page does; you asked for it in jianmu, so jianmu asks again with what Avibe listed.

```
jianmu avibe default
```

## FAQ

### Do Claude Code and Codex inside Avibe get jianmu's models too?

Yes. jianmu is a Model Hub source, and a hub source serves Vibey and every backend Avibe runs: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

### Why does jianmu say to start Avibe first?

Avibe adds and removes model sources only through its internal API while it runs; config.json can't be edited for it. Run vibe start and try again.

### Which models does Avibe offer?

The ones you picked for Avibe on jianmu's Agents page. Avibe reads them from the gateway's /v1/models, and jianmu has it refresh when the list changes.

### How do I remove jianmu?

Switch Avibe back to its default in jianmu, or run jianmu avibe default. jianmu deletes the source it added.

More agents on the same models: [MothX on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mothx), [PenguinHarness on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/penguin), [Paimon on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/paimon) and [StepCode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepcode). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepcode

# StepCode on any model

StepCode is StepFun's coding agent in the terminal, the `step` command. Its default provider and model are in config.toml, and its providers in models.json, in Pi's provider format. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu to models.json and makes it the default in config.toml, so StepCode runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up StepCode

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for StepCode on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu. On the command line, `jianmu step` is the same agent.
3. **Start StepCode.** StepCode reads both files when it starts, so a new session is on the model you picked.

```
jianmu stepcode deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## config.toml and models.json

The files are in `~/.stepcode`, or the folder above an absolute `STEP_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. A folder renamed with `STEPCODE_CONFIG_DIR` is followed on this computer. In config.toml jianmu writes only these keys, and the rest of the file stays as it was:

```
# ~/.stepcode/config.toml
defaultProvider = "jianmu"
defaultModel = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
enabledModels = ["…", "jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"]
```

In models.json jianmu writes only `providers.jianmu`: the gateway's `/v1` as baseUrl, the `openai-completions` api, jianmu's own key for StepCode, and jianmu's models. models.json may have comments (JSONC). jianmu checks it first: the root, providers and providers.jianmu must be objects, or nothing is written, so a file it can't read safely isn't broken.

```
// ~/.stepcode/models.json
{
  "providers": {
    "jianmu": {
      "name": "jianmu",
      "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "apiKey": "",
      "models": [ { "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", … } ]
    }
  }
}
```

## The enabledModels scope

`enabledModels` is a scope of patterns matched against models. At start-up StepCode uses the default model when a pattern in the scope takes it, and otherwise the scope's first entry, with any `:level` suffix taken off. So the default alone isn't enough: when you have a scope, jianmu appends its pick to it and remembers that it did. Switching back takes out only those entries, never your own. A provider renamed takes its scope entries with it.

## Switching back

Before its first write jianmu saves the original provider, model and scope, the original `providers.jianmu` text, and whether config.toml, models.json and providers existed. Switching back puts all of these back, and removes files jianmu made.

```
jianmu stepcode default
```

## FAQ

### Can StepCode run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for StepCode on jianmu's Agents page, then start StepCode.

### Why did StepCode start on another model when defaultModel was set?

With enabledModels set, the default is used only when the scope takes it. jianmu appends its pick to the scope and removes only that entry when switching back.

### Does a models.json with comments work?

Yes. jianmu reads it as JSONC, and writes nothing when the root, providers or providers.jianmu isn't an object.

### Does switching back restore my settings?

Yes. The original provider, model, scope and providers.jianmu go back, and files jianmu made are removed.

More agents on the same models: [Avibe on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/avibe), [MothX on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mothx), [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi) and [omp on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/omp). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/omp

# omp on any model

omp (oh-my-pi, the `omp` command) is a fork of Pi, a coding agent in the terminal. It gives each kind of work a model role: default for the session, task for subagents, smol for small jobs, slow for review, plus plan, commit and more. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu to models.yml and points the roles you pick at it, so each of omp's roles runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up omp

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick models for omp on the Agents page.** Pick the default role's model first, then one for any other role and a thinking level if you want. On the command line, `jianmu oh-my-pi` is the same agent.
3. **Start a new session.** A new omp session starts on the default role's model.

```
jianmu omp deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## config.yml and models.yml

omp's settings are in `~/.omp/agent/config.yml`; `PI_CONFIG_DIR` renames `~/.omp`, and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` moves the agent folder. Each role's model is under `modelRoles` as provider/model, so one of jianmu's is `jianmu/<provider>/<model>`, with an optional `:level` on the end.

```
# ~/.omp/agent/config.yml
modelRoles:
  default: jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
  slow: jianmu/…:high
enabledModels:
  - …
  - jianmu/**
```

In models.yml beside it, jianmu's provider takes no key on this computer (`auth: none`), and its models carry their context window, cap on a reply, whether they read images, the thinking levels each takes and the price per million tokens. With the price, omp counts what each call cost; without it a jianmu model matches none of omp's bundled ones and every call costs 0. Your own providers and what else you keep in models.yml, such as modelOverrides, are left alone.

```
# ~/.omp/agent/models.yml
providers:
  jianmu:
    baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1
    auth: none
    models:
      - id: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
        …
```

## A model per role

default is the model a session starts on. task is for subagents; scout and sonic run on smol and reviewer on slow. Unset, task takes the parent session's model, and smol and slow the default's. plan is plan mode's, vision handles images, advisor gives a second opinion (slow first when unset), commit writes commit messages, tiny names sessions, and memory follows tiny. Every role but default can have a thinking level of its own, say medium for sessions and high for slow. The levels are minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and max; an omp before 16.4.0 doesn't take max, so it gets xhigh. Image models set in jianmu's Settings › Models › Images show up for omp's image role in its own Roles view, from omp 18.7.0.

## enabledModels

While `enabledModels` lists models, a new session is held to it: a default model outside the list never starts, and omp picks another from the list. So when you have one, jianmu adds `jianmu/**` to it, which also keeps all of jianmu's models in omp's picker and Ctrl+P. The list is yours: jianmu keeps its entries, order and comments, never makes one where there is none, and leaves entries scoped to folders as they are. The other roles aren't held to it.

## Each model on its own API

As with Pi, each model is asked on its provider's native API, and the gateway relays it as it is: OpenAI's Responses, Anthropic's Messages, Gemini's `/v1beta`. Over Chat, a Claude lost its thinking's signatures between tool turns, since Chat has no place for them. jianmu also has omp send its session id and its own name in headers, so Usage counts it as omp and Record gateway conversations keeps its turns.

## Profiles and WSL

Each profile in `~/.omp/profiles/<name>/agent` is an omp of its own, shown on the Agents page as `omp#<name>` with its own config.yml and models.yml; the one `OMP_PROFILE` picks is the default row. omp in a WSL distro uses `~/.omp/agent` there; when it reaches Windows' address from behind NAT, the provider carries the key the gateway is shared on the network with.

## Switching back

Before jianmu takes a role over it saves what the role had, and setting the role back puts that back as it was, a YAML list in the style it was written. jianmu's provider stays in models.yml while any role, fallback chain or task agent is on one of its models, and goes once none is, with the `enabledModels` entry jianmu added.

```
jianmu omp default
```

## FAQ

### Can omp run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for omp's default role on jianmu's Agents page, then start a new session.

### Can smol, slow and commit each have their own model?

Yes. Each role can take its own jianmu model, and every role but default its own thinking level.

### Why did omp start on another model when default was set?

While enabledModels lists models, the default model has to be in it. jianmu adds jianmu/** and removes it when switching back.

### Does switching back restore my settings?

Yes. Each role gets back what it had; once nothing is on jianmu, its provider and its enabledModels entry go too.

More agents on the same models: [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi), [StepCode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepcode), [MothX on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/mothx) and [Ante on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ante). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ante

# Ante on any model

Ante is antigma.ai's coding agent in the terminal, the `ante` command. It ships its own providers, and takes more of yours in catalog.json, merged on top. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu there and has Ante start on it in settings.json, so Ante runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Ante

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Ante on the Agents page.** Pick a model via jianmu.
3. **Restart Ante.** Ante reads catalog.json once per process, so a running one needs a restart.

```
jianmu ante deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## catalog.json

The file is `~/.ante/catalog.json`, or `$ANTE_HOME/catalog.json` when `ANTE_HOME` is set. A key under providers is what `--provider` takes. jianmu's entry points at the gateway's `/v1` on the OpenAiCompatible wire style, which is how Ante speaks Chat Completions, and the gateway takes every model on it. jianmu's models are listed in `preferred_models`, Ante's model picker.

```
// ~/.ante/catalog.json
{
  "providers": {
    "jianmu": {
      "display_name": "jianmu",
      "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
      "wire_style": "OpenAiCompatible",
      "preferred_models": [
        { "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "display_name": "…",
          "context_limit": …, "max_tokens": …, "supported_efforts": […] }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The entry has no auth: the gateway listens on this computer and lets its requests in without a key, and Ante counts a provider with no auth block as signed in. A bearer env_key would mean putting a key into Ante's environment, which is yours to decide. An auth block, http_headers or extra_body you add inside jianmu's entry stays, which is how a gateway shared on the network or reached from WSL gets its key. Your own providers and the models section are left alone. jianmu doesn't write support_vision either: Ante takes a model as seeing images unless told otherwise, and false would have Ante drop your images before the gateway, which can describe them to a model that can't see. A routing group gets no thinking levels, since which member answers each turn, and what it takes, is the group's to decide.

## settings.json

Being in the catalog isn't enough. The provider a session starts on is `provider` and `model` in `~/.ante/settings.json`; with neither set, Ante takes the first signed-in provider in catalog order, and the ones it ships come first. So jianmu sets those two as well, and saves what was there.

```
// ~/.ante/settings.json
{ "provider": "jianmu", "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro" }
```

## Restart Ante

Ante reads the catalog once per process, so an edit needs a restart. It parses the file leniently: an entry it can't read is skipped with a notice and the rest still load, so a bad entry would cost you jianmu's provider, not your own.

## Switching back

Switching back puts Ante's original provider and model back (or nothing, which leaves Ante to its own detection) and takes jianmu's entry out of the catalog, with a providers map left empty and files jianmu made. A provider you picked in Ante's own /providers while jianmu was set up is your choice and stands.

```
jianmu ante default
```

## FAQ

### Can Ante run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu model for Ante on jianmu's Agents page, then restart Ante.

### Why didn't Ante use jianmu's provider when it was in the catalog?

Ante starts on provider and model in settings.json, else the first signed-in provider it ships. jianmu sets those two as well.

### Why is there no API key in jianmu's entry?

The gateway takes no key on this computer, and Ante counts a provider with no auth as signed in. An auth block you add stays.

### Does switching back restore my settings?

Yes. Your original provider and model go back and jianmu's entry comes out; a choice you made in Ante since stands.

More agents on the same models: [omp on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/omp), [StepCode on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/stepcode), [Avibe on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/avibe) and [Aside on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aside). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aside

# Aside on any model

Aside (the `aside` command) keeps settings, a model list and sign-in for each account. jianmu adds a provider named jianmu to the account's models.json and has Aside itself make it the default, so Aside runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription, and draws with jianmu's image models too.

## Set up Aside

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Aside on the Agents page.** Pick a default model via jianmu, and a thinking level, categories and an image model if you want.
3. **Carry on in Aside.** jianmu has Aside change its own settings, then reads them back to check they took.

```
jianmu aside deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## models.json

Each Aside account has a folder, `~/.aside/u/<id>`, with settings.json, models.json and its sign-in. jianmu writes `providers.jianmu` in models.json in Pi's format: the gateway's `/v1` as baseUrl, jianmu's own key for Aside, and jianmu's models.

```
// ~/.aside/u//models.json
{
  "providers": {
    "jianmu": {
      "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
      "api": "…",
      "apiKey": "",
      "models": [ { "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", … } ]
    }
  }
}
```

jianmu changes only its own entry. When the jianmu entry there has no key or another key, jianmu won't write over it; one pointing at another gateway changes only when you reconnect on purpose.

## Aside's own settings

jianmu doesn't edit settings.json for the default model and the like. It has Aside set them, through `aside repl --account <id> --host local`, then reads them back. When the value read back differs, jianmu says so instead of calling it done. The default model is a provider and a modelId, and jianmu's are the ones whose provider is jianmu. The thinking level goes with the default model, offering only the levels that model takes.

## Categories and the image model

Aside's `modelCategories` are fast, standard, deep and visual, and each can take its own model; unset, they follow the default. `imageGenerationModel` is the model Aside draws with, and can be one of jianmu's image models. One unticked in its provider's editor isn't offered, but one already picked keeps drawing.

## More than one account

`currentAccountId` in `~/.aside/accounts.json` is the account Aside is on. jianmu sets up the account picked in jianmu, else the one Aside has active, else u0 when neither can be read. Each account's settings, and what jianmu remembers of them, stay with that account. Picking another account changes only which one jianmu sets up; nothing in Aside changes.

```
jianmu aside account u1
```

## Switching back

Before each setting it changes, jianmu saves what was there. Switching back restores only the settings jianmu changed; the rest are left as they are.

```
jianmu aside default
```

## FAQ

### Can Aside run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. Pick a via-jianmu default model for Aside on jianmu's Agents page; jianmu has Aside apply it.

### Can fast, standard, deep and visual each have their own model?

Yes. Each category can take its own jianmu model, and follows the default when unset.

### Which account does jianmu set up when Aside has several?

The one Aside is on, unless you pick one in jianmu, for example jianmu aside account u1.

### Does switching back restore my settings?

Yes. jianmu restores only the settings it changed, from the values it saved before.

More agents on the same models: [Ante on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ante), [omp on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/omp), [Pi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/pi) and [fx on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/fx). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/fx

# fx on any model

fx (fx.sh, from Vercel Labs, not the JSON viewer of the same name) keeps its settings in `~/.fx/settings.json`: `provider` is the provider it talks to (gateway, codex, grok or one of your own), `models` each provider's model, and `providers` the providers of your own. jianmu adds itself there as the provider jianmu, so fx runs on any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up fx

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for fx on the Agents page.** Pick one via jianmu. jianmu finds fx by its `~/.fx` folder, not the `fx` command, as the name is a common one.
3. **Restart fx.** fx reads its settings at start-up.

```
jianmu fx deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## settings.json

With one of jianmu's models picked, jianmu sets `provider` to jianmu and `models.jianmu` to the model, such as `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, and writes `providers.jianmu`: the openai-chat-completions protocol, the gateway's `/v1` as base_url, and auth none, so no key. In fx the model reads `jianmu/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`.

```
// ~/.fx/settings.json
{
  "provider": "jianmu",
  "models": { "jianmu": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro" },
  "providers": {
    "jianmu": {
      "protocol": "openai-chat-completions",
      "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1",
      "auth": { "type": "none" },
      "tool_choice_mode": "send",
      "model_metadata": {
        "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro": { "supports_tool_use": true, "supports_vision": …, "context_window": …, "max_output_tokens": … }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

fx sends no effort to a provider of your own, so there is no effort to pick. An fx in WSL is set up the same way, its base_url the gateway as that distro reaches it.

## The model list

fx's model picker lists `model_metadata`: jianmu's catalog, each model marked as taking tools, with whether it takes images, its context window and its output limit. fx refuses an output limit that isn't below the context window, so jianmu leaves such a limit out. fx takes at most 256 models and refuses the whole settings file past that, so jianmu writes at most 256, the model in use first so it is never the one cut. When the catalog changes, jianmu brings the list up to date while fx is connected.

## What you set yourself

A provider in fx can have a `reviewer_model`, the model its auto permission mode asks. jianmu doesn't write one, and one you set stays. jianmu writes `tool_choice_mode` send, and omit stays when you turn it to that. The protocol, address, auth and model_metadata are jianmu's; auth is written whole, as fx refuses an env beside type none.

## Restarting fx

fx reads its settings at start-up. When fx is running as the model changes, jianmu says to restart open fx sessions.

## Switching back

Picking one of fx's own models removes `providers.jianmu` and `models.jianmu`, and `provider` when it is jianmu, so fx is back on the provider it talks to without jianmu: Vercel's AI Gateway when none was set. The model goes into that provider's `models`; default removes it, leaving fx on its own default.

```
jianmu fx default
```

## FAQ

### Which fx is this?

Vercel Labs' coding agent fx (fx.sh), with its settings in ~/.fx. The JSON viewer named fx is another program.

### Does fx need an API key for jianmu?

No. jianmu's provider in fx has auth none and talks to the gateway on this computer.

### Why does fx list at most 256 of jianmu's models?

fx refuses the whole settings file when model_metadata holds more than 256, so jianmu writes at most 256, the model in use first.

### Which provider does fx use after switching back?

The one it talks to without jianmu; Vercel's AI Gateway when none was set.

More agents on the same models: [Aside on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aside), [Ante on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ante), [omp on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/omp) and [Grok App on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok-app). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/grok-app

# Grok App on any model

Grok App (RongleCat/grok-app) is a desktop front end for the grok CLI, which it starts over ACP. Its own model list is Grok Build's official catalog only; a model of your choosing is a provider channel in its settings. jianmu adds itself as a custom provider named jianmu, so Grok App's model picker offers any model in jianmu: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, Claude or a ChatGPT subscription.

## Set up Grok App

1. **Add a provider in jianmu.** Add an API key on the Providers page, or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Pick a model for Grok App on the Agents page.** Pick one via jianmu, and jianmu writes its custom provider.
3. **Press Use in Grok App.** Press Use on jianmu in Grok App's Settings › Account; that is what moves the App onto jianmu.

```
jianmu grok-app deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
```

## jianmu's custom provider

jianmu writes `[model.jianmu]` in `agent-home/config.toml` under the App's data folder, the way the App writes a channel itself: the gateway's `/v1` as base_url, jianmu's own key for Grok App, chat completions. `app_models` is a JSON list of jianmu's models, each with its context window, whether it takes images and its effort levels, so the custom providers in Settings list jianmu and the model picker can offer those models and their efforts.

```
# /agent-home/config.toml
[model.jianmu]
model = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
name = "jianmu"
api_key = ""
api_backend = "chat_completions"
app_provider_mode = "generic"
app_models = "[…]"
app_efforts = "[…]"
supports_reasoning_effort = …
context_window = …
```

The channel's context window, images and efforts follow the model picked. When the picked model is one jianmu no longer has, the channel moves to the first in the list.

## The route is yours to switch

`[models] default` is the route the App starts on. jianmu doesn't write it: making it jianmu takes the App over, and the App then drops its own sign-in and the session no longer runs. So the route stays what the App had, and pressing Use in the App's settings is what switches it, the App's own choice. An older jianmu set the route to jianmu; this one puts the old route back once, on the next sync or connect, and a Use you press after that stays. A model you pick in the App's picker since is yours too, and stays through a sync.

On jianmu, the App starts the CLI with GROK_HOME at agent-home, its independent mode; its default shared mode uses `~/.grok`, Grok Build's home.

## Models and efforts

Grok Build has no effort none for a channel, so the levels are the model's others. The one the picker starts on is the default you marked for that model on the App's Providers page, while the model still has it, else medium, or the middle level without it.

## The data folder

jianmu finds Grok App's data folder at `$GROK_APP_HOME` when it is set, else by system, the first that is there.

```
macOS    ~/Library/Application Support/com.grokapp.grok-app
Windows  %APPDATA%\grokapp\grok-app\data
Linux    $XDG_DATA_HOME/grok-app (~/.local/share/grok-app)
         or ~/.grok-app; $GROK_APP_HOME when set
```

## Disconnecting

Disconnecting takes `[model.jianmu]` out. The route is touched only when it still names jianmu, a route that doesn't run: jianmu puts back the one it remembered, or clears it. Any other route is the App's and stays. Picking one of the App's own routes in jianmu, such as the official Grok, also takes jianmu's channel out and makes that the route.

## FAQ

### Can Grok App run on DeepSeek, GLM or a ChatGPT subscription?

Yes. jianmu adds itself as a custom provider in Grok App, so its model picker offers jianmu's models; press Use on jianmu in its settings to switch.

### Why is Grok App not on jianmu after connecting?

jianmu leaves the App's route alone, as taking it over makes the App drop its own sign-in. Press Use on jianmu in Grok App's Settings › Account.

### Can I pick an effort in Grok App?

Yes. Each jianmu model comes with its own effort levels, starting on the one you marked, else medium.

### Does disconnecting put Grok App's old route back?

Yes, when the route still names jianmu; any other route is left alone.

More agents on the same models: [fx on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/fx), [Aside on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aside) and [Ante on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/ante). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/cherry-studio

# Every model in Cherry Studio, through jianmu

Cherry Studio is a desktop chat client that takes any OpenAI-compatible provider. jianmu adds itself there as one provider, named jianmu, so every model you have in jianmu shows up in Cherry Studio: providers with an API key and the Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot subscriptions you signed in to.

jianmu runs a gateway on your computer at `http://127.0.0.1:3425`. It speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions API and translates each request for the provider behind the model, Anthropic’s, Google’s or a subscription’s, with streaming, tool calls and reasoning. Cherry Studio sees one OpenAI-compatible provider at `http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1`.

Cherry Studio keeps its providers in its own database, and jianmu never writes to it. It adds itself through Cherry Studio’s add-provider link instead, and you confirm it in Cherry Studio. This works in Cherry Studio 1.x and 2.x.

## Add jianmu to Cherry Studio

1. **Add providers in jianmu.** In the Providers tab, add an API key (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, OpenRouter…) or sign in to a subscription.
2. **Open the Agents tab.** jianmu lists Cherry Studio once it has run on this computer, including a data folder you moved elsewhere.
3. **Click Add jianmu.** On Cherry Studio’s row, press Add jianmu. Cherry Studio opens its model provider settings with jianmu filled in: name jianmu, type OpenAI, the gateway’s address and a key.
4. **Confirm it in Cherry Studio.** Nothing is added until you do.

If nothing opens, no app on this computer handles Cherry Studio’s links yet: open Cherry Studio once, or install it again, then click Add jianmu again.

## Pick the models

Cherry Studio lists a provider’s models from `/v1/models`, so the jianmu provider offers every model jianmu has, named `provider/model` (for example `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`). Add the ones you want to the jianmu provider in Cherry Studio, and choose them in a chat like any other model.

A provider you add in jianmu later shows up the next time Cherry Studio fetches the list; there is nothing to change in Cherry Studio. Several accounts behind one model, rest periods after a 429 and failover work as they do for every agent.

## From a terminal

```
jianmu cherrystudio add      # opens Cherry Studio to add jianmu, confirm it there
```

`cherry-studio` works as the name too.

## How jianmu knows it was added

Once Cherry Studio has a provider at the gateway’s address, the row shows jianmu instead of the button. jianmu reads Cherry Studio 2.x’s database for this, read-only. Cherry Studio 1.x keeps providers where jianmu doesn’t read them, so there the button stays.

## Usage and keys

On a gateway that isn’t shared, the key in the link is Cherry Studio’s own, so its requests are counted as Cherry Studio’s in jianmu’s Usage, apart from your coding agents. When the gateway is shared on your network with gateway keys, the link carries a key that works there.

## FAQ

### Do I need an API key to use Claude or ChatGPT in Cherry Studio?

No. Sign in to a Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot subscription in jianmu, and its models appear in the jianmu provider in Cherry Studio.

### Does jianmu change Cherry Studio’s settings?

No. jianmu opens Cherry Studio’s own add-provider dialog, and you confirm it. It only reads Cherry Studio’s database to show whether jianmu was added.

### What address and type does the jianmu provider use?

Type OpenAI, at http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1, or the gateway address you set in jianmu.

### Why don’t I see a new model in Cherry Studio?

Cherry Studio shows models you added to the provider. Fetch the jianmu provider’s model list again and add the new one.

### Cherry Studio isn’t in jianmu’s Agents tab.

jianmu lists it once Cherry Studio has run on this computer. Open Cherry Studio once, then look again.

Another desktop app on the same models: [AionUi on any model](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/aionui). Using a coding agent too? See [Subscriptions in any agent](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/subscriptions) and [Get started](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/start). Something fails? See [Fixing common errors](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting), or ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/troubleshooting

# Fixing common errors: 401, 429, 502, 504 and more

An error from jianmu’s gateway says what went wrong in its own words. This page lists the common ones, what causes them, and the fix.

Every request is listed on jianmu’s Routing page, with which provider and account it went to and how each try ended. Copy Report on a request copies what you need to ask for help.

## 401 and 403: a key or sign-in refused

**From the vendor.** The provider turned down the key or sign-in jianmu sent. jianmu sets that key or account aside and tries the next one, so you see the error only when none is left. A sign-in that has run out says so, for example “the ChatGPT sign-in has expired — sign in again”.

- **Fix:.** sign in again from ＋ Add provider (or `jianmu accounts add <provider>`), or give the provider a new key.

**From jianmu itself.** jianmu answers 403 on its own in a few cases, before anything is sent:

| Error | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| model disabled | You turned the model off in jianmu. | Turn it on again on its provider. |
| model not allowed for the gateway key | The gateway key is held to some models. | `jianmu gateway-key models <id>` lists or changes them. |
| jianmu doesn’t answer the web page … | A web page called the gateway from a browser. | List it in Settings › Network and sharing › Web pages, and send a gateway key. |

## 429 and rest periods

A 429 means the provider is out of quota, out of credit or rate limiting you. jianmu rests the key or account that was refused and sends the request to the next account, the next member of a routing group, or the provider’s Fallback. The provider’s row shows Resting · {why} · back at {time}.

| Refused for | Rests |
| --- | --- |
| Quota, with a reset time | Until the reset |
| Rate limit, with Retry-After | Until then |
| Credit | 30 minutes, then 2 hours, 8 hours, a day, 3 days and a week if it is refused again |
| A ChatGPT account out of credits | Until the reset its refusal names, else until its full window renews, else 5 hours |
| Any other failure | A minute, doubling on repeats up to 10 minutes (30 for a rate limit) |

- **Ask it again now..** Try now ends the rest: the next request asks it again. Refused again, it rests again.
- **Cap the rest..** `jianmu provider rest-cap <id> 4h` sets the longest rest for a provider; `off` stops it resting for failures that say nothing of why.
- **A relay whose limits pass in a moment..** Untick Set it aside when out of quota or rate limited in the provider editor’s Advanced: a 429 then rests nothing, and the next request goes to it as usual.
- **Never all at once..** Add a second account or a fallback model, so a spent one never stops the agent. `jianmu accounts` shows how much of each account’s allowance is used.

Rests are kept across restarts, so quitting jianmu doesn’t bring a resting account back early.

## 502: the provider didn’t answer

A 502 means jianmu couldn’t get an API reply from the provider. What follows the provider’s name says which case it is:

- **“didn’t answer: …”.** The connection failed: a name that doesn’t resolve, a refused connection, a proxy that is down. When this computer has no network at all, jianmu notices and rests nobody.
- **“… not an API reply”.** The provider answered, but with a web page (a sign-in page, a Cloudflare challenge), nothing at all, or something that isn’t JSON. The base URL usually points at a web site instead of the API: check it against the vendor’s docs, and whether it should end in `/v1`.
- **OpenCode: “… which is no error, not an API reply”..** OpenCode’s gateway sometimes answers a 400 holding only the model’s name. The same request is answered some seconds later, so jianmu reads it as a 502, asks again within the request’s patience or tries a group’s next member, and rests nobody. It is tied to requests carrying very large tool lists.

A 502, 503, 504, 529 or Cloudflare’s 520 to 524 counts as busy: jianmu asks again or moves to a routing group’s next member before the agent sees it.

## 504: no answer in time

- **“<provider>: no first token in Ns”..** A routing group gives each member a time to start answering (First token). The member was slower, so the next was asked. Raise it on the group for a slow model.
- **“no member of the group answered within its Ns budget”..** Every member of the group was tried within the group’s time and none answered.
- **“jianmu held this request for … without routing it to any provider”..** The request waited inside jianmu and was stopped rather than left waiting. Send it again; if it comes back, Copy Report on that request on the Routing page and share it.

## Model not found (404)

The error reads *jianmu knows no model “…”*, often with *did you mean …?* and the list of your provider ids.

- **Name it as jianmu does..** Use `provider/model`, as `jianmu models` lists it, a routing group’s id or name, or a bare model id.
- **“… is switched off in Jianmu, so … is not served”..** The provider or routing group is off. Switch it on again on the Providers or Routing page.
- **No providers yet..** The error says “add a provider in jianmu first”.

## The agent doesn’t show the model

- **Restart the agent..** Most agents read their config only when they start. jianmu says so on the agent’s row after a change, for example “Codex builds its model list at start-up”. Codex’s app also keeps an app-server running; restart it as the notice says.
- **Check jianmu serves it..** `jianmu models` lists every model you can pick. A model you turned off, or one whose provider is switched off, isn’t listed.
- **Claude Code..** `/model` lists jianmu’s models marked “via jianmu”. If `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` is set in your shell, Claude Code goes to that cloud instead of jianmu; remove it from your shell profile.

## Port 3425 is in use

The gateway listens on `127.0.0.1:3425`. To move it, open Settings › Network and sharing › Gateway address. Only the port is set there, 1024 to 65535, and the agents jianmu connected move with it.

| jianmu says | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Port … is in use by another program: pick another one | Pick a free port. |
| Another jianmu serves the gateway at …: set its port there, or quit it first | Two copies of jianmu are running. Quit one. |
| Port … is taken by another program, jianmu web perhaps: jianmu tries again every few seconds | Find what holds the port, or move the gateway to another. |
| JIANMU_ADDR=… sets the gateway’s whole address, host:port: unset it to set the port here | Unset `JIANMU_ADDR`, or change it. |

## Agents in WSL

On Windows, jianmu looks in running WSL distros for agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kimi Code and Qwen Code. Each one it finds gets a row of its own on the Agents page, and jianmu sets it up as it does on Windows. It never starts a stopped distro.

- **The agent isn’t listed..** Start the distro, and check Settings › General › Detect agents in WSL is on.
- **It can’t reach jianmu..** Under WSL’s default NAT networking, jianmu also serves the gateway at Windows’ address on the WSL network, with a key of its own, and writes that address into the agent’s config. With mirrored networking the agent uses `127.0.0.1` as on Windows. Windows’ firewall still decides: WSL’s network counts as Public, so allow jianmu there if the connection is blocked.
- **A change doesn’t show..** An agent in WSL reads its config at start-up: restart it there.

## From another computer on the network

By default the gateway answers only this computer. To use it from another: Settings › Network and sharing › Share on local network. The other computer sends a gateway key from the Gateway page’s Gateway keys.

- **“jianmu isn’t shared on the local network”..** Turn sharing on, on the computer that runs jianmu.
- **401..** The key is missing, off or expired. Send an enabled gateway key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key`.
- **403 for a model..** The key is held to some models: `jianmu gateway-key models <id>`.

Don’t open the port to the internet; use a VPN between your computers. The full setup, another jianmu included, is in [Remote jianmu](https://usejianmu.ai/docs/remote).

## A subscription moved to a plugin isn’t served

Command Code, Cursor, Devin, Factory, Grok, Kiro, Xiaomi MiMo, Qoder, WorkBuddy, ZCode and Zed are no longer built into jianmu. Each is served by a community plugin that does the same job. Accounts added before still need to move to the plugin, and nothing serves them until they do.

- **Fix:.** a line over the Providers list says “… built-in subscription is retired, and its accounts haven’t moved to its plugin yet”. Press Move to the plugin: jianmu installs the plugin and checks each account. Moving keeps your accounts, models and agents as they are. jianmu also moves them by itself, and installing the plugin from the Plugins page does too.

An error after the move comes from the plugin, which does the sign-in, models and requests.

## FAQ

### Why does jianmu answer 502 when the provider is up?

The provider answered with something that isn’t an API reply, such as a web page or an empty body. The base URL usually points at the vendor’s web site instead of its API.

### Why does an account stay unused after a 429?

jianmu rests it until the reset the vendor named, or for a while if none was named. The provider’s row says when it is back, and Try now ends the rest.

### What does “jianmu knows no model” mean?

No provider serves a model by that name. Name it as provider/model, as jianmu models lists it, or switch its provider on again.

### How do I change jianmu’s port?

Settings › Network and sharing › Gateway address. The agents jianmu connected move with it.

### Can an agent in WSL use jianmu on Windows?

Yes. jianmu finds agents in running WSL distros and sets each up with an address it can reach. Under NAT networking, Windows’ firewall must let WSL’s connection through.

### Can I use jianmu from another computer?

Yes. Turn on Settings › Network and sharing › Share on local network, and send a gateway key from the other computer. Don’t open the port to the internet.

Still stuck? Copy the request’s report from the Routing page and ask on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/DamonZS/Jianmu/issues).

---

Source: https://usejianmu.ai/docs/library

# Library

jianmu’s Library keeps instructions, MCP servers, skills, hooks and subagents in one place, and writes each of them into every agent you tick for it, in that agent’s own files and format. The agents read those files as they always do. jianmu adds no layer between an agent and what it is given: the agent itself decides when to use a skill, an MCP tool or a subagent.

The page has seven tabs: Instructions, MCP servers, Skills, Hooks, Subagents, RTK and billion-context. Each item has a row of agents; tick an agent to give it the item, untick it to take it away. An agent reads the change when it starts again.

## Where it is kept

- **The library.** is `library.json` in jianmu’s config folder (`~/.config/jianmu`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jianmu` when that is set). Instruction texts and skill folders are in `library/` next to it.
- **Every change.** saves the library and writes it into every agent at once. jianmu records what it wrote, so it only ever takes away its own entries and leaves yours alone.
- **Backups..** Before a change, the files it replaces are copied to `backups/` in the same folder. The last 30 are kept. The Backups button at the top of each tab opens them.
- **Write it again..** After you install an agent, or edit its files by hand, `jianmu library sync` writes the library into every agent again.

```
jianmu library          # what the library gives each agent
jianmu library sync     # write it into the agents again
```

## Instructions

Instructions are text every session of an agent starts with, such as house rules or a coding style. jianmu writes its part between two marker lines in the agent’s instructions file:

```
<!-- jianmu:begin · written by jianmu from its Library -->
…the Library's instructions…
<!-- jianmu:end -->
```

Everything outside the markers is yours and is never changed. You can keep several named sets and give each set to different agents, and a set can live in a file of your own.

| Agent | File |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (or `AGENTS.override.md` when you use one) |
| Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` |
| Antigravity | `~/.gemini/config/GEMINI.md` |
| OpenCode | `AGENTS.md` in its config folder |
| Copilot CLI | `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` |
| Goose, Crush, Qwen Code, CodeBuddy | `.goosehints`, `CRUSH.md`, `QWEN.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md` |
| Droid, Grok, dsh, omp | `AGENTS.md` in the agent’s own folder |
| Pi, OmO | the first one there of `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` |

Folders follow the agent’s own setting: a custom `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` is used in place of the default.

## MCP servers

An MCP server is either a command (a program the agent starts, such as `npx …`) or a URL (HTTP or SSE). jianmu writes one entry per server into each ticked agent’s MCP config, in that agent’s format, and keeps any fields you added to the entry yourself.

| Agent | File |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude.json` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/settings.json` |
| Antigravity | `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` |
| OpenCode | `opencode.json` |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| Copilot CLI | `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` |
| Zed | `context_servers` in its `settings.json` |

- **Variables..** `${NAME}` in a header or an env value is written in each agent’s own syntax. An agent that has no such syntax is not given that server, and the page says why.
- **SSE..** Codex, Goose, dsh, Grok, Command Code and Zed can’t use an SSE server. Claude Desktop takes no remote servers at all.
- **Single tools off..** You can turn off tools one by one for Codex, Gemini CLI, Crush, Hermes Agent, Claude Code and OpenCode, each in its own setting. Every other agent gets the whole server.
